en.name: The martyrdom of St. Laurence
description: Cobalt-blue on white painted and glazed tiles, *azulejos*. The Italianate Baroque style of the painting is due to the interpretation of Italian prints by the artist.
partner: Institute for the Administration of Architectural and Archaeological Heritage -  IGESPAR

pt.name: Martírio de S. Lourenço
description: Azulejos em azul-cobalto sobre branco. O estilo barroco italianizante da pintura deve-se à interpretação pelo artista de gravuras italianas.

en.name: Bob Walter [veiled dancer]
short_description: The "serpentine dance", invented by Mary Louise Fuller, was copied by many dancers, and even parodied. Like Fuller, these dancers also used veils and lighting effects, characteristics typical of the Art Nouveau movement.
keywords: Dance; Orientalism

fr.name: Bob Walter [danseuse aux voiles]
short_description: La "danse serpentine" inventée par Mary Louise Fuller a été plagiée par nombre de danseurs et de danseuses, et même parodiée. Comme Mme Fuller, ces danseurs utilisent des effets de voiles et de lumières dans le style Art nouveau.
keywords: Danse; orientalisme

ar.name: زبدية
description: هذه الزبدية لها زر ترصيع عالي وجوانب ذات حواف محدبة. والأوعية من هذا الشكل تشبه أوعية الخمر القديمة والتي كانت تستخدم في العالم الإسلامي في الحمّام أو كأوعية سحرية. وإن خواص الشفاء السحرية لهذه الزبدية الخاصة  تتجلى بالرموز المجهولة المعنى على الإطار. والزخرفة بالآيات القرآنية على الإفريز تحت الإطار وجوانب زر الترصيع بينما على سطحها المسطح منقوش اسم الله ضمن نجمة سداسية.

el.name: Κούπα
description: Η κούπα έχει κεντρικό ομφαλό και τοιχώματα με αυλακώσεις. Το σχήμα αυτού του σκεύους πάει πίσω στις αρχαίες φιάλες σπονδής και χρησιμοποιείται στον ισλαμικό κόσμο ως κούπα για το χαμάμ ή μαγικό μπολ. Οι μαγικές θεραπευτικές ιδιότητες του συγκεκριμένου μπολ φανερώνονται από τα κρυπτογραφημένα σύμβολα στο χείλος. Κορανικοί στίχοι κοσμούν τη ζώνη κάτω από το χείλος και γύρω από τον ομφαλό, η πλατειά έδρα του οποίου φέρει εξακόρυφο άστρο και το όνομα του Αλλάχ.

en.name: Bowl
description: This bowl has a central high boss and gadrooned sides. Vessels of this shape, harking back to antique libation bowls, were used in the Islamic world in the hammam or as magic bowls. The magic healing properties of this particular bowl are betrayed by the undeciphered symbols on the rim. Qur’anic verses ornament the frieze under the rim and the sides of the boss, while on its flattened top is inscribed, within a six-pointed star, the name of Allah.
keywords: Ottoman bath culture; Quranic inscriptions; Magical bowl

en.name: Cooking pot
description:
This kitchen utensil was discovered at the al Wakra site during excavations carried out in 2011.  
It is a cooking pot that was made in Julfar (in the Emirate of Ras al-Khaymah) and used for storing and preparing foodstuffs and liquids. With a globular body and a flat base, this pot bears a grey slip, and some of the specific decoration painted in red from the Julfar production workshop can be discerned on the upper part of the body, neck and shoulder. This bears witness to the import of pottery and to Qatar's commercial links and activities.
place: Julfar, Ras al-Khaymah Emirate, United Arab Emirates
keywords: earthenware, transportation, storage, kitchenware

ar.name: سقف.
description:
تلبيسة سقف من الطراز المُدَجَّن، مصنوعة من خشب البلوط المعالج بطريقة آلفارج *alfarje* . زُخرف السقف زخرفة غزيرة، ويحتوي على تشبيكات حادة ومتراكبة تشكل نجوماً من 8 إلى 16 طرف. يعطي تعقيد الشكل المركزي، الذي يعاد تصويره بوضوح في الزلّيج، ديناميكية كبيرة للتكوين؛ وتزداد حيوية الشكل بالتعددية اللونية وببقايا التذهيب التي ما زالت بادية للعيان.  
  
تاريخ صنع هذا السقف معروف (1477)، ونعلم أنه شكل جزءاً من عملية الأشغال التي بادر إليها أسقف – كونت كويمبرا، د. جواو غالفاو (1460 – 1481) في كاتدرائيته.

كسرة سقف محصل عليها من أعلى موضع الخورس بالكاتدرائية القديمة لكويمبرا عام 882 هجري / 1477 ميلادي. زخرفت القطعة زخرفة وافرة؛ وتقدم تشبيكات منكسرة ومتراكبة تشكل نجوما مكونة من ثمان أو ستة عشر رأسا. تمت الزيادة في الحيوية المفرطة للشكل بإدخال تعدد الألوان إذ لازالت بعض بقايا التذهيب بادية لحد الآن.
place: موضع الخورس العلوي في الكاتدرائية القديمة (سي فيلها) في كويمبرا.
keywords: آلفارج؛ تشبيكات هندسية؛ سقف؛ سي فيلها (الكاتدرائية القديمة)؛ مدجّنون؛ نجمة.
materials: خشب البلوط، مصنوع بطريقة آلفارج  alfarje.
tags: خشب البلوط، مصنوع بطريقة آلفارج alfarje.

en.name: Ceiling.
description:
Remnant of a Mudéjar ceiling, with *alfarje* work (an Iberian decorative style), made from chestnut wood. It is profusely decorated, with pointed and intersecting lacework, forming eight-pointed and sixteen-pointed stars. The complexity of the central motif, widely known on *azulejos* (glazed tiles), gives this composition a very dynamic appearance. The exuberance of this motif was enhanced by its polychromy, and some vestiges of its gilding are still visible.  
The date of its production is known (1477) and it is also known that it was part of the campaign of work undertaken by the Count Bishop of Coimbra, João Galvão (1460–81), in his cathedral.

Ceiling fragment from the upper choir of the Old Cathedral in Coimbra from AH 882 / AD 1477. It is profusely decorated with broken and interlacing knots, forming eight- and sixteen-pointed stars. Its varied colouring, some traces of which have survived, enhance the exuberance of the piece.
place: Chancel of the Sé Velha cathedral of Coimbra.
keywords: ceiling; Coimbra; Mudéjar; alfarje; geometric patterns; star

es.name: Techumbre.
description:
Fragmento de techumbre mudéjar en madera de castaño tallada. Está profusamente decorado con lazo quebrado y entrecruzado que forma estrellas de ocho y dieciséis puntas. La complejidad del motivo central, ampliamente divulgado en azulejos, confiere un gran dinamismo a la composición. La exuberancia de este motivo se veía reforzada por la policromía, de la que aún son visibles restos de dorado.  
Se conoce la fecha de su ejecución, 1477, y se sabe que formó parte de la campaña de obras emprendidas por el obispo-conde de Coimbra, João Galvão (1460-1481), en su catedral.

Fragmento de techumbre del coro alto de la Catedral Vieja (Sé Velha) de Coimbra, datado en 1477. Está profusamente decorado con un lazo quebrado y entrelazado que forma estrellas de ocho y de dieciséis puntas. La exuberancia de este motivo se veía reforzada por la policromía, de la que aún son visibles restos de dorado.
place: Coro alto de la Catedral Vieja (Sé Velha) de Coimbra.
keywords: diseño géométrico; estrella; techumbre

fr.name: Plafond.
description:
Lambris de plafond mudéjar en bois de châtaignier traité en *alfarje*. Abondamment décoré, il présente des entrelacs brisés et superposés, formant des étoiles de huit à seize pointes. La complexité du motif central, amplement reproduit dans les *azulejos*, apporte une grande dynamique à la composition. L'exubérance du motif est accentuée par la polychromie, quelques vestiges de dorure étant encore visibles.  
La date de sa réalisation est connue (1477), et on sait qu'elle a fait partie de la campagne de travaux entreprise par l'évêque-comte de Coimbra, D. João Galvão (1460-1481), dans sa cathédrale.

Fragment de plafond provenant du haut-chœur de l'ancienne cathédrale de Coimbra 882 H / 1477 J.-C.. Abondamment décoré, il présente des entrelacs brisés et superposés, formant des étoiles de huit à seize pointes. L'exubérance du motif est accentuée par la polychromie, quelques vestiges de dorure étant encore visibles.
holder: Musée national de Machado de Castro.
place: Haut-chœur de l’ancienne cathédrale (Sé Velha) de Coimbra.
keywords: plafond ; mudéjar ; alfarje ; motif géométrique ; étoile
materials: Bois de châtaigner ; travail en alfarje.

pt.name: Tecto.
description:
Esteira de tecto mudéjar, com trabalho de alfarge, executado em madeira de castanho. É profusamente decorado, apresentando laçarias quebradas e entrelaçadas, formando estrelas de oito e dezasseis pontas. A complexidade do motivo central, amplamente divulgado nos azulejos, confere grande dinâmica a esta composição. A exuberância deste motivo era consolidada pela sua policromia, sendo ainda actualmente visíveis alguns vestígios de douradura.  
  
Conhece-se a data da sua execução – 1477 –, sabendo-se igualmente que integrou a campanha de obras empreendidas pelo Bispo-Conde de Coimbra, D. João Galvão (1460-1481), na sua Catedral.

Fragmento do tecto do coro-alto da Sé Velha de Coimbra, datado de 882 AH / 1477 AD. É profusamente decorado, apresentando laçarias quebradas e entrelaçadas, formando estrelas de oito e dezasseis pontas. A exuberância deste motivo era consolidada pela sua policromia, da qual restam alguns vestígios.
holder: Museu Nacional de Machado de Castro.
place: Coro-alto da Sé Velha de Coimbra.
keywords: tecto; Coimbra; mudéjar; alfarge; padrão geométrico; estrela
materials: Madeira de castanho com trabalho de alfarge.
tags: Madeira de castanho com trabalho de alfarge.

ar.name: صحن
description: في تركيا الفخار المطلي تحت الزجاج ينتج من أجل الطبقة الحاكمة العثمانية وهو معروف بطرازه الفريد من الرسوم والألوان وكان دائما محط الإعجاب في أوربا. والعناصر الأكثر جمالا منه هي الصحون ، الزبديات وأوعية الشرب وهذه القطع  من إزنيق كانت ذات تأثير كبير آخر على إنتاج الخزف الأوربي .وهذا اللون للصحن من إزنيق ذو الرسوم المزهرة المركبة مطلي بالكوبالت الأزرق تحت الزجاج وباللون الأخضر الناعم والمنغنيز ومؤطر بالأسود ويعود للعام 1540 ميلادي تقريبا.

en.name: Dish
description: In Turkey, underglaze-painted pottery, produced for the Ottoman court and wealthy patrons, is renowned for its unique style of motifs and colours, once again widely admired in Europe. Mostly fashioned into dishes, bowls and drinking vessels, these Iznik wares were another major influence on Western ceramic production. This Iznik dish with composite floral motifs is painted in underglaze cobalt blue, sage green, manganese and outlined in black is dated AD c. 1540.

en.name: El Sayyid Muhammad Idris al-Mahdi al Senussi (1889–1983), from 1916 Chief of the Senussi Muslim order
short_description: El Sayyid (or Sidi) Muhammad Idris al-Mahdi al Senussi (1889-1983), the grandson of the founder of the Senussi Sufi order, became head of the Senussi order in 1916. He took the title of Emir and ruled as King of Libya from 1951 through 1969. In 1920 Italy reached an agreement with him and invited him to Rome, where he met King Victor Emmanuel III. Idris’ relations with the Italian government later deteriorated, and he went into exile in Egypt and encouraged anti-Italian guerrilla from there.
holder: Italian Institute for African and Oriental Studies

en.name: *The arrival of the refugees*
short_description:
A black and white photo from an album depicting the arrival of Greek refugees after the Asia Minor catastrophe. Photographer unknown.  
The “Convention concerning the exchange of Greek and Turkish population" was signed at Lausanne, on 30 January 1923, by the two governments. It involved approximately 2 million people (around 1.5 million Anatolian and 500,000 Muslims in Greece), most of whom were forcibly made refugees.
keywords: photo; refugees

en.name: Naval Cemetery
description:
Right next to the Portuguese bastion, which stretches an arm out to the sea and is known as *Curaa*, lies a small cemetery placed near the marabout of Sidi Ahmed Ibn Musa and his sister Lalla Mennana.  
This cemetery and its marabout were laid out on a platform that was constructed outside the Portuguese ramparts. The imported ceramics which cover the tombs brighten up this austere place.

es.name: Cementerio marino
description: Muy cerca del bastión portugués, rodeado de un brazo de mar denominado *Curaça*, se encuentra un pequeño cementerio situado junto al morabito de Sidi Ahmed Ibn Musa y de su hermana Lalla Mennana. Tanto el cementerio como el morabito están construidos sobre una plataforma artificial, fuera de las murallas portuguesas. Las cerámicas de importación que recubren las tumbas alegran este austero lugar.

fr.name: Cimetière marin
description: Tout près du bastion portugais, qui étend un bras vers la mer et qui est dénommé *Curaça*, se trouve un petit cimetière implanté auprès du marabout de Sidi Ahmed Ibn Moussa et de sa soeur Lalla Mennana. Ce cimetière et son marabout ont été aménagés sur une plate-forme construite en dehors des remparts portugais. Les céramiques d’importation qui recouvrent les tombes égaient ce lieu austère.

en.name: Carpet
description:
Initially, the production of Arraiolos carpets was characterised by a rigid and faithful adoption of Eastern carpet patterns, with their palmettes, lotus flowers, “vine scrolls”, arabesque motifs and other elements. This faithfulness to characteristic design elements allows recognition of the main sources of inspiration in this production, such as carpets from the Iberian Peninsula, Persia and Turkey, the “Holbein” and “Lotto” versions among them.  
This carpet is of great interest, since it is a rare extant example of an Arraiolos carpet based on the standard “Lotto” pattern, the influence of which in carpets currently extant in Portugal is residual. “Lotto”-design carpets were popular in Europe during the 16th century, as evidenced by interiors represented in many contemporary paintings of the period, such as in *Presentation of the Head of Saint John the Baptist*, attributed to Gregório Lopes (c. 1539‒1541).  
The carpet’s field features the characteristic geometric design of palmettes and stylised arabesques. In a contrasting colour, rosettes with angular forms fill the border. Originally, the background colour of the field was red; and traces of the pigment can still be seen in between the wool embroidery.
keywords: carpet; Arraiolos; 17th century; Portugal; embroidery; Slavic cross-stitch; *ponto de Arraiolos*; Arraiolos stitch
materials: Linen and wool; embroidered; oblique or Slavic cross-stitch (known as *ponto de Arraiolos*)
tags: oblique or Slavic cross-stitch (known as ponto de Arraiolos)
partner: National Museum of Ancient Art ‒ MNAA

cs.name: Zámek Židlochovice
description: K hlavní budově dvoupatrového dvoukřídlého zámku se připojují přízemní trakty, vytvářející směrem k městu čestný dvůr. Levý z nich prodloužen o bývalou jízdárnu a správní budovu, nachází se zde také kaple, která měla být otevřena i veřejnosti. Průčelí jsou členěna mělkými rizality s kuželkovou balustrádou a tympanonem a dekorována květinovými festony. Vstupní hala s reprezentativním schodištěm, jakož i interiéry jsou řešeny v pozdně klasicistním a neobarokním stylu. Doplňují je lovecké trofeje a galerie s díly holandských malířů. S historickými bažantnicemi a oborami pro vysokou zvěř vytváří zámek ojedinělý lovecký komplex, představující místní mysliveckou tradici.

Zámek stavěný na místě staršího sídla dvorským kancléřem, který se několikrát účastnil mírových jednání s francouzským králem a byl generálním superintendantem vídeňské umělecké akademie, je příkladem reflexe nového, klasizujícího vkusu. Patří mezi první příklady francouzského zámeckého půdorysu s čestným dvorem ve tvaru „U“. Jde o typ. tzv. korespondenční architektury – stavbu projektoval podle zaslaného plánu pařížského královského dvorního architekta místní stavební mistr. Zahrada byla považována za jednu z nejkrásnějších v zemi. R. 1784 zde startoval první balón na Moravě.
artist: Bedřich ze Žerotína, Filip Ludvík Sinzendorf (1671–1742), Karel Maxmilián z Dietrichštejna (1748–1784), Albrecht, vévoda sasko-těšínský, Arcivévoda Fridrich (zámek vlastnil v letech 1895–1918)

Robert de Cotte (1656 Paris – 1735 Paris), Ernst August Charbonnier (1677–1747 Hannover?), Ludwig Sebastian Kaltner, František Antonín Grimm (1712 Brno – 1784 Brno), Bartoloměj Zintner (1717–1773), Johann Stern, Joachim Günter, Wenzel Frieb
history: Původní vodní tvrz na jantarové stezce, spojující Středomoří s baltským pobřežím, doložená v 1. polovině 14. století, byla přestavěna Bedřichem ze Žerotína na renesanční zámek. Za Třicetileté války poničená stavba byla obnovena dostavbou jihozápadního křídla pány z Valdštejna. Následující majitel, hrabě Sinzendorf, byl nejvyšším dvorským kancléřem. Několikrát se účastnil mírových jednání s francouzským králem, stal se generálním superintendantem vídeňské umělecké akademie. Pracoval pro něj také Pieter van Roy. Z finančních důvodů byl zámek prodán r. 1743 Dietrichštejnům, kteří panství drželi do r. 1819, kdy je koupil vévoda sasko-těšínský Albrecht, zeť Marie Terezie.

en.name: Židlochovice Chateau
description: The main building of the two-floor, two-wing chateau is adjoined by ground-floor sections making up a ceremonial courtyard that opens in the direction of Židlochovice town. In the left section there is the former riding hall and administration building, and also a chapel which is open to the public. The frontage is segmented by shallow bays with a skittle balustrade and a tympanum, decorated with flower festoons. The entrance hall with a spectacular staircase, and the interiors, are in the late-Classical and Neo-Baroque styles. They contain hunting trophies and a gallery with paintings by Dutch masters. Together with a pheasantry and game park, the chateau constitutes a unique hunting complex, bearing witness to the strong local hunting tradition.

The chateau was built by an imperial chancellor on the site of an older residence. The chancellor – who took part in several peace negotiations with the French King and was a general superintendent of the Vienna Academy – built a chateau that exemplified the new Classicism. It was one of the first chateaux to feature a ground plan with a U-shaped ceremonial courtyard. It can be considered as “correspondence architecture”, for the building was designed by a local master builder following a plan sent to him by an architect from the Parisian royal court. The garden was considered one of the most beautiful in the country.
artist: Friedrich of Žerotín, Filip Ludvík Sinzendorf (1671–1742), Karel Maxmilián of Dietrichstein (1748–1784), Albrecht, Duke of Saxony and Těšín, Archduke Friedrich (owner, 1895–1918)

Robert de Cotte (1656–1735, Paris), Ernst August Charbonnier (1677–1747 Hannover?), Ludwig Sebastian Kaltner, František Antonín Grimm (1712–1784, Brno), Bartoloměj Zintner (1717–1773), Johann Stern, Joachim Günter, Wenzel Frieb, Jan Jiří Schauberger (?before 1725 Vienna, active in Olomouc – 1744 Brno)
history: Originally a water fortress on the Amber Trail that connected the Mediterranean region with the Baltic coast, documented in the first half of the 14th century, the building was converted to a Renaissance chateau by Friedrich of Žerotín. Damaged during the Thirty Years’ War it was restored, with the addition of a south-west wing, by the Lords of Valdštejn. The next owner, Count Sinzendorf, was the supreme court chancellor. He took part in several peace negotiations with the French King and was a general superintendent of the Vienna Academy. In 1743 the chateau was sold to the Dietrichsteins who held the demesne until 1819. It was then purchased by Albrecht Duke of Saxony and Těšín, son-in-law of Empress Maria Theresa.

en.name: Altar of St. Cross
description: The story of Redemption through the sacrifice of Christ is represented by burning souls behind the bars of the altar cavity; *Supper at Emaus,* modelled in low relief on the doors of the *tabernaculum*; the huge sculptures of St. Veronica and St. Barbara on either side; St. Mary, Mary Magdalen and St. Joseph standing in front of the painted *Crucifixion* and, finally, God surrounded by angels in the attic.
place: The Chapel of the Holy Cross

en.name: Villa of the Emperor Vitellius (Via D. Marinelli)
description:
During the imperial period, *Aricia* underwent major urban developments, as testified by several sites and remains of patrician villas scattered throughout the district of the ancient city. Of particular interests are the ruins traditionally thought to be Emperor Vitellius’ villa, built not far from the Via Sacra. The ruins and the large perimeter indicate it was an imposing construction of which we can still identify a nymphaeum in *opus caementicium* and *opus reticulatum*, as well as two cisterns that ensured the huge water supply for the villa’s *thermae* (bath complexes).  
  
In 1740, following the excavations on the site, Augusto Chigi reused the floors of the villa to create the brecciated marble tables that can now be admired in the Chigi Palace in *Aricia* as part as the historical furnishing.

it.name: Villa dell'Imperatore Vitellio (V. D. Marinelli)
description:
Il grande sviluppo urbanistico conosciuto dal territorio di Ariccia in periodo imperiale, è testimoniato da siti e resti di ville patrizie sparsi in tutto il circondario dell’antica Aricia. Eloquenti a tale proposito, i ruderi tradizionalmente noti come la Villa dell’Imperatore Vitellio, imponente costruzione, stando alla perimetrazione presumibile, che sorse verosimilmente non distante dal tracciato della Via Sacra e della quale ci sono pervenute (In località Muracce, nei pressi del campo sportivo) alcune vestigia, fra le quali un ninfeo, con murature in opera cementizia e opera reticolata, oltre a due cisterne per assicurare l’ingente approvvigionamento idrico della villa che disponeva anche di impianti termali.  
Nel 1740 Augusto Chigi in seguito a scavi fatti effettuare nel sito, riutilizzò i pavimenti della villa per realizzare i tavoli in marmo brecciato che si possono ammirare fra gli arredi del Palazzo Chigi di Ariccia.

en.name: Table
short_description: This table bore witness to the signing of the so-called "Treaty of Bardo" the 12 May 1881 by Mohamed Sadok Bey and the General Bréart. This circular marble table has a diameter of around 120 cm and an ebony base, carved and embellished with gold leaf.
holder: Musée d’Histoire Moderne et Contemporaine de Kassar Saïd
keywords: Mohamed Sadok Bey; General Bréart; French protectorate in Tunisia
partner: Higher Institute for the Study of Contemporary History of Tunisia, University of Manouba

fr.name: Table
short_description: Objet témoin de la signature du traité dit du Bardo le 12 mai 1881 par Mohammed Sadok Bey et le général Bréart. Table en marbre circulaire d’environ 120 centimètres de diamètre avec un socle en bois d’ébène sculpté et décoré à la feuille d’or.
holder: Musée d’Histoire moderne et contemporaine de Kassar Saïd
keywords: Mohammed Sadok Bey; Général Breart; Protectorat francais en tunisie
partner: Institut Supérieur d’histoire contemporaine de la Tunisie, Université de la Manouba

ar.name: طبق
description: خلال الثلث الأخير من القرن السادس عشر فقد ظهر نوع من التزيين المزهر في خزف إزنيق المعروف بـ ""الباقات ذات الأزهار المنحنية "" . و كانت أزهار التوليب الزرقاء والقرنفل الأحمر والزهور المتفتحة الزرقاء ترش بشكل عش طائر بترتيب متناظر حول الطبق. والنوعية التخطيطية في تشكيل رشة الأزهار المتفتحة يتجلى بشكل مثير للإعجاب مقابل الخلفية البيضاء. والأشكال الموجية ذات الطراز الخاص في نموذج الحدود تقريبا يفقدها لمستها ذات المصدر الصيني.
materials: خزف من عجينة الكوارتز ، تزيين : طلاء تحت التزجيج بما يعرف بتقنية الطماطم الحمراء

de.name: Teller
description: Im letzten Drittel des 16. Jahrhunderts entsteht im floralen Dekor der Iznik-Keramiken der Typus des „Bouquets mit geknickter Blume“. Unsymmetrisch angeordnet, schmiegen sich blaue Tulpen, rote Nelken und ein blauer Blütenzweig an den Rand des Tellers. Die grafische Qualität in der Darstellung der Blütenstängel kommt vor dem weißen Hintergrund besonders gut zur Geltung. Stilisierte Wellenmotive im Randmuster lassen ihr chinesisches Vorbild kaum noch erkennen.

en.name: Plate
description: During the last third of the 16th century, a type of floral decoration emerged in Iznik ceramics known as “bouquets with bent flowers”. Blue tulips, red carnations and a blue blossom spray nestle in asymmetrical arrangement around the plate. The graphic quality in the rendering of the blossom spray is admirably enhanced against the white background. Stylized wave motifs in the border pattern have almost lost touch with their Chinese source.
keywords: Ceramic; floral decoration; Iznik style

en.name: Hammam (Arab Baths)
description:
Probably coming from the re-use of an analogous Roman existence, the *hammam* is built on a small hillock sloping gently down towards the valley of the River Cefal, almost hidden by modest buildings which surround it on three sides, and therefore thought by G. Lo Jacono to have been an original concept of an inn and hospital combined. Within the complex, the positioning of the buildings, apart from the widespread typology of the farms in the Sicilian countryside, recalls the theme of the enclosure, nuclear generator of so much Islamic architecture.  
The true *hammam* is built as only one rectangular-shaped room, articulated in two distinct rooms: one, more extended in length, is divided transversally into three basins decreasing from four saddle-shaped masonry separators; the other, adjacent, placed in the vicinity of the spring, is formed of one sole basin. The two areas are divided by a large *transenna* with three ogival arches on columns, almost a lay *tribelon*. The columns are a variant of the Corinthian order, having an attic plinth and chalice-shaped capitals of terracotta with a double row of leaves twisting round a decoration ornamented with gadroons and pods. The thrust of the arcades is augmented by the insertion of a brickwork skewback. The arches are also of brick and support a wall of the same type, positioned so as to close the overreaching vault that crumbled and was reconstructed in the 15th century together with the arches. Three small rectangular windows, much lengthened, open in the walls above the arches; an ogival vault of large proportions and having air vents covers the whole system. The edifice has a closed and blocked volumetry; the external walls possess a facade consisting of a central band in calcarous ashlars bearing a much worn inscription in *kufic* characters and by two narrower bands surrounding it. These have been worked in oversized bricks, visible, however, in different parts of the structure (possibly bricks of Roman origin used once again in pre-Norman construction). The system of underground channelling for the filling and emptying of the basins is still largely identifiable in the areas nearest to them.  
Opinion as to the date of construction is still controversial, especially since the geographer al-Idrisi in his *Libro di Ruggero*, completed shortly before the death of the Norman sovereign in 1154, and despite signaling the presence of 11 thermal baths in large and small centres of Sicily, failed to mention the one at Cefal Diana. One scholar has proposed recently a chronological distinction between the various parts of the construction, attributing the northern, western and eastern outside walls to the Hellenistic-Roman Period (between 50 BC and 59 AD). The two columns sustaining the arches of the *tribelon* are attributed to the Arabic era and the stringcourse faade with the inscription in kufic characters to the Norman period following the death of the first Guglielmo, in 1166 (Ryolo, 1971). A final dating attributed it entirely to the later period of the Norman reign (Krnig in Di Stefano, 1979) claiming many analogies with the language applied to architecture of the period of Guglielmo II.

es.name: Hammam
description:
Aprovechando probablemente un establecimiento romano análogo, el baño está construido sobre un pequeño alcor que baja en ligera pendiente hacia el valle del río Cefalà, casi escondido por modestas construcciones que lo rodean por tres lados, razón por la cual G. Lo Jacono pensó en una función originaria de hostal-hospital. En el complejo, la disposición de los edificios, además de retomar la difundida tipología de las masadas presentes en la campiña siciliana, recuerda también a un recinto, núcleo generador de tanta arquitectura islámica.  
El baño propiamente dicho está formado por una única sala de forma rectangular, articulada en dos ambientes distintos: uno, más largo, partido transversalmente en tres piletas decrecientes por cuatro tabiques en forma de asiento; el otro, contiguo, situado cerca de la fuente y formado por una única pileta. Los dos ambientes están separados por una amplia divisoria de tres arcos ojivales sobre columnas, casi un laico *tribelon*. Las columnas, una variante del orden corintio, tienen base ática y capiteles de terracota en forma de cáliz, con doble orden de hojas que envuelven una decoración de óvolos y volutas. El arranque de las arcadas está aumentado por la inserción de un salmer de ladrillo. También los arcos son de ladrillo y sostienen una mampostería del mismo tipo que cierra la bóveda, desmoronada y rehecha en el siglo XV junto con las arcadas. Tres ventanitas rectangulares, muy alargadas, se abren en la mampostería encima de los arcos; una bóveda de cañón, de grandes dimensiones y dotada de respiraderos, cubre todo el sistema. El edificio tiene un esquema volumétrico cerrado y bloqueado; las paredes externas presentan, como único elemento decorativo, una franja constituida por una hilada central de sillares calcáreos y con una inscripción en caracteres *cúficos* muy deteriorada, y por dos franjas más estrechas que la encuadran. Estas están realizadas con ladrillos de gran formato, por lo demás visibles en diversos puntos de la fábrica (quizá ladrillos de la época romana reutilizados en la construcción prenormanda). El sistema de canalizaciones subterráneas que garantizaba el llenado y el vaciado de las piletas es todavía parcialmente reconocible en las cercanías.  
Sobre la fecha de construcción, las opiniones son aún controvertidas, tanto más cuanto en el *Libro de Ruggero* el geógrafo al-Idrisi, que concluyó su obra poco antes de la muerte del soberano normando (1154), pese a las señales de la presencia de once baños termales en grandes y pequeños centros de Sicilia, no hace mención alguna del de Cefalà Diana. Un estudioso ha propuesto recientemente una distinción cronológica entre las varias partes de la construcción, atribuyendo los muros norte, oeste y este a la época helenístico-romana (entre el año 50 a. C. y el 50 d. C.); las dos columnas que sostienen los arcos del *tribelon*, a la época árabe; la franja de imposta con la inscripción en caracteres *cúficos*, al periodo normando siguiente a la muerte del primer Guglielmo en 1166 (Ryolo, 1971). Una última datación lo atribuye entero al periodo más tardío del reino normando (W. Krönig, en Di Stefano, 1979), reivindicando muchas analogías con el lenguaje propio de la arquitectura del periodo de Guglielmo II.

ar.name: هذه الصفحات من الشهنامة  للفردوسي معمولة لشاه طهماسب الأولمنسوبة لسلطان محمد  ، مير سعيد علي مير مصور ، أقا ميراك وميرزا علي
description: هذه الصفحات العشر أتت من الشهنامة والتي صنعت للحاكم الصفوي شاه طهماسب الأول (حكم بين 1524 – 1576). وإنها واحدة من أروع المخطوطات الفارسية المصورة التي أنتجت قط المسماة الشهنامة وفقا للجامع الذي جزأها في نيويورك في 1970s . وهي ذات شكل كبير على ورق رائع مرشوش بالذهب وذات 258 شكل مصور. والشكل معروض بشكل مستقل لكل لوحة ويجب أن يكون قد تم هناك تشاور مستمر بين الكتاب والرسامين وواضعي الهوامش حولها. والصفحة 516 التي هي في مجموعة الخليلي هي الصفحة الوحيدة من المخطوطة التي تحتوي تاريخا.وقد أعطيت المخطوطة من قبل شاه طهماسب إلى السلطان العثماني سليم الثاني عند اعتلاء الأخير العرش في عام 1566. وفي عام 1903 كانت المخطوطة في حيازة إدموند روتشيلد وقد تغير المالك مرة أخرى في 1960s عندما بدأ مالكها آرثر هجتون جونيور في تفريقها.واليوم هناك نحو 140 من لوحاتها في متاحف ومجموعات في كل العالم . وبقية المخطوطة – التجليد و بلوك النص و118 لوحة قد صارت في متحف الفن المعاصر في طهران منذ عام 1994.صفحات الخليلي :صفحة 25b ، موت الملك مرداس ، منسوبة للسلطان محمودصفحة 27b ،  الضحاك يستلم ابنتي جمشيد ، منسوبة للسلطان محمودصفحة 30b ،  الضحاك يقتل البقرة المقدسة برمايه ، منسوبة للسلطان محمود ومير سيد علي صفحة 38b : ترسل فريدون أم فاراناك هدايا لابنها ربما بتوجيه من السلطان محمودصفحة 89b : زوجة محراب ، سندوخت تخرج مع عبيد يحملون الهدايا للترحيب بسام  ربما بتوجيه من المير مصورصفحة 119b : رستم يقتل تنينا ، منسوبة لعبد الوهاب صفحة 135b : رستم والمحاربين السبعة في أرض الصيد في أفراسياب. منسوبة لمير سيد علي صفحة 279b : قتال رستم وشنغول ، منسوبة لأقا ميراك صفحة 516b : عبدة أردافان جلنار مع أردشير الشاب ، منسوبة لمير مصور صفحة 731a : الموسيقي بارباد يخفي نفسه في شجرة ، منسوبة لميرزا علي

en.name: Ten folios from the *Shahnamah* of Firdawsi made for Shah Tahmasp I
description:
The ten folios come the *Shahnamah* made for the Safavid ruler, Shah Tahmasp I (r. 1524–1576). One of the finest illustrated Persian manuscript ever made, it has been referred to as the ‘Houghton’ *Shahnamah* after the collector who broke it up in New York in the 1970s. It is of large format, on fine gold-sprinkled paper, and with 258 illustrations. The format is independently conceived for each painting and must have involved constant consultation between scribes, painters and marginators. Folio 516, which in the Khalili Collection, is the only folio in the manuscript to bear a date.  
The manuscript was given by Shah Tahmasp to the Ottoman Sultan Selim II at the time of the latter’s accession in 1566. By 1903, the manuscript was in the possession of Edmond de Rothschild. It changed hands once again in the 1960s, when its then owner, Arthur Houghton Jr, began to disperse it. Today, some 140 of its paintings are in museums and collections throughout the world. The rest of the manuscript – the binding, the text block and 118 paintings – have been in the Contemporary Art Museum in Tehran since 1994.

en.name: Detail of the Fortress
place: Built of clay, brick, wood and some stone, the fortress complex was designed to accommodate 4,000 soldiers and 150 cannons.

en.name: Roqueta Castle
description:
The remains of the Castle built on the rocks by D. Manuel I to defend the bar of the River Lima from marauding pirates is part of the modern-day bastioned Fortress of Santiago da Barra. A curious structure, similar to the Torre de Belém in Lisbon, with a Mediaeval tower and bulwark to the south, it demonstrates the evolution of fortifications in Portugal at this period of transition from more rudimentary weapons to the use of pyro-ballistics, of which there are few examples still remaining.  
Although it is difficult to date the castle, there is little doubt that it was built at around the same time as the Torre de Belém around 1510-1520, although, originally, it was thought that it was built somewhat later.

en.name: Bowlegarnitur
description: An essential association for the foundation and development of Czech modern art was the one of Artěl – an initiative that was founded by two men: Alois Dyk, an art enthusiast, and banker. and Vilem Štech, an art theoretician and art historian also responsible for endorsing young Czech modernism. Several artists joined in the beginning, such as Pavel Janak, Jan Konupek and Helena Johnova. The name of the association was taken from Tolstoy’s novel *Anna Karenina* and meant a merely verbally agreed-upon community of people who work together and jointly vouch for each other, as well as have an equal share of the income. Since they lacked the finances, the Artěl could not afford their own workshop, and therefore performed manufacturing in different factories, such as the Rydl and Thon Company in Svijany-Podoli in Northern Bohemia for ceramics and porcelain, and the Pryl glass factory in Růženin in Central Bohemia for glass. Among the various artists that participated in Artěl, Josef Rosipal, even though he was an architect, was of particular importance for the implementation of the association’s ideas in the medium of glass. Rosipal’s most famous pieces are his cut services, created in simple shapes, commonly overlayed in red or blue with cut geometric decorative motifs Additionally, since the sentiment of the Artěl association was oriented more towards expressionism, and, even more, cubism, these tendencies can be seen most clearly in the decorative motifs of the glass. This long glass piece, part of a set consisting of a punch bowl, lid, spoon, and five other glasses, closely follows the cubistic tendencies in glass decoration of the Czech modernist applied arts, which Josef Rosipal applied gracefully.
artist: Rosipal, Josef (design); Glashütte Arnost Pryl, Ruzenin u. Chocerad (manufacturer); Artěl, Kunstgewerbliches Unternehmen (client / customer)
partner: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art

en.name: Bullfight Arena of Campo Pequeno
names: Campo de Touros do Campo Pequeno
short_description: The Bullfight arena, built with monochromatic brick, is an iconic example of the 19th century neo-Arab style in Lisbon, was the neo-Mudejar one in Madrid. With an external perimeter of 80 m, its circular plan includes 4 polygonal towers attached symmetrically and topped by bulbous domes originally polychromatic. The 40.7 m diameter arena was covered with sand, encircled by a wooden fence and separated from the circular rows of seats by a corridor. It seats 8,438 spectators three levels namely in five rows mounted on an iron structure and two rows of 165 lodges and galleries. The access is provided by two 3 m wide covered walks. One of its main features is the use of the brick particularly enhanced on the segments of the several arches rhythmically opened at the external walls.
history:
In 1821 King João VI hands over the organization of non free bullfights to Real Casa Pia de Lisboa, an educational institution founded by his mother in 1780 to support youngsters in risk. To overcome the exiguity of its first arena, in 1889 Casa Pia orders a new one to architect António Dias da Silva who sent the plans from Madrid according to the meanwhile disappeared Neo-Mudejar Bullfight Arena of Madrid by Emilio Rodriguez Ayuso. Built between 1890-1892 it will be inaugurated still unfinished by Royal Prince Afonso of Braganza (1865–1920) on the 18th August 1892.  
From those days onwards keeps being one of the main bullfight arenas in Portugal nowadays renovated and transformed into a multifunctional venue.
keywords: Architecture; Arab Style; Leisure; Bullfight arena; Lisbon

en.name: Chapel of Santa Clara
names: Ermida de Santa Clara (Chapel of St Clara)
description:
This was a small Parish Church until, in 1540, it was rebuilt by Francisco da Gama, the son of the famous admiral. It has essentially retained its Manueline structure, probably dating from about 1520, but the main vessel of the church was altered later. The Manueline-style chancel is particularly fine, with a Late Gothic entrance arch with naturalist capitals, and ribbed vaulting with foliate decorative bosses.  
The exterior is also Manueline, with buttresses, decorative battlements and conical *pinnacles*. The simple portal with a pointed arch is also Manueline.

de.name: Landtagssaal
description: Der über anderthalb Stockwerke reichende Mittelsaal des zweiten Stockwerkes ist als Sitzungssaal des Landtages als der repräsentative Höhepunkt der Innenräume des Landhauses konzipiert. Nach dem Vorbild italienischer Galerien wurde der Festsaal statt im ersten im zweiten Stockwerk eingerichtet, was auch in süddeutschen Profanbauten des Frühbarock anzutreffen ist, wie dem Augsburger Rathaus. Die erstrangige Ausstattung folgt der Idee der politischen Selbstdarstellung des Landes und seiner Regierung. Statuen von Fürsten und Regenten, Nikolaus Moll zugeschrieben, zeigen Herrscher und Regenten Tirols, die Fresken von Cosmas Damian Asam bringen das Land und seine Geschichte mit biblischen Szenen in Verbindung und stellen es unter den Schutz der göttlichen Vorsehung. Die Putten von Ingenuin Lechleitner weisen die Symbole der Stände vor.
place: Mitte des zweiten Stockwerks im Haupttrakt
artist:
Georg Anton Gumpp  
Nikolaus Moll  
Ingenium Lechleitner  
Cosmas Damian Asam

en.name: Parliament hall
description: The central hall, the parliament’s assembly hall, extends over one and a half floors and is the representative highpoint of the interior. Following the model of Italian galleries, it is situated on the second as opposed to the first floor (cf. Augsburg Town Hall). The excellent interior design work pursues the idea of the state’s political self-representation. Statues of princes and regents, attributed to Nikolaus Moll, depict Tyrol’s rulers and regents, the frescos from Asam present the state and its history in connection with biblical scenes, placing it under the protection of divine providence, the putti from Lechleitner display the symbols of the estates.
place: Centre of the second floor in the main wing, (Old) Federal State Parliament
artist: Georg Anton Gumpp (1682–1754); sculptural work: Ingenuin Lechleitner (1676–1731); Nikolaus Moll (1676–1754); Cosmas Damian Asam (1686–1739)

en.name: *Ivan III Adam Ratkay*
description:
The Ratkays were a noble family originating from Hungary whose family name is spelled in several different ways: Rathkay, Rattkay, Ratkay. In 1502, the Ratkays gained possession of the castle and estate of Veliki Tabor in north-west Croatia. From thereon they called themselves “Ratkay de Nagy Tabor”. Marriage connects the Ratkays to the Croatian nobility.  
Ivan III (Veliki Tabor, Croatia, 1640–Mexico, 1683) was a page at the court of Emperor Leopold I. He studied philosophy and theology in Graz before becoming a Jesuit, and was ordained in 1676. In 1678, he departed via Genoa, Seville and Cadiz for Mexico, landing in Vera Cruz two years later. From 1681, he lived among the Tarahumara Indians as a missionary, dying there from the effects of a native poison in 1683. He wrote journals of his travels in Latin, documenting his journey to Mexico and New Mexico, which he enriched with a map of Tarahumara with missionary settlements and Spanish fortresses (thereby making him one of the first Croatian cartographers). The family died out at the end of the 18th century.  
The painting consists of a portrait, four scenes from his life as a Jesuit, and a family coat of arms, all in separate painted frames. This painting is unique in the Museum collection in that it depicts the short life of the missionary in a series of smaller scenes arranged around the central oval with the portrait of Ivan III. It was painted by an unknown artist in the first decades of the 18th century.

From a noble family, Ivan III had been a page at the court of Emperor Leopold I. He studied philosophy and read law before becoming a Jesuit. In 1678, he departed for America landing in Vera Cruz two years later. Working as a missionary among the American Indians, he died there from the effects of a native poison in 1683. He wrote journals of his travels in Latin and drew a map of the territory where he worked, making him one of the first Croatian cartographers.
keywords: Portrait; Ratkay family; religious mission; Jesuit; education; Mexico; travel journal; travelling; native

en.name: *St. George*
description: The saint, shown as he transfixes the dragon writhing under his feet, along with the figure of St. Martin on the same altar, has similarities with the statues of Filip Jakob Straub on the High Altar of Welsche Kirche in Graz, which probably served Weinacht as an inspiration.
place: Far-left intercolumniation of the High Altar, Parish Church of Our Lady of the Snow

en.name: Double niche ‘Transylvanian’ carpet
description: The term “Transylvanian” rug refers to 17th- and 18th-century rugs preserved in large numbers in Transylvanian Saxon churches, and once considered to have been made in Transylvania, whereas in fact they were produced in western Anatolia. Certain Transylvanian rugs have a *mihrab* design, typical of prayer rugs; others, such as the present one, feature two opposing arches. The shape of this double niche and its undecorated beige ground are characteristic of later “Transylvanian” rugs, while the border of alternating polygonal cartouches and octagons can also be found in earlier examples. Several technical imperfections such as the inaccurate rendering of space, which accounts for the incomplete motifs in the main border, and the lack of left–right symmetry though indicative of a modest workshop, retain a certain appealing charm.
holder: The National Museum of Art of Romania
keywords: Transylvanian rug
partner: The National Museum of Art of Romania

en.name: Sepulchres
description:
Among Ariccia's archaeological heritage there are also several burials and funerary monuments. These include: a square-plan sepulchre in peperino blocks at the so-called Tomb of the Horatii and Curiatii, and the funerary monument with a rectangular plan and in *opus latericium*, both on via Appia Antica; a rupestrian tomb on via della Costa and one on via del Pometo; a sepulcher *in opus latericium* at Palombara Tower, and two on Via Appia Antica near the Chigi Tower; one circular burial in *opus caementicium* on via della Polveriera; one at the end of the Substructure of via Appia Antica.  
(Bibliography: E. Lucidi, 1796; G. R. Florescu, 1925; R. Lefevre, 1977; M. Lilli, 2002; G. Gazzetti, 2002; M. Leoni, 2008)

it.name: Sepolcri (V. Appia Antica)
description:
Fra i beni archeologici di Ariccia si annoverano anche varie sepolture e monumenti sepolcrali fra i quali ricordiamo un Monumento funerario a pianta quadrata in blocchi di peperino, via Appia Antica, presso c.d. Tomba degli Orazi e Curiazi e il Monumento funerario a pianta rettangolare, opera laterizia e listata sempre in via Appia Antica; Sepolcro rupestre in via della Costa; Sepolcro rupestre in via del Pometo; Torre Palombara, sepolcro in opera laterizia; Torrione Chigi, sepolcro in opera laterizia; Due Sepolcri in opera laterizia, via Appia Antica presso Torrione Chigi; via della Polveriera, sepolcro circolare in opera cementizia; Sepolcro, alla fine della Sostruzione, via Appia Antica.  
(Bibliografia: E. Lucidi, 1796; G. R. Florescu, 1925; R. Lefevre, 1977; M. Lilli, 2002; G. Gazzetti, 2002; M. Leoni, 2008)

en.name: Beylical salon
short_description: This beylical salon is furnished with carved wood from the beylik era, and consists of three large double-seater benches and four smaller benches with full armrests and topped with a pediment. The set is decorated with rectangular panels in the middle and square panels on the sides, all decorated with a mashrabiya. A wood carved table completes the set.
keywords: Palace; Husainid dynasty; carved wood; mashrabiya
partner: Higher Institute for the Study of Contemporary History of Tunisia, University of Manouba

fr.name: Salon beylical
short_description: Il s’agit d’un salon en bois sculpté de l’époque beylicale. Il est composé de trois grandes banquettes à deux places et de quatre bancs surmontés de fronton et terminés aux extrémités par des accoudoirs ; l’ensemble est décoré par des panneaux rectangulaires au centre et carrés sur les côtés ornés de moucharabieh. Une table rectangulaire en bois sculpté complète l’ensemble.
keywords: Palais; Dynastie Husseinite; Bois sculpté; Moucharabieh
partner: Institut Supérieur d’histoire contemporaine de la Tunisie, Université de la Manouba

en.name: Traditional Lebanese house
description: Traditional Lebanese houses in the 19th century were generally rather modest. The roofs were supported by wooden beams, and were accessible by an internal stairway made of stone, compared to the wooden stairways of more modest abodes.
history: The houses were built with wooden windows which were filled with tinted glass. A balcony could usually be found on the first floor, which was covered with a clear window for lighting and ventilation purposes. This architectural style was clearly influenced by European architecture and design, indicating the growing influence of European culture and trends in 19th century Beirut and elsewhere in the region.
keywords: Archetypes; Typology; Architecture; Tradition

en.name: *Monastery on Mount Carmel*
short_description: Another important landmark described in the book *Palestine Past and Present* by Laura Jewry Valentine is Mount Carmel and its monastery. Again, the history of this site is described in terms of its Biblical and Christian past, as the location of the fight between Elijah and the priests of Baal, and the place where the monastery of the Virgin of Mount Carmel was founded in the 12th century. The description highlights other details about specific places on the mount related to episodes from Elijah’s story, the story of the monastery and the description of the monastery of Mar Eliyas built in 1826. Each naturalistic, archaeological and historical detail (such as the discovery of a small synagogue and a Jewish tomb) is presented in such a way that recalls a continuous connection with the Jewish and Christian past.
keywords: Pilgrimage; pilgrims; Christian pilgrimage; Jewish pilgrimage; Palestine; Holy Land; Jerusalem; sacred places; travel; travel book; Ottoman Palestine; local Jewish community; Biblical places; Biblical archaology

en.name: Fiat 130 HP
description: The  Fiat 130 HP, derived from the 100/110 HP type, whose design was entrusted to engineer Gio- vanni Enrico. This giant car featured over 16 litres of displacement. Furthermore, it was characterised by overhead valve timing in a 90° V shape, with a power of 130 HP and a weight of 1,025 kg, capable of reaching a speed of 160 km/h, with peaks of up to 200 km/h. Three exam- ples were made for the French Grand Prix driven by Vincenzo Lancia (under the name F1), Felice Nazzaro (F2) and Louis Wagner (F3). The two-block, four-cylinder engine displaces 16,286 cubic centimetres.
keywords: Historic Car; Engine; Grand Prix; Felice Nazzaro; Racing cars
materials: Wood, steel, copper, leather, paint; assembling, casting, forging, welding, modelling, painting
tags: assembling, casting, forging, welding, modelling, painting
