en.name: Bowl
description:
While the motifs on figurative bowls painted in luster in Abbasid Iraq were stylized, a number of quite naturalistic depictions of courtiers, dancers, wrestlers, etc. are known from Fatimid Egypt.  
There are many figurative elements in Fatimid art, something that should perhaps be seen in the context of the region’s Coptic Christian tradition.
keywords: Bowl; Fatimid; Eartnenware
materials: Earthenware, painted in luster over a white glaze

en.name: Portrait of Shaykh Ibrahim al-Yaziji
short_description: Ibrahim al-Yaziji was born on 2 March 1847 in Beirut. He was educated by his father, Shaykh Nasif, and then in 1872 he became the chief editor of the magazine *al-Najah*. In 1884 he began publishing for *al-Tabib* with Bishara Zalzal and Khalil Sa'adeh. He edited all his father's books, and republished them alongside the *Diwan* of al-Mutanabbi. In 1894 he travelled around Europe, and then settled in Cairo, were he began publishing a new magazine *al-Bayan* and then later *al-Dhiya'*, for eight years. His most famous publication was titled "The Language of Newspapers". He died in Egypt on 28 December 1906.
keywords: Publisher; Books; Literature; Religion; Teacher

en.name: Fleeing the barbarians on the road to Amiens
short_description: Around 700,000 French citizens fled the country in the face of the German invasion at the beginning of the First World War (Spring 1914–1915). Pictured here are families who have abandoned their homes in a  hurry, taking just a few belongings with them on these carts.
keywords: Forced migration; exodus; First World War; France

en.name: Incense Burner
description:
This hollow cast incense burner in the shape of a bird has an opening in its chest. The decoration consists of engraving and openwork. A weld seam is visible on the lower stomach surface which could suggest that it consisted of two halves.  
The head has engraved feathers. A *kufic*\-inscription on tendril ground marks the transitional area leading towards the shoulders. The quadratic opening of the chest concludes with an interwoven band. The wings are decorated with perforated scroll ornaments. Between them lies another interwoven band. The wingtips have a drop motif. The underside is left blank.  
The characteristics of this object are the fully perforated wings and the inscription. It has, in contrast to other incense burners, a raised gaze.
holder: University Museum of Islamic Art | The Bumiller Collection
keywords: Incense burner; Bronze; metalwork; Inlaid metalwork; Iran; Iranian world; Afghanistan; Persian world; Inscription; Bird; Animal
partner: University Museum of Islamic Art | The Bumiller Collection

en.name: Buzuq
short_description: The word *buzuq* comes from Turkish. *Bashi-buzuq* for example, literally meaning 'burnt head', was one of the nicknames given to the Ottoman troops. The *buzuq* is of hybrid origin and thus is considered neither a traditional Arabic instrument nor a traditional Turkish instrument. Used for *dabke* music, the instrument was originally associated with the traveller communities in Lebanon. It consists of a long, fretted neck with four sets of double strings, and is played with a plectrum.
holder: Lebanese National Higher Conservatory of Music
keywords: Dabke; Music; Lebanese; Oriental; Hybrid; Sound

en.name: Kula prayer rug
description:
The rug-weaving areas of Anatolia are conventionally divided into western, central and eastern regions. Western Anatolian centres such as Uşak, Ghiordes, Kula and their vicinity have a long tradition of carpet and rug production. Carpets from these centres were very popular in Europe. The town of Kula lies southeast of Ghiordes. The most notable of its varied weaves is a type of prayer rug formerly considered as among the most successful Anatolian town and village weaves. Characteristic of Kula rugs are mellow and subdued colours of yellow and brown, and more solemn shades of red, blue and green. The cross panel is usually found only above the arch.  
In the central field there is a *mihrab* (prayer niche) with field repeat motifs organized in three rows. An interesting fact is that all motifs are faced in the opposite direction from the *mihrab* arch. Motifs in the central row resemble motifs on the so-called cemetery carpets. This motif has its origin in pictorial landscapes of the Turkish Baroque period beginning in the second half of the 18th century. The other two rows have vase with stylized flower motifs. Such a large repeating hanging floral ornaments are typical for mid-nineteenth century Kula carpets. Above the spandrel there is oblong field with a dragon and phoenix motif. The central field is framed with six rows of *sobokli* border and two minor borders with a dragon motif. The *sobokli* border is common in prayer rugs. It is made up of narrow stripes, usually seven, which symbolize seven steps of paradise.
keywords: prayer rug; Kula; Anatolia; Ghiordes

de.name: Dom zu St. Jakob
description: Die Kirche ist als kreuzförmiger Längsbau mit einer Abfolge von vier von Flachkuppeln überwölbten Raumeinheiten angelegt. Auf das Langhaus mit zwei querovalen Kuppeljochen folgt die ebenfalls querovale Vierung, an die seitlich querhausartige Konchen angehängt sind. Der Chor hingegen ist quadratisch. Der Raumeindruck ist wesentlich durch die Reihung der Kuppeljoche in venezianischer Tradition geprägt. Kräftige Wandpfeiler bilden das Tragegerüst und bestimmen die Wirkung des Raumprospekts, in dessen Zentrum der Hochaltar mit dem Gnadenbild der Mariahilf steht.

Die Innsbrucker St.-Jakobskirche gilt als der erste Großbau Tirols im voll entwickelten hochbarocken Stil. Sie ist ein Ableger der Füssener Bauschule. Als Alterswerk von Johann Jakob Herkomer konzipiert, wurde der Kirchenbau von Johann Georg Fischer, seinem Schüler, mit neuem spätbarocken Formengut angereichert (erkennbar z. B. an Fenster- und Gewölbeformen). Mit den Brüdern Asam wurde auch die Ausstattung durch Fresken und Stuck in zeitgemäßen Formen auf höchstem Niveau ausgeführt.
artist: Propstei St. Jakob; Landesgubernator Karl Philipp von der Pfalz
history: Schon vor der Gründung von Innsbruck 1180 bestand wohl eine erste St.-Jakobs-Kirche. Der direkte Vorgänger des heutigen Baus stammte im Wesentlichen aus dem hohen Mittelalter. Schwere Schäden bei Erdbeben machten einen Neubau nötig, der vom Landesgubernator Karl Philipp von der Pfalz unterstützt wurde. Als Architekt wurde der Allgäuer Baumeister Herkomer berufen. Der Bau wurde in seinem Todesjahr 1717 begonnen und von seinem Schüler Fischer bis 1722 vollendet. Stuck und Fresken wurden durch die Brüder Asam 1722/23 ausgeführt, die Weihe fand am 9. September 1724 statt, Altäre und die weitere Ausstattung kamen erst 1725-32 hinzu. Bombenschäden 1944, Wiederherstellung 1949-52. Zur Kathedrale 1964 erhoben.
keywords: Hochbarock; Füssener Bauschule; Doppelturmfassade; Freskomalerei;

en.name: St. Jacob’s Cathedral
names: Catholic Provost Parish Church of St. Jacob the Elder
description: The church is a cross shaped longitudinal building with a succession of four spatial units with shallow dome vaulting. The nave with two horizontal oval dome bays is followed by the crossing, also in horizontal oval form, to which transept-like side apses are appended, the choir is quadratic. The spatial impression is largely formed by the sequence of dome bays in the Venetian tradition. Massive pilasters form the supporting structure and determine the spatial prospect, at the centre of which is situated the high altar with the miraculous picture *Mariahilf* (Mary Help).

Innsbruck Cathedral is considered the first major building in Tyrol in the mature Late Baroque style. It is a product of the Füssen school of architecture, conceived by Johann Jakob Herkomer and enriched with new forms by his pupil, Johann Georg Fischer. The stuccowork and frescos were also executed in accordance with contemporary forms by the brothers Asam and are of the highest quality.
artist: Provost of St. Jacob, Provincial Governor Karl Philipp von der Pfalz

Architecture: Johann Jakob Herkomer (1648–1717), Johann Georg Fischer (1673–1747); stuccowork: Egid Quirin Asam (1692–1750); altar builder: Christoph Benedetti [n.d.], Theodor Benedetti [n.d.]; sculptor: Dominikus Molnig (1691–1761), Nikolaus Anton Moll (1676–1754); frescos: Cosmas Damian Asam (1686–1739); paintings: Josef Schöpf (1745–1822), J. G. Grasmair (1691–1751), Egid Schor (1627–1701)
history: Even before the founding of Innsbruck in 1180 there existed a building on this site. The forerunner of today’s church originates from the High Middle Ages. Earthquake damage meant a new building was required, an undertaking supported by the Provincial Governor Karl Philipp von der Pfalz. Herkomer from Allgau was appointed architect and began work on the building in the year of his death, 1717, which was subsequently completed by his pupil Fischer in 1722. Stucco and frescos were executed by the brothers Asam in 1722/23; the consecration took place on 9 September 1724. Altars and further interior work were added between 1725 and 1732. Bomb damage occurred in 1944 and reconstruction was undertaken between 1949 and 1952. The church was elevated to cathedral status in 1964.
keywords: High Baroque; Füssen school of architecture; double-tower façade; fresco paintings

en.name: *The Virgin at the Nile*
short_description: Federico Faruffini made his debut as a painter at the 1856 annual exposition of Brera. In his works the artist breaks away from the academic rule of ‘disegno’, or artistic drawing, and focuses on colour. The painting *The Virgin at the Nile* shows a sacrifice. Numerous study sketches survive. They attest that the artist was well educated on customs, traditions and architecture of ancient Egypt. In the painting the artist proposes the integration of two separate themes through different rendering styles: on the brighter upper part he sets the historic characters and in the lower zone the more narrative one, of obvious academic inspiration. The painting was brought to Paris by the artist after he decided to leave Italy because he was having difficulty finding work. After the artist committed suicide, *The Virgin at the Nile* was on display at the retrospective exhibition in Rome in 1883 where Faruffini’s entire portfolio was reconsidered, and the painting was declared his undiscussed masterpiece.
keywords: Egyptomania; Orientalism; painting; Orientalist paintings; artistic exchange; Egyptology; archaeology; imaginary trips; reinvention; historical events in painting; exoticism; architectural trends in painting; Italian painters; travel
partner: MIBACT | National Gallery of Modern Art (GNAM)

en.name: Amulet
short_description: This object is a piece of horse jewellery, an amulet worn around the horse's neck to ward off misfortune. Horse jewellery was used among Bedouins and villagers communities. This amulet consists of a silver-cased crescent composed of two joined tusks of wild boar. A ¼ Majidi Ottoman gold coin dangles from the crescent with three crescents and stars at the end. The silver chain is called “heal of gazelle”.
type: Cultic Object; ornament; talismanic object; jewellery
holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
keywords: Talisman; crescent; tusks; wild boar; heal of Gazalle
partner: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery

ar.name: مسجد النبي يونس.
description:
يتكوّن المبنى من مسجد ومقام (قبر). المسجد حديث البناء أقيم على أنقاض المسجد الأصلي الأيوبي. وهو مؤلف من طابقين، الطابق الأول يضم بين جدارنه ما تبقى من آثار المسجد الأيوبي، ومغارة مقام عليها منارة. ويمكن الوصول إلى مقام النبي يونس من هذا المسجد الكبير عبر بوابة الطابق الأرضي. كما يمكن مشاهدة ما تبقى من البناء القديم للمسجد بالتوجّه إلى وسط المسجد باتجاه القبلة.  
يتكون المقام القديم من بناء ذي مسقط مربع محاط من جهاته الجنوبية والغربية والشرقية بأروقة. ويستند كل رواق على ثلاث دعامات كبيرة تحمل عقوداً متقاطعة بشكل جميل ومتقن. ويقع تحت الأروقة شبابيك لطيفة تطل على غرفة الضريح التذكارية مربعة الشكل والتي يعلوها قبو برميلي. يغطي الضريح قماش أخضر، كما هي العادة في الأضرحة الإسلامية. وفوق الشباك الغربي لغرفة الضريح هناك لوحة منسوجة بخيوط حريرية توضح اسم صاحب القبر، وهي من الطراز العثماني المتأخر (قد تكون من زمن السلطان عبد الحميد) وتشبه مثيلاتها في الحرم الإبراهيمي. والقبر نفسه عبارة عن هيكل خشبي تقبع حجرة الدفن في أسفله في مغارة تحت المسجد لا يمكن زيارتها ولا الوصول إليها. ولا يتجه القبر باتجاه القبلة على عادة القبور في الإسلام، بل ينحرف بزاوية حادة باتجاه جنوبي غربي. وربما يعود ذلك إلى كون تراث هذا المكان يرجع إلى ما قبل الإسلام،‎ ويدلل على ذلك اكتشاف سلسلة من القبور القديمة أثناء أعمال توسيع المسجد. وينسب سكان البلدة إلى هذا المقام الكرامات، وهو يشكل مركزاً للتراث الديني والفلكلوري للبلدة.

يقع المقام في بلدة "حلحول"، إلى الجنوب من الخليل. وهو عبارة عن مقام أنشئ ضمن سلسلة من المقامات التي شجَّع سلاطين وأمراء بني أيوب على بثِّها في الديار الفلسطينية. يقع المقام التاريخي اليوم داخل مسجد ضخم حديث. ويقوم المقام المربَّع الشكل فوق مغارة، ومحاط من جهاته الثلاثة بأروقة لطيفة، تسمح للزائر مشاهدة غرفة الضريح من النوافذ المنتشرة في جدرانه. الضريح هيكل خشبي مُغطَّى بكسوة خضراء، تشبه تلك التي تغطي الأضرحة المقدسة.
artist: رعى البناء الملك المعظم عيسى بن الملك العادل الأيوبي (حكم في الفترة 615 - 624 / 1218- 1227)، ورُمِّم المبنى لاحقاً من قِبَل بعض سلاطين المماليك.
keywords: عمارة تذكارية؛ عمارة دينية؛ مسجد؛ مسجد النبي يونس.

en.name: Mosque of Nabi Yunus (Prophet Jonah).
description:
The building is composed of a mosque and a *maqam* (tomb). The mosque is a new construction undertaken amidst the rubble of the original Ayyubid mosque. Composed of two stories, the first level includes the remains of the Ayyubid mosque, while the burial area is at the basement (crypt) level of the *maqam*. The *maqam* of the Prophet Jonah is accessed from inside the mosque via the ground-floor entrance, thus the visitor can see what remains of the old mosque by passing through the centre of it in the direction of the *qibla* (south).  
The old *maqam* consists of a building with a square ground plan that is surrounded on the south, east and west by porticoes. Each portico is supported by three large piers which bear skilfully built cross vaults. Beneath the porticoes, are windows that overlook the commemorative tomb chamber, this is square in form and topped by a barrel vault. The tomb is covered by a green cloth, as is customary for Islamic shrines. Above the west window of the tomb chamber there is a woven-silk panel (*kiswa*) upon which is the name of the deceased. The panel, which resembles those found in the Haram al-Ibrahimi in Hebron, is in the late Ottoman style and may date to the period of Sultan Abd al-Hamid. The tomb itself is a wooden structure with the burial chamber beneath it in an underground room below the mosque. The tomb is inaccessible and cannot be visited. It does not face the *qibla* as is customary in Islam but deviates towards the southwest. This is perhaps because the *maqam* dates to the Pre-Islamic era, along with a series of other old tombs that have been discovered during expansion works of the mosque. The residents of this area associate the *maqam* with miracles and it forms a centre for religious heritage and the folklore of the region.

The building consists of a modern mosque and a *maqam* (tomb sanctuary) and is located in the city of Halhul, north of Hebron. The *maqam* was built as part of a series of *maqamat* whose dissemination was encouraged by Ayyubid sultans and amirs in Palestinian regions. The *maqam* is square in shape and built on top of a cave. Three of its sides are surrounded by delicate porticoes enabling visitors to view the tomb in its chamber from windows distributed in its walls. The tomb has a wooden frame shrouded in a green *kiswa* (cloth) resembling those which cover holy tombs.
artist: The building was sponsored by al-Malik Mu’addam ‘Isa bin al-Malik al-‘Adil al-Ayyubi (r. AH 615–24 / AD 1218–27). The building was renovated subsequently by a number of Mamluk sultans.
keywords: Commemorative architecture; religious architecture; mosque

es.name: Mezquita del Profeta Jonás (Nabi Yunus).
description:
El edificio se compone de una mezquita y un *maqam* ('tumba'). La mezquita es un edificio nuevo construido entre los escombros de la mezquita ayyubí original y tiene dos plantas: la primera alberga los vestigios de la mezquita ayyubí y el sótano (la cripta) es la planta en la que está la zona funeraria o *maqam*. A la del profeta Jonás se accede desde el interior de la mezquita, a través de la entrada de la planta baja. El visitante cruza la antigua mezquita por el centro, en dirección a la *qibla* (sur) y, al pasar, puede apreciar las ruinas de la antigua mezquita.  
El antiguo *maqam* es un edificio de planta cuadrada con los laterales sur, este y oeste porticados. Cada pórtico descansa sobre tres grandes pilares que sostienen bóvedas de crucería muy bien construidas. Bajo los pórticos se abren ventanas que dominan la cámara funeraria conmemorativa, que es cuadrada y está cubierta por una bóveda de cañón. Siguiendo la costumbre islámica, un manto verde cubre la tumba. Sobre la ventana occidental de la cámara hay un tejido de seda *(kiswa)* con el nombre del fallecido. Este tejido, que recuerda a los del Haram al-Ibrahimi de Hebrón, es de estilo otomano tardío y podría datar del periodo del sultán Abdulhamid. El cenotafio es una estructura de madera que reposa sobre la cámara mortuoria, situada en una sala subterránea bajo la mezquita. La tumba es inaccesible y no puede visitarse. No está orientada hacia la *qibla*, en contra de la costumbre islámica, sino hacia el suroeste. Esto se debe a que el *maqam* data de la época preislámica, al igual que otras tumbas antiguas descubiertas durante las obras de ampliación de la mezquita. Los habitantes de la zona atribuyen propiedades milagrosas a este *maqam*, que forma parte del patrimonio religioso y folclórico de la región.

Complejo arquitectónico de la ciudad de Halhul, al norte de Hebrón, que consta de una mezquita moderna y un *maqam* (tumba-santuario). Los sultanes ayyubíes y los emires de las regiones palestinas ordenaron construir una serie de *maqam*, entre los que se incluye este. Es un edificio rectangular construido sobre una cueva. Tres de sus lados están rodeados de elegantes pórticos que permiten ver la tumba a través de las ventanas de las paredes. En la cámara mortuoria hay una *kiswa* (manto) de color verde, como las que cubren las tumbas sagradas.
artist: Al-Malik Muaddam Isa ibn al-Malik al-Adil al-Ayyubi (r. 615-624 / 1218-1227) patrocinó este edificio. Continuó remodelándose bajo los mandatos de posteriores sultanes mamelucos.
keywords: Arquitectura conmemorativa; arquitectura religiosa; mezquita.

fr.name: Mosquée de Nabi Yunis (prophète Jonas).
description:
Le bâtiment se compose d'une mosquée et d'un *maqam* (tombeau). La mosquée est une construction nouvelle édifiée parmi les vestiges de la mosquée ayyoubide d'origine. Elle compte deux niveaux. Le rez-de-chaussée comprend les restes de la mosquée ayyoubide, le sous-sol ou crypte constitue la zone funéraire ou *maqam*. Le tombeau du prophète Yunis est accessible de l'intérieur de la mosquée, qui s'atteint en traversant les ruines de la partie ayyoubide.  
Le tombeau ancien consiste en une construction de plan carré entourée de portiques donnant dans les quatre directions. Chacun repose sur trois importants piliers qui soutiennent des voûtes entrecroisées. Sous les portiques, des fenêtres ouvrent sur l'intérieur du mausolée de forme carrée couverte par une voûte en berceau. La tombe est recouverte d'un tissu vert, comme il est de coutume pour les tombeaux musulmans. Au-dessus de la fenêtre ouest, un panneau de soie tissée (*kiswa*) porte le nom du disparu. Il rappelle des textiles similaires trouvés dans le Haram al-Ibrahimi à Hébron. De style ottoman tardif, il peut dater de la période du sultan Abd al-Hamid. Le tombeau lui-même est une structure en bois au-dessus d'une chambre funéraire souterraine située sous la mosquée. Elle est inaccessible et ne fait pas face à la *qibla*, mais regarde vers le sud-ouest, sans doute parce que le tombeau date de la période préislamique, de même que les autres tombes découvertes au cours des travaux d'agrandissement de la mosquée. Pour les habitants de la région, des miracles sont attribués à ce *maqam*, qui appartient au patrimoine religieux et au folklore local.

Le bâtiment se compose d’une mosquée moderne et d’un *maqam* (tombeau) et est situé dans la ville de Halhoul, au nord d’Hébron. Ce *maqam* fait partie d’une série, leur multiplication ayant été encouragée par les sultans et les émirs ayyoubides dans les régions de Palestine. Le *maqam* est de plan carré et placé au-dessus d’une crypte. Trois de ses faces sont soutenues par d’élégants portiques permettant aux visiteurs de voir le tombeau dans sa chambre à partir d’ouvertures ménagées dans ses parois. Le tombeau lui-même consiste en une structure en bois enveloppée d’un tissu vert (*kiswa*) rappelant ceux qui couvrent les tombes sacrées.
artist: La construction, commanditée par al-Malik Mu‘addam ‘Isa bin al-Malik al-‘Adil al-Ayyoubi (r. 615-624 H / 1218-1227 J.-C.), a été rénovée par plusieurs sultans mamelouks au cours des siècles.
keywords: Architecture commémorative ; architecture religieuse ; mosquée

en.name: Ribat
description:
The *ribat* faces the Great Mosque. This monastery-fortress was no doubt founded towards the end of the 1st/beginning of the 8th century, but was completely rebuilt by Ziyadat Allah I at the heart of the Great Fortress, *al-Qasr al-Kabir*, which he had erected in 205/821. A garrison composed of about 50 warrior monks, who had avowed themselves to the *jihad*, lived there permanently. This in particular, gave the army base a dual character, one that was both military and religious, that was manifested through the austerity of the building, the crampedness of the rooms and the choice of layout. The *ribat*, square in shape measuring 36 m. on each side, built in stone, has been fitted out with a round tower in each corner except for the south-eastern one, where, instead, there is a square-base circular minaret of outstanding beauty. It was inspired by the prototype of Abbassid minarets that became popular across the Maghreb from the end of the 2nd/8th century. Semi-circular towers stand half-way across the walls except on the south side where there is a rectangular porch that precedes the sole entrance to the fort. This direct access entrance, a form that preceded the elbow-shaped entrance which became common in defence buildings, appeared in Ifriqiya from the 3rd/9th century. The building’s entrance seems to take after the entrances of the Abbasid palaces of Ukhaydir and Atshan, palaces that also heavily influenced the exterior architecture of Sousse’s *ribat*. In all other respects, the *ribat* is a reproduction of the original plan of the Monastir Ribat founded by Harthama, the author of several similar military construction works found on the eastern front.  
The *ribat*’s porch is surmounted by a defence feature consisting of a group of machicolations made of parallel stone openings or slits. Its pole-axes are surmounted by a domed kiosk on squinches, made of freestone, constituting the oldest specimen of its kind known to us. This allows for the study of the evolution of this prototype dome, which originated in the East, was adopted in Ifriqiya in the 2nd/8th century, and reached its maturity as the dome of the *mihrab* of the Great Mosque of Kairouan (3rd/9th century). The dome of the Ribat of Sousse constitutes an intermediary stage in its evolution, as it demonstrates by the direct transformation from octagon to circular skullcap. From the porch, one enters a square hallway covered by a well-bonded groin vault, appearing to confirm the survival of certain Byzantine and Roman traditions. The central courtyard is surrounded by four galleries, covered by a series of barrel vaults, whose arcades rest on freestone pillars. The north and east wings, rebuilt in 1134/1722, are covered by groin vaults. The ground floor is composed of 33 cramped rooms, covered by barrel vaults made of rubble. One reaches the first floor via a staircase that leads onto a passage used by rooms on three of the sides; the fourth side houses the prayer hall. The latter consists of 11 naves and two bays. The wall of the *qibla*, the same wall as that of the rampart enclosure, is pierced with arches: the worshippers could thus transform themselves at any moment to soldiers of war in order to defend the *ribat*.  
There is not a single element that expresses more eloquently the mixed nature of the *ribat* than this: it is an institution that is both simultaneously religious and military. After the confrontation between the two Mediterranean shores had come to an end, and the techniques involved in warfare had evolved, the military role of the *ribat* ceased, and the essential purpose retained therein was that of the spiritual. Several *ribat*s were transformed into schools in which the religious sciences were taught; in fact, the architectural plan of *ribat*s directly inspired that of Tunisian *madrasa*s.

es.name: Ribat
description:
El *ribat* se encuentra enfrente de la Mezquita Mayor. Esta fortaleza monacal fue fundada, sin duda, a fines del siglo I/p. VIII, pero fue completamente renovada por Ziyadat Allah I, y quedó incluida en la gran fortaleza (el-Ksar el-Kebir) que se construyó en el año 205/821. Una guarnición compuesta por unos 50 monjes guerreros juramentados por el *yihad* residía allí permanentemente. Esta particularidad confiere a la construcción un doble carácter, militar y religioso, que se traduce claramente en la austeridad del edificio, en lo exiguo de sus habitaciones y en la elección de su trazado general.  
El *ribat*, de forma cuadrada (con unos 36m de lado, construido en piedra), está provisto en sus ángulos de torres redondas, a excepción del ángulo sudeste, en el que se eleva un alminar circular, aunque de base cuadrada, de una soberbia belleza. Está inspirado en el modelo de los alminares abbasíes, extendido en el Magreb desde finales del siglo II/VIII. En mitad de sus muros laterales aparecen unas torres semicirculares, excepto en la parte sur, donde se eleva un porche rectangular que antecede a la única entrada del fortín. Este acceso directo, que precede a la entrada en zigzag de los edificios defensivos, apareció en Ifriqiya a partir del siglo III/IX. El acceso al edificio parece inspirarse en las entradas de los palacios abbasíes de Ujaydir y de Atchan, que influyen en toda la arquitectura exterior del *ribat* de Susa que, por otra parte, constituye una reproducción del plano inicial del *ribat* de Monastir, fundado por Hartama, autor de varias obras militares análogas, situadas en la costa oriental.  
El porche del ribat está coronado por un dispositivo de defensa, formado por un conjunto de matacanes con hendiduras paralelas, en piedra. Estas mazas están, a su vez, coronadas por un edículo con una cúpula sobre trompas en sillares que constituye el más antiguo ejemplo de su género. Esto permite estudiar la evolución de este tipo de cúpula llegado de Oriente y adoptado en Ifriqiya en el siglo II/VIII, que alcanza su madurez con la cúpula del *mihrab* de la Mezquita Mayor de Kairuán, ya en el siglo III/IX. La cúpula del *ribat* de Susa constituye una etapa intermedia, que se caracteriza por el paso directo del octógono al círculo. Desde el porche, se accede a un vestíbulo cuadrado cubierto por una bóveda de aristas bien aparejada, cuya existencia confirma la supervivencia de ciertas tradiciones bizantinas y romanas. El patio central está rodeado por cuatro galerías cuyos arcos reposan sobre pilares de piedra tallada y aparecen cubiertos por bóvedas de cañón. Las alas norte y este, reconstruidas en 1134/1722, están rematadas, en cambio, por bóvedas de aristas. El piso bajo queda configurado por 33 exiguas celdas, cubiertas por bóvedas de cañón en sillería. Se accede al primer piso por una escalera que llega a un pasillo, comunicando así las celdas por tres de sus partes; la cuarta parte está reservada a la sala de oración. Esta última está formada por once naves de dos tramos. El muro de la *qibla*, que se confunde con la muralla del recinto, está horadado por arquerías, de forma que los fieles pueden así transformarse en todo momento en guerreros para defender el *ribat*.  
Podemos ver así, de forma muy elocuente, el carácter mixto del *ribat*, institución a la vez religiosa y militar. Cuando terminó la confrontación entre ambas orillas del Mediterráneo y tras el profundo cambio surgido en las técnicas de guerra, el *ribat* perdió su papel militar, aunque conservó una vocación esencialmente espiritual. Varios *ribat*s fueron transformados en escuelas, donde se estudiaban las ciencias religiosas. Los planos de las *medersa*s de Túnez se inspiraron en el tipo arquitectónico de los *ribat*s.

fr.name: Le Ribat
description:
Face à la Grande Mosquée se trouve le *ribat*. Cette forteresse-monastère fut sans doute fondée à la fin du Ier/d. VIIIe siècle, mais complètement réaménagée par Ziyadat Allah Ier au sein de la Grande Forteresse, *el-Qasr el-Kebir*, qu’il édifia en 205/821. Une garnison composée d’une cinquantaine de moines guerriers voués au *djihad* y résidait en permanence. Cette particularité confère à cet ouvrage militaire un double caractère, militaire et religieux, qui se traduit d’une façon manifeste dans l’austérité du bâtiment, l’exiguïté des chambres et le choix du plan.  
Le *ribat*, de forme carrée de 36 m de côté, bâti en pierres, est pourvu aux angles de tours rondes sauf à l’angle sudest où s’élève un minaret circulaire, de base carrée, d’une superbe beauté. Il s’inspire du prototype des minarets abbassides qui s’est répandu au Maghreb à partir de la fin du IIe/VIIIe siècle. Au milieu des courtines figurent des tours semi-circulaires, exception faite du côté sud, où s’élève un porche rectangulaire qui précède l’unique entrée du fortin. Cet accès direct qui a précédé les entrées en chicane dans les bâtiments défensifs est apparu en Ifriqiya à partir du IIIe/IXe siècle. L’accès au bâtiment semble s’inspirer des entrées des palais abbassides d’Ukhaydhir et de Atshan qui ont beaucoup influencé l’architecture extérieure du *ribat* de Sousse —lequel, par ailleurs, constitue une reproduction du plan initial du *ribat* de Monastir, fondé par Harthama, auteur de plusieurs ouvrages mili taires analogues se trouvant sur le front oriental.  
Le porche du *ribat* est surmonté d’un dispositif de défense formé par un ensemble de mâchicoulis constitués par des fentes parallèles en pierre. Ces assommoirs sont surmontés par un édicule à coupole sur trompes, en pierre de taille, qui constitue le plus ancien spécimen de son genre qui nous soit parvenu; il permet d’étudier l’évolution de ce prototype de coupole venu d’orient et adopté par l’Infriqiya au IIe/VIIIe siècle, et qui atteignit sa maturité avec la coupole du *mihrab* de la Grande Mosquée de Kairouan (IIIe/IXe siècle). La coupole du *ribat* de Sousse constitue une étape intermédiaire qui se distingue par le passage direct de l’octogone à la calotte circulaire. Du porche, on accède à un vestibule carré couvert d’une voûte d’arête bien appareillée qui semble confirmer la survivance de certaines traditions byzantines et romanes. La cour centrale est entourée de quatre galeries dont les arcades reposent sur des piliers en pierre de taille et que couvre une série de voûtes en berceau. Les ailes nord et est, refaites en 1134/1722, sont couvertes en voûtes d’arête. Le rez-de-chaussée est constitué de 33 cellules exiguës, couvertes de voûtes en berceau faites en moellons. On accède au premier étage par un escalier qui débouche sur une allée desservant des cellules sur trois côtés; le quatrième côté est réservé à la salle de prière. Cette dernière est constituée de onze nefs et de deux travées. Le mur de la *qibla*, qui se confond avec le rempart d’enceinte, est percé d’archères: les fidèles peuvent ainsi se transformer à tout moment en guerriers pour défendre le *ribat*.  
Nul trait ne peut exprimer d’une façon plus éloquente le caractère mixte du ribat: institution à la fois religieuse et militaire.  
A la fin de la confrontation entre les deux rives de la Méditerranée et à la suite de l’évolution des techniques de guerre, le *ribat* a perdu son rôle militaire et gardé une vocation essentiellement spirituelle. Plusieurs *ribat*s furent transformés en écoles où l’on professait les sciences religieuses; d’ailleurs, les plans des médersas en Tunisie s’inspirent parfaitement du type architectural des *ribat*s.

en.name: Borghese Palace
description:
The palace, elongated precisely to connect the existing Colonna and Massimo palaces, is characterised by the monumental three-storey gallery that rises to align the two palaces and whose architectural decorative layout is visible from the outside. Of particular interest is the elliptical, sweeping staircase, adorned by heraldic symbols, also designed by Vasanzio, next to which there stands the first genuine *ex novo* building expansion intended by the Cardinal: as if highlighting the new ownership of the entire region, which was so markedly characterised by the Borghese stamp.  
The intention to restructure the entire site, almost as if to overpower the village, is evident immediately from the entrance (the Borghese arch), which is characterised by its merlon-decorated top-storey *loggia*, in addition to the square and terrace. This monumental design used a model that is comparable to the later Piazza di Corte in Ariccia, thereby contributing to the unity of the entire design.  
Inside, the *loggia* is painted with panoramic frescos that were originally attributed to Paul Brill, but which are now attributed to Giovanni Battista Corradini, whom it is known was active in Rome in the first half of the 17th century, and also undertook some projects in Sicily.

The palace has an elongated structure with its short side bordering the square, duly enlarged and arranged by Scipione Borghese, and the rear façade of the long side fully facing the Valle del Sacco and the Via Latina, which was the most important route to Southern Italy. The whole is brought together by the monumental three-storey gallery that rises up to align the two older, originally separate, buildings, and it is distinguished by decorative architectural divisions that are visible from the outside.
artist: Flemish architect: Jan van Santen (also known as Giovanni Vasanzio; c. 1550, Utrecht ­­– died Rome 1621)
history: Cardinal Borghese, nephew of Paul V (1605–21), acquired the Montefortino estate (the village changed its name to Artena in 1873) from the Colonna family in 1614. The feudal Colonna nobility was replaced by a noble middle-class family, who were originally jurisconsults from Siena, and arrived in Rome in the 16th century; a similar situation to that of the Barberini family in Palestrina. In addition to modernising the entire village by way of a master plan that gave a scenographic entrance to the ancient stronghold, Scipione Borghese sought to completely restructure the existing palace by unifying the two originally separate buildings (the Colonna and the Massimo buildings), making it one of the largest palaces in Latium. After Vasanzio’s death in 1621 his design was completed by others.
keywords: Feudal, architecture, conversion, Baroque
partner: Province of Rome (Città metropolitana di Roma Capitale)

it.name: Palazzo Borghese
description:
Il Palazzo, dalla struttura allungata, proprio per collegare i palazzi preesistenti dei Colonna e dei Massimo, è contraddistinto dalla monumentale Galleria a tre piani che sviluppandosi in altezza riesce ad allineare i due palazzi e presenta una partitura architettonica decorativa visibile dall’esterno. Di particolare interesse lo scalone ellittico con simboli araldici, ugualmente progettato dal Vasanzio. All’interno la loggia è affrescata con vedute già attribuite a Paul Brill e recentemente ricondotte a Giovanni Battista Corradini, pittore attivo a Roma nella prima metà del XVII secolo di cui si conoscono alcune opere in Sicilia.  
La volontà di compiere un’opera di ristrutturazione urbanistica dell’intero borgo è già evidente nell’arco di accesso, l’arco Borghese, la cui sommità a loggia ornata di merli lo caratterizza quasi come un’appendice della nuova piazza-terrazza, secondo un modulo urbanistico che si può confrontare con la più tarda piazza di corte di Ariccia, e contribuisce così all’unità dell’intero progetto. Accanto all’inizio della rampa di salita si svolse inoltre la prima vera e propria espansione edilizia *ex novo* voluta dal Cardinale, a sottolineare quasi la presa di possesso dell’intero territorio che veniva così marcatamente connotato dall’impronta borghesiana.

Il Palazzo presenta una struttura allungata che ha il lato corto sulla piazza, appositamente ingrandita e sistemata da Scipione Borghese, e il fronte retrostante del lato lungo completamente affacciato a dominare la Valle del Sacco e la via Latina che costituiva il più importante asse di penetrazione verso l’Italia meridionale. L’elemento unificante è costituito dalla monumentale Galleria a tre piani che sviluppandosi in altezza riesce ad allineare i due palazzi preesistenti, in origine separati, ed è contraddistinta da una partitura architettonica decorativa visibile dall’esterno.
artist: Jan van Santen (Giovanni Vasanzio), architetto di origine fiamminga (Utrecht 1550ca.) morto a Roma nel 1621
history: Il cardinale Borghese, nipote di Paolo V (1605-1621), nel 1614 acquistò dai Colonna il feudo di Montefortino, borgo che dal 1873 prese il nome di Artena, con una operazione di sostituzione della nuova nobiltà di matrice borghese – la famiglia era in origine formata da giureconsulti senesi approdati a Roma durante il XVI secolo – a quella feudale dei Colonna, analoga a quella più tardi operata dai Barberini a Palestrina. Oltre a modernizzare l’intero abitato attraverso un vero e proprio piano regolatore che trasformò in senso scenografico l’accesso all’antica rocca, volle ristrutturare completamente il Palazzo preesistente unificando due corpi di fabbrica in origine separati, quello dei Colonna e l’altro dei Massimo, rendendolo così uno dei più vasti palazzi laziali. I lavori su progetto del Vasanzio furono completati da altri dopo la sua morte.
keywords: Architettura di origine feudale rimaneggiata in epoca barocca

en.name: 'Saz'-style drawing of a dragon amid foliage
description: The mid‑sixteenth century saw the flourishing of the so‑called *saz* style—characterized by the depiction of stylised, serrated leaf foliage, often paired with fantastic creatures including dragons and phoenixes. This imagery appears on Ottoman art in a variety of media, including textiles. This magnificent dragon drawing is ascribed to the master of the style, Shah Quli, an artist who emigrated from Iran to Istanbul and became head of the royal atelier under Sultan Süleyman the Magnificent.

en.name: Lithographs after the panoramic photograph taken by Robertson and Beato, *Faust: Poligrafisch Illustrirte*, Zeitschrift, 1857, Vienna
short_description: James Robertson is the first Istanbul photographer known to have taken 360 degree panoramic photographs of the city. The first panorama, which was taken in May 1854 from the War Ministry tower in Beyazıt, consists of twelve separate photographs. The most successful printed reproductions based on Robertson’s photographs curiously enough were produced in Vienna. Issues of *Faust* published during 1857 report fascinating bits of information as well as pictures that are important to the history of printing and visual arts in the Ottoman Empire. A plate published in *Faust* contained a panoramic view from the Istanbul Beyazıt tower that is made from Robertson’s panorama.
keywords: Istanbul panorama; Faust; tower of War Ministry in Beyazıt

ar.name: دلائل الخيرات للجزولي
description: إن كتاب دلائل الخيرات  وشوارق الأنوار في ذكر الصلاة على النبي المختار الذي عرف اختصارا بدلائل الخيرات هو أحد الأعمال الأكثر شعبية للذكر في العالم الإسلامي. وقد تم تاليفه من قبل أحد المؤلفين من سوس ، أبو عبد الله محمد ابن سليمان ابن أبو بكر الجزولي (توفي عام 1645). وكما يبين اسمه يتألف العمل من العديد من الصلوات على النبي مع ألقابه ووصف لقبره وتصوير بياني الذي وجد في أكثر النسخ الجنوب أفريقية. لكن النسخ العثمانية للعمل خاصة تلك العائدة للقرن الثامن عشر فصاعدا تميل لأن تتضمن أشكال منظورية للحرمين الشريفين في مكة والمدينة وبالتالي تختلف عن نص المخطوطة.إن طراز الكتابة – هو مغربي شفاف / واضح – والصيغة المربعة لهذه المخطوطة يجعل أصلها شمال أفريقيا. ولكن التذهيب وتضمين مكة والتجليد الأصيل هي أقرب للأعمال العثمانية الاعتيادية  ومن الممكن أن تكون قد نسخت في أي مكان وربما مكة .

en.name: The *Dala’il al-khayrat* of al-Jazuli
description:
The *Dala’il al-khayrat wa shawariq al-anwar fi dhikr al-salat ‘ala al-nabi al-mukhtar* – better known by its abbreviated tilte, *Dala’il al-khayrat* – is one of the most popular works of prayer in the Islamic world. It was composed by a natïve of Sus, Abu ‘Abdullah Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn Abu Bakr al-Jazuli (d. 1645).  
  
As its name suggests, the work consists of numerous prayers for the Prophet, together with his epithets, and a description of his tomb, a diagrammatic depiction of which is found in most North African copies. Ottoman copies of the work, especially those from the 18th century onwards, however, tend to include perspective views of the two Holy Sanctuaries at Mecca and Medina, thus diverging from the text of the manuscript.  
  
The style of writing – a clear, Maghribi hand – and the square format of this manuscript place its origin in North Africa. However, the illumination, the inclusion of Mecca, and the original binding, are closer to mainstream Ottoman work, and it is posible that it was copied elsewhere, perhaps in Mecca.

en.name: Batári-Crivelli Carpet Fragment
description: Dating from the first half of the 14th century a new type of carpet with Anatolian animal figures appeared in European, mostly Italian paintings. These floor rugs utilized squares or octagons, each shape containing animal or bird figures. This design was popular until the last third of the 15th century and was subsequently replaced by carpets of only geometric design. Literature classifies the early 15th–16th century Ottoman Turkish rugs by the name of the European painters who depicted them. The dating of these carpets relies on the dates of the paintings as clues. In two paintings by the Venetian artist Carlo Crivelli (c. 1435–c. 1495), the right wing of the *Annunciation Triptych* (1482, Frankfurt am Main, Städel Museum and the altarpiece *The Annunciation with St Emidius of 1486* (London, National Gallery), an as-yet unknown carpet type appears. Two star-shaped medallions filled with birds and geometric forms appear in a yellow background. This design element, the only known specimen of the carpet type in Crivelli’s picture with naturalistic bird representations, became a part of the collection of the Museum of Applied Arts in 1917, likely acquired from Transylvania. Its world fame owes to Ferenc Batári (1934–2005), a prominent expert of Ottoman Turkish carpets who published this design under the name “Crivelli Rug” in his study of 1984. The Museum re-named it “Batári–Crivelli Rug Fragment” in honour of Ferenc Batári on the second anniversary of his death.
keywords: Bird; Fragment; Ottoman rug; Wool

en.name: Panel with abstract decoration
description: This carved panel comes from Egypt, where wood, on account of its rarity and cost, was decorated with care and used in contexts generally reserved for luxury materials. Although it is impossible to say how this wood panel was used originally, it is possible to assign it to the late 3rd/late 9th century on the basis of its distinctive decoration. Decorated in the bevelled style, the panel depicts highly stylised leaves that have been transformed into abstract motifs. As is typical of this style, it is impossible to distinguish between background and foreground or between natural and abstract forms. The bevelled style may have first been developed at Samarra, in northern Iraq, which replaced Baghdad as the Abbasid capital, from Hegira 221–279 / AD 836 to 892. This style was quickly adopted in other parts of the Islamic empire including Egypt, as exemplified by the decoration in the Mosque of Ibn Tulun, Cairo.
holder: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA)
dates: Hegira late 3rd century / AD late 9th century

de.name: Ansicht von Stiftsgebäuden und Kirche
description: Wiewohl die Fassaden des Stifts und der Kirche aus der ersten Bauphase stammen, sind sie doch wesentlich von der Stukkierung aus dem Ende des 17. Jahrhunderts geprägt. Immerhin dürfte das Kirchenportal noch zu der urkundlichen belegten Erstausstattung des Alexander Colin gehören. Die dreiachsige Kirchenfassade mit ionischer Kolossalordnung wird von einem geschweiften und getreppten Giebel bekrönt, der sich im Wesentlichen aus drei mächtigen Figurennischen zusammenfügt.
artist: Giovanni und Alberto Lucchese; Alexander Colin (Portal, Zuschreibung)

en.name: View of convent buildings and church
description: Although the façade of the convent and the church originate from the first building phase they are largely characterised by the stuccowork from the end of the 17th century. Nevertheless, documents confirm that the church portal forms part of the original inventory from Alexander Colin. The tri-axial church façade with Ionic colossal order is crowned by a curved and stepped gable which is largely composed of three massive alcoves for statues.
artist: Giovanni Lucchese [n.d.], Alberto Lucchese [n.d.]; Alexander Colin [n.d.]

ar.name: لوحة باب
description: ارتبط تطعيم السطوح الداخلية بالعاج مع إنتاج الأثاث والعناصر المعمارية في أواخر القرون الوسطى في مصر. وهذه الطريقة الشاقة في التصنيع التي استخدمت العاج والخشب النادر مثل الأبنوس تطلبت غالبا أن تكون العناصر الإفرادية  بحجم صغير والتي تقص وتحفر عليها أشكال معقدة وبعدها تشكل مثل الفسيفساء حتى تكوِّنِ وحدة أكبر وذات تصميم هندسي بشكل عام. والدقة في القص والتجميع كانت أساسية نظرا لأن كل قطعة تؤثر على الكل. ومن الصعب القول تماما كيف يعمل الباب الحالي ولكن في الأرجح أنه واحد من زوج من الأبواب ربما لخزانة ركبت في الجدار لبناء ديني أو دنيوي.

en.name: Door Panel
description: Ivory inlays were frequently combined with wood in the production of furniture and architectural fittings in late medieval Egypt. This elaborate method of fabrication, which used costly ivory and rare woods like ebony, required that individual elements, often of minute size, be cut, carved with intricate motifs, and then carefully constructed like a mosaic to form a larger unit of generally geometric design. Accuracy in cutting and assembling was essential since every piece affects the whole. It is difficult to say exactly how the present door functioned, but most likely it was one of a pair, perhaps for a cupboard set into a wall of either a religious or a secular building.
holder: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA)
dates: Hegira second half of 7th century / AD second half of the 13th century
keywords: Panel; door; Mamluk; architectural element; wood; ivory; carving; carved decoration; marquetry; inlay; geometric design; ebony
partner: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA)

ar.name: كوب نصف كروي.
description: قطعة تعود لجزء من الجسم تتكون من حافة جزئية وقاعدة كاملة. تتميز الحافة بشفة مقطعها نصف دائري، وتستند على ساق عالية حلقية؛ لون العجينة أسمر فاتح مائل للوردي؛ ويقدم السطحان مينا ملتصق لونه أبيض لامع قليلاً. يحتوي السطح الداخلي على شكل نجمي مدهون بالأخضر مع ثمانية أشعة متساوية الأبعاد ومرتبة انطلاقاً من المركز. من خلال نوعية ونعومة عجينته، يوحي هذا الكوب نصف الكروي المسطح بالجو المترف والاستخدامات المنزلية في مدينة سيلفش خلال ذلك الوقت.

كوبٌ نصف كروي يرجع إلى الفترة الموحدية؛ زُخرف بنجمة مدهونة باللون الأخضر، مع ثمانية أشعة متساوية الأبعاد مرتبة انطلاقا من المركز. تشير جودة ونعومة القطعة إلى جو مترف واستعمال منزلي من المحتمل أن يكون في مدينة سيلفش خلال هذه الفترة.
dynasty: الفترة الموحدية، القرنان 6 - 7 الهجريان / القرنان 12 – 13 الميلاديان
materials: فخار مطلي بالمينا وملمع بزخارف على شكل نجوم.
tags: فخار مطلي بالمينا وملمع بزخارف على شكل نجوم.

en.name: Hemispherical plate.
description: A fragment corresponding to a section of the body including part of the rim and the complete base. The rim has a lip semi-circular in cross-section and the base has a high foot-ring. It is made from pinkish beige paste. Both surfaces are coated in white enamel with a slight sheen. The interior surface has a motif of intersecting lines, painted green, creating eight equidistant spokes radiating from the centre. The quality and fine grain of the paste of this flattened hemispherical plate reflects the sophistication of domestic articles used in Silves in this period.

Hemispherical bowl from the Almohad period. It is decorated with a star painted in green consisting of eight evenly spaced spokes radiating from the centre. The quality and finesse of this piece suggest a refined environment and probable domestic use in the town on Silves during that time.
keywords: trade
materials: Enamelled and glazed ceramic with decoration of intersecting lines in a star.
tags: Enamelled and glazed ceramic with decoration of intersecting lines in a star.

es.name: Cuenco.
description:
Fragmento del cuerpo de un cuenco, con parte del borde y el fondo completo. Tiene pie alto y anular, y el labio del borde es de sección semicircular. La pasta es de color beige rosada. Ambas superficies, exterior e interior, presentan un esmalte adherente de color blanco con cierto brillo. La interior está decorada con un motivo en estrella de color verde, con ocho rayos equidistantes.  
La calidad y delicadeza de la pasta dan idea del ambiente de refinamiento y de los usos domésticos de la Silves de entonces.

Cuenco hemisférico del periodo almohade, con decoración de color verde en forma de estrella de ocho rayos equidistantes que parten de su centro. La calidad y delicadeza de esta pieza dan idea del ambiente de refinamiento y de los usos domésticos en la ciudad de Silves durante aquel periodo.
dates: Siglo VI o VII de la Hégira / XII–XIII d. C.
keywords: comercio
materials: Cerámica esmaltada y vidriada con decoración estrellada.
tags: Cerámica esmaltada y vidriada con decoración estrellada.

fr.name: Coupe hémisphérique.
description: Fragment correspondant à une portion du corps avec bordure partielle et base entière. La bordure est à lèvre de section semi-circulaire et s'appuie sur un haut pied annulaire. La pâte est de couleur beige rosé. Les deux surfaces présentent un émail adhérent de couleur blanche légèrement brillante. La surface intérieure contient un motif en étoile, peint en vert, avec huit rayons équidistants et disposés à partir du centre. Par la qualité et la finesse de sa pâte, cette coupe hémisphérique aplatie évoque l'ambiance raffinée et les usages domestiques de la Silves d'alors.

Coupe hémisphérique de la période almohade. Elle est décorée d'une étoile peinte en vert, avec huit rayons équidistants disposés à partir du centre. La qualité et la finesse de cette pièce évoquent un environnement raffiné et un probable usage domestique dans la ville de Silves à cette époque.
dates: VIe-VIIe siècles de l’Hégire (XIIe-XIIIe siècles J.-C.).
materials: Céramique émaillée et vernissée à décor étoilé.
tags: Céramique émaillée et vernissée à décor étoilé.

pt.name: Taça hemisférica.
description:
Fragmento correspondendo a porção do corpo com parte de bordo e fundo completo. O bordo tem o lábio de secção semi-circular e assenta em pé alto e anelar. Pasta de cor beje rosada. Ambas as superfícies apresentam esmalte aderente de cor branca com algum brilho. A superfície interior oferece um motivo em estrela, pintado de cor verde, com oito raios equidistantes entre si e dispostos a partir do centro.  
  
Esta taça hemisférica achatada mostra-nos, pela qualidade e finura da sua pasta, o ambiente de requinte e os usos domésticos da Silves de então.

Taça hemisférica do período almóada. Apresenta uma decoração em estrela, pintada a verde, com oito raios equidistantes entre si e dispostos a partir do centro. A qualidade e finura desta peça sugerem o ambiente de requinte e os usos domésticos da cidade de Silves durante aquele período.

dates: Séc. VI-VII AH / Séc. XII-XIII AD.

ar.name: زخرفة من قلنسوة انكشارية
description: إن التفوق العسكري الذي ساعد في بسط السلطة العثمانية عالميا كان يستند بشكل كبير على القوات الإنكشارية – وهي قوات مشاة هجومية وكجزء من لباسهم فإن الإنكشارية كانوا يرتدون قلنسوات شكلها مثل الجورب التي كانت تلبس أيضا على الساعد كتزيين مثل هذا المثال النادر المطلي بالفضة والقطعة المقعرة بشكل طفيف المزينة بتصاميم متقنة هندسية مشغولة تحمل شارات وعلامات مميزة تظهر الولاء الإنكشاري للسلطان – في الأغلب هي ملعقة والتي تشير إلى أن الحاكم هو الذي قدم له حساءه اليومي.

en.name: Ornament from a Janissary’s cap
description: The military supremacy that had helped make the Ottomans a world power was largely based on the highly disciplined Janissary corps – crack infantry troops. As a part of their uniform, the Janissaries wore a distinctive felt hat somewhat like a stocking cap in appearance, known as a *börk*, to which was affixed just above the forehead an ornament such as this rare silver gilt example. The slightly concave device, decorated with delicately worked geometric designs, would have held an insignia demonstrating the Janissary's loyalty to the Sultan–possibly a feather or even a spoon, signifying that it was the ruler who provided him with his daily soup.
holder: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA)
keywords: Military object; metalwork; geometric decoration; Ottoman army; costume; Janissaries; devşirme; military wear
materials: Silver, gilt, decorated with flattened wire and granulation
tags: Silver, gilt, decorated with flattened wire and granulation

ar.name: مصباح زيتي مصنوع من النحاس الممزوج
description: للوهلة الأولى يبدو هذا الوعاء الغريب، المسبوك والمزدان بزخارف منقوشة، كإبريق. ومع ذلك، واستنادًا إلى الحكم على بقائه إلى يومنا هذا والكتابات المنقوشة المعاصرة والفن التصويري، فإنه على الأرجح كان يستخدم كمصباح للقراءة. فجسمه البصلي الشكل مصمم لتوفير الزيت اللازم للإنارة المتواصلة لفترة طويلة، كما صممت فوهته لوضع الفتيل.
