en.name: Tile from ceramic inscription panel of the Dome of the Rock.
description:
A tile forming part of a ceramic inscription panel that once decorated the exterior octagonal pinnacle of the Dome of the Rock. Sultan Sulayman the Magnificent (r. AH 926–73 / AD 1520–66) commissioned the panel while renovation work of the Dome of the Rock was being carried out, in around AH 969 / AD 1560. Each tile is 25 cm high by 25 cm long, and the whole inscription panel is 160 m long. The panel is decorated with a long Qur'anic inscription consisting of the complete text of the chapter “Ya-sin” (Chapter 36). The text is written in the Ottoman *thuluth* script in white against a dark-blue background. The inscription is interspersed with vegetal decoration consisting of intertwining spiralling stems, with blossoms and leaves. The tiles have a characteristic simplicity, and are of fine colouring and very detailed workmanship. The tiles represent an early example of Ottoman ceramics, used generally in architecture during the period, and more specifically in the Dome of the Rock. Buildings were often panelled with ceramic tiles during the Ottoman period, in fact, such tile work is a distinguishing trait of Ottoman contributions to the restoration and renovation of holy places, not only in Jerusalem but also in places such as Mecca and Medina.  
The Islamic Museum have acquired all sections of this inscription panel which was removed from The Dome of the Rock in 1960 during restoration works. The Museum has since housed and preserved the inscription panel as a witness to the first stage of ceramic-tile panelling on the outer walls of the Dome of the Rock. It is worth noting that previous to these tiles, the outer octagon of Dome of the Rock was covered with a glass mosaic, which had deteriorated badly due to age, until Sulayman the Magnificent ordered the removal of the damaged mosaic and replaced it with these tiles.

A glazed tile from a band that wrapped round the exterior octagonal pinnacle of the Dome of the Rock, ordered by Sultan Sulayman the Magnificent during his renovation of the Dome. It is written in *thuluth* script in white against a dark-blue background. The verses are interposed with vegetal decorations.
holder: Islamic Museum, al-Aqsa Mosque / al-Haram al-Sharif.
keywords: Ceramic tile; thuluth; vegetal decoration; “Ya-sin”; glazed tiles

es.name: Panel de azulejos epigráfico de la Cúpula de la Roca.
description:
Este conjunto de azulejos con inscripción formaba parte de un gran panel que decoraba el tambor octogonal exterior de la Cúpula de la Roca. Hacia 969 / 1560, el sultán Suleyman el Magnífico (r. 926-973 / 1520-1566) ordenó la restauración de la Cúpula de la Roca y mandó hacer este panel de 160 m de largo, compuesto por azulejos de 25 × 25 cm. El panel está decorado con una larga inscripción del Corán que reproduce entera la sura 36, “Ya sin”. Está escrito en letra *zuluz* otomana blanca sobre un fondo azul oscuro, salpicado con motivos decorativos vegetales en forma de tallos rizados entrelazados, con flores y hojas. Los azulejos se caracterizan por su sencillez, por su calidad técnica y por la exquisita aplicación de los colores. Estos azulejos son ejemplo de un tipo de cerámica de principios de la época otomana que se usó de forma generalizada en arquitectura y, en particular, en la Cúpula de la Roca. En la era otomana, los edificios solían revestirse con azulejos; de hecho, la presencia de este tipo de revestimientos en recintos sagrados de Jerusalén y otras ciudades como La Meca o Medina es señal inequívoca de que los otomanos participaron en su restauración y renovación.  
En 1960, el Museo Islámico adquirió el panel epigráfico completo retirado de la Cúpula de la Roca durante su restauración. Desde entonces, el museo lo conserva como testimonio de la primera etapa de la tradición de recubrir con azulejos los muros exteriores de la Cúpula de la Roca. Cabe mencionar que, antes de instalar este panel, el octágono exterior de la Cúpula de la Roca estaba decorado con un mosaico de vidrio que estaba muy deteriorado cuando el sultán Suleyman el Magnífico ordenó sustituirlo por estos azulejos.

El sultán Suleyman el Magnífico ordenó la colocación de una banda de azulejos alrededor del tambor octogonal exterior de la Cúpula de la Roca cuando renovó este templo. La inscripción, en letra *zuluz*, es blanca sobre un fondo azul oscuro. En los versículos se intercalan motivos decorativos vegetales.
keywords: Azulejo de cerámica; escritura zuluz; escritura zuluz otomana;
materials: Arcilla cocida con decoración bajo vidriado.
tags: Arcilla cocida con decoración bajo vidriado.
partner: Museo islámico en la mezquita de Al-Aqsa

fr.name: Carreaux d’un panneau épigraphique en céramique du Dôme du Rocher.
description:
Carreau faisant partie d'un panneau épigraphique qui décorait jadis le pinacle octogonal extérieur du Dôme du Rocher. Le sultan Soliman le Magnifique (r. 926-973 H / 1520-1566 J.-C.) avait commandé ce panneau à l'occasion des travaux de rénovation du Dôme vers 969 H / 1560 J.-C. Chaque carreau mesure 25 x 25 cm et l'ensemble 160 m de long. Il reproduit l'intégralité de la sourate IIIVI, “Ya-sin”. Le texte en style *thoulouth* ottoman blanc sur fond bleu foncé est interrompu par des éléments décoratifs végétaux faits de tiges spiralées, de feuilles et de fleurs entrelacées. Ces carreaux d'une simplicité de traitement caractéristique ont bénéficié d'une mise en couleurs raffinée et d'une exécution très soignée. Ils constituent l'un des premiers exemples de céramique ottomane en architecture et plus spécifiquement dans le Dôme du Rocher. Pendant la période ottomane, les bâtiments étaient souvent carrelés, à tel point que la présence de carreaux est le signe de la contribution ottomane à la restauration des lieux saints, non seulement à Jérusalem mais aussi à La Mecque et à Médine.  
Le Musée islamique a acquis toutes les parties de ce panneau qui ont été prélevées lors des travaux de restauration du Dôme en 1960. Elles faisaient partie de la première phase de l'habillage de céramique des façades extérieures du bâtiment. Auparavant, l'octogone était recouvert d'une mosaïque de verre très détériorée par le temps, et que Soliman fit remplacer par ces carreaux.

Carreau de céramique faisant partie d’un bandeau qui entourait le pinacle octogonal extérieur du Dôme du Rocher. Le sultan Soliman le Magnifique avait fait exécuter ce panneau à l’occasion de la rénovation du Dôme. Le texte en style *thoulouth* blanc sur fond bleu foncé est ponctué d’éléments décoratifs végétaux.
holder: Musée islamique, mosquée al-Aqsa / Haram al-Charif.
keywords: Carreaux en céramique ; écriture thoulouth ; écriture thoulouth ottomane ; décoration végétale ; Ya-sin ; carreaux vernissés

en.name: An Egyptian woman giving a public speech during the events of the 1919 Revolution
short_description: An Egyptian woman talking to the crowds, encouraging them to fight for their rights. The 1919 Revolution – one of the most important Egyptian revolutions in modern times– started due to objections to the practices of the British occupation and the exile of symbols of Egyptian patriotism.

ar.name: دينار (سوليدوس).
description:
يشكل هذا الدينار الذهبي ذو الصناعة المتقنة والجميلة قطعة من بين القطع النقدية الأموية الأولى ومن أكثرها ابتكاراً. ضربت القطعة في إفريقية (تونس الحالية) إبان حكم سليمان ابن عبد الملك، وتنطوي على السمات الأساسية التي سَنَّ والده في مجال سك النقود، والمتمثلة في جعل الدينار عملة رسمية وإلغاء كافة التصويرات الإيقونوغرافية والاستخدام الحصري لفن الخط العربي. وهكذا، تم في المواضع البادية للعيان من العملة – مركز وجه وظهر العملة – وكما كانت تقضي قاعدة ذاك العصر، نقش شهادة العقيدة الإسلامية بأحرف كوفية قديمة :" لا إله إلا الله " و"محمد رسول الله". في حين، وخلافاً للاستخدام المعمول به، كتبت العبارات المنقوشة على المحور الدائري لوجه القطعة وعلى ظهرها بأحرف لاتينية مختصرة على شاكلة العملات البيزنطية المضروبة في إفريقيا؛ فقد تم على محيط الوجه تحديد القيمة النقدية للقطعة ""*Solidus* (دينار)، ومكان ضرب النقد "*Feritus in Africa*" (تم في إفريقيا)، وسنة الإصدار الهجرية "*ِAnno: XCVIII*" (عام 98).  
أما العبارات الدائرية المكتوبة بأحرف لاتينية على ظهر القطعة فتنادي بوحدانية الله:" *In nomini Domini*"" ( باسم الله)، ""*Non Deus Nisi Solus Deus* ( لا إله إلا هو)، " "*Non Deo Socius* (وحده لا شريك له)، مما قد يبرهن على أن إقليم إفريقية لم يكن معربا تماماً خلال تلك الفترة ، وأن هناك شعوبا كانت ماتزال لم تعتنق الديانة الإسلامية، ولاتتحدث إلا باللغة اللاتينية. ومن المرجح أن هذا الوضع أرغم السلطات بالمنطقة، وهم الولاة الذين تم تعيينهم من طرف الأمويين، على سك دنانير عليها عبارات لاتينية - عربية، وعلى استخدام لغة أخرى غير العربية لنشر العقيدة الإسلامية، وبالتالي، جرى استعمال النقود المستخدمة أصلا للتجارة بغرض الدعاية الدينية.

يتبعُ هذا الدينار القواعدَ المؤسسة لضرب النقود الإسلامية: التمثيلات التصويرية محرمة، والشهادة منقوشة بالأحرف العربية؛ لكن احتفظ باللغة اللاتينية من أجل الإشارة إلى قيمة النقد، وتاريخه ووحدانية الله. إن هذه الازدواجية اللغوية المستعملة لأهداف دعائية تشكل أصالة القطعة.
keywords: تجارة؛ دار السكة؛ ديانة ؛ دينار؛ فن الخط؛ كتابة كوفية؛ ذهب مصبوب؛ سكة؛ عملة؛ علم العملة

en.name: *Dinar* (*solidus*).
description: Beautifully made gold *dinar*, which belongs to the first and most original Umayyad coins. Issued in Ifriqiya under the rule of Sulayman (AH 96–99 / AD 715–17), son of 'Abd al-Malik, this coin includes the features that his father established for coining: the introduction of the *dinar* as an official currency, abolition of iconographic representations and an exclusive use of Arabic inscription. Thus, in accordance with contemporary practice, the most noticeable areas of the coin, the centre of the obverse and reverse, are inscribed with the professions of the Islamic faith in archaic *kufic* script: 'La ilaha ill allah' (There is no god but Allah) and 'Muhammad Rassul Allah' (Muhammad is God's prophet). However, contrary to prevailing practice, the circular legends on the obverse and reverse are written in abbreviated Latin characters, as on Byzantine coins from Africa. The obverse rim includes the monetary value, 'Solidus' (*dinar*), the place of striking, 'Feritus in Africa' (made in Africa) and the Hegira year it was struck 'Anno: XCVIII' (year 98). The circular legends in Latin script on the reverse proclaim God's uniqueness, 'In nomine Domini' (In the name of God), 'Non Deus Nisi Solus Deus' (there is no god but the one God), 'Non Deo Socius' (God has no equal). This demonstrates that the province of Ifriqiya was not entirely arabicised in that period. Moreover, there were some parts of its non-Islamised people that spoke only Latin. The authorities, governors named by the Umayyads, were obliged to strike *dinar*s with Latin–Arabic legends and they had to use a language other than Arabic so as to spread the profession of the Islamic faith. Coins, essential for trading, were therefore used for religious propaganda.

This *dinar* follows the rules laid down for Islamic coinage: iconographic representations were forbidden, and the profession of faith is in Arabic, although Latin is used for the value of the coin, its date and the proclamation of the oneness of God. Its originality lies in the way bilingualism is used as propaganda.
holder: Numismatic Museum of the al-Maghreb Bank
keywords: trading; religion; calligraphy; coin; coinage; numismatics

es.name: Dinar (*solidus*).
description:
Este hermoso dinar de oro bien ejecutado se encuentra entre las primeras y más originales monedas omeyas. Emitido en la Ifriqiya de Sulayman, presenta las características en la acuñación introducidas por su padre, Abd al-Malik: institución del dinar como moneda oficial, eliminación de las representaciones iconográficas y empleo exclusivo de la epigrafía árabe.  
Siguiendo la tradición de la época, en las partes más visibles de la moneda –el centro de cada cara– figuran, en caracteres cúficos arcaicos, las profesiones de fe islámica: *La ilaha illa allah* (No hay más dios que Dios) y *Muhammad Rasul Allah* (Mohamed es el Profeta de Dios).  
No obstante, contrariamente al uso en vigor, las leyendas circulares del anverso y del reverso están inscritas en caracteres latinos abreviados, como las monedas bizantinas de África: en el contorno del anverso se indica el valor monetario, *solidus* (dinar), el lugar de acuñación, *Feritus in Africa* (hecho en África) y el año hegiriano de emisión, *Anno XCVIII* (98).  
Las leyendas circulares del reverso proclaman la unidad de Dios en latín: *In nomine Domini* (En nombre de Dios), *Non deus nisi solus Deus* (No hay más dios que el Dios único), *Non Deo Socius* (Dios no tiene semejante). De ello se deduce que, en este período, la provincia de Ifriqiya no estaba completamente arabizada ni islamizada, pues una parte de su población sólo hablaba latín.  
Esta debió ser la razón que obligó a los dirigentes locales, o gobernadores designados por los omeyas, a acuñar dinares con inscripciones latino-árabes y a emplear un idioma diferente al árabe para divulgar la religión musulmana. Un instrumento comercial se convertía así en soporte del proselitismo religioso.

En este dinar se aprecian las normas instauradas para las monedas musulmanas: eliminación de las representaciones iconográficas, inscripción en árabe de la profesión de fe, el latín se mantiene para indicar el valor monetario, la fecha y la unicidad de Dios. En este bilingüismo al servicio de la propaganda religiosa reside la originalidad de la pieza.
holder: Museo Numismático del Banco de Marruecos.
keywords: Comercio; religión; caligrafía; moneda; numismática

fr.name: Dinar (solidus).
description: Ce dinar en or de bonne et belle facture est parmi les premières monnaies omeyyades, et des plus originales. Émise en Ifriqiya sous le règne de Sulayman fils de Abd al-Malik, elle présente les caractéristiques instaurées par son père en matière de monnayage : institution du dinar comme devise officielle, abolition des représentations iconographiques et usage exclusif de l'épigraphie arabe. C'est ainsi qu'aux endroits les plus visibles de la monnaie – le centre de la face et du revers – sont inscrites, comme le voulait la règle de l'époque, les professions de la foi islamique en caractères coufiques archaïques : “*La ilaha illa allah*” (Il n'est d'autre dieu que Dieu) et “*Mohamed Rassoul Allah*”(Mohamed est le Prophète de Dieu). Cependant, contrairement à l'usage en vigueur, les légendes circulaires de la face et du revers sont écrites en caractères latins abrégés, comme sur les monnaies byzantines d'Afrique : sur le pourtour de la face sont précisés la valeur monétaire de la pièce, “*Solidus*” (dinar), le lieu de frappe, “*Feritus in Africa*”(fait en Afrique)et l'année hégirienne d'émission, “*Anno : XCVIII*” (année 98). Les légendes circulaires du revers proclament en caractères latins l'unicité de Dieu : “*In nomine Domini*”(Au nom de Dieu)*,* “*Non Deus Nisi Solus Deus*”(Il n'est de dieu que le Dieu unique),“*Non Deo Socius*”(Dieu n'a pas son pareil).Ce qui prouverait qu'à cette époque la province d'Ifriqiya n'était pas complètement arabisée et qu'il existait encore des populations non islamisées qui ne parlaient que le latin. C'est sans doute ce qui a obligé les autorités des lieux, les gouverneurs nommés par les Omeyyades, à frapper des dinars à légendes latino-arabes et à utiliser une autre langue que l'arabe pour diffuser la profession de foi musulmane. La monnaie, objet utilitaire de commerce, était ainsi exploitée au profit de la propagande religieuse.

Ce dinar suit les règles instaurées pour le monnayage musulman : les représentations iconographiques sont proscrites, la profession de foi est inscrite en arabe, mais le latin est conservé pour indiquer la valeur de la monnaie, sa date et l'unicité de Dieu. Ce bilinguisme utilisé à des fins de propagande fait l'originalité de la pièce.
keywords: commerce ; religion ; calligraphie; numismatique

en.name: Horse adornment used in wedding ceremonies (*Gushnik*)
short_description: A *gushnik* is an article used for the adornment of horses. This item shows the tradition of decorating horses on some festive occasions, particularly on weddings. The decoration consists of a string and numerous ornaments made of *monistra* (tiny beads in varied colours) applied on canvas. The pendants are decorated with varied patterns and have fringes at the bottom.
keywords: Horse ornament; monistra; horse jewellery; accessories; marriage; wedding

en.name: Castle
description: This small fortification was profoundly remodelled in the 14th century and its earlier history is generally ignored by written sources. The castle’s semicircular corner towers, surmounted by conical pinnacles, are extremely eye catching and were clearly built at a later date. The base of these towers is, however, much older and displays typical features of the building systems normally associated with the Emirates period. With the nearby ruins of Alter Pedroso and Cabeço de Vide, this whole area provides suggestive evidence of an important settlement from the earliest days of Islamicisation. Roughly 4 km. away, it is possible to visit the Coudelarias de Alter (Royal Stud), where a breed of horses descending from ancient Andalusian lineage is still bred and maintained.

es.name: Castillo
description: En esta pequeña fortificación, profundamente remodelada en el siglo XIV y cuya historia anterior no figura en las fuentes escritas, lo que llama la atención son las torres de esquina de sección semicircular. Estos torreones, con remate cónico y cimborrio, y de factura claramente posterior, se asientan sobre un basamento de fábrica arcaica, igual que otros sistemas constructivos que se atribuyen a la época del emirato. Con las ruinas cercanas de Alter Pedroso y Cabeço de Vide, esta zona muestra sugestivas pruebas de una población importante en los primeros tiempos de la islamización. A unos 4 km pueden visitarse las Coudelarias de Alter, donde tradicionalmente se cría una raza de caballos emparentada con antiguas estirpes andalusíes.

en.name: Unguentarium
description: This perfume bottle was blown from dark green transparent glass of good quality. It has a slender piriform body two-thirds of total height, a small rim folded out and flattened and a slightly flattened narrow base. Its short tubular neck was tooled at bottom. Part of the rim is broken and missing. The term "unguentarium" is mainly applied to a small vessel that held perfumed oils and cosmetic lotions. These vessels were found in relatively large quantities in the entire Mediterranean, where they were produced between the early Hellenistic and early Medieval periods. The glass unguentarium became popular by the 1st century AD, after the invention of a blowing technique which was originated in the Syro-Palestinian region before the middle of the 1st century BC. Formerly in the collection of Hüseyin Kocabaş.
holder: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum
keywords: Glass; unguentarium; free-blown
partner: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum

ar.name: كتان موشَّى.
description:
نسيج موشَّى، ربما كان يُستخدم إما غطاء للديوان ( أريكة منخفضة ) أو وجهاً لمِفرش صغير أو حجاباً يعلَّق على الباب. يتألف من ثلاثة قطع كتانية خِيطت معاً بشكل طولاني ثم وُشيَّت. أما تشكيل الغصينات المتموجة والأوراق ونبتات الخزامى فمستوحى من أشغال المخمل والبروكار والحرير المنسوج العائد للفترة العثمانية في القرن العاشر - الحادي عشر / السادس عشر- السابع عشر. تعتبر ألوان الخيوط الحريرية الحمراء والخضراء والزرقاء والبنية نمطية خلال تلك المرحلة؛ كما تعتبر الدرزات نظامية الحبكة: ثلاثة خيوط معدودة طولانياً على سطح القطعة الكتانية وخيط واحد من الأسفل. يطغى اللون الأحمر على التشكيل، بحيث أنه يغطي القسم الأعظم من الغصينات ونبتات الخزامى كلّها وبعض الأوراق. استخدم اللون الأزرق على الأوراق والأخضر لتوشية كؤوس الخزامى وبعض الأغصان. أما اللون البني، الباهت في الغالب، فقد استخدم لملء الفراغات بين الألوان جميعها، على شكل لمسات خفيفة وبراعم صغيرة. ينطوي هذا النسيج على حاشية مصممة من نسق أصغر من أزهار الخزامى الحمراء والغصينات الخضر ذات الأوراق الزرقاء، ولمسات خفيفة وبراعم بنية اللون، متعاقبة في ميلانها، تارة نحو اليمين وتارة نحو الشمال.  
كانت التوشية بالحرير في القرن الحادي عشر / السابع عشر تشكِّل خياراً رخيصاً نسبياً بالنسبة لأولئك الذين يرغبون في التنعُّم بالأنسجة المترفة، نظراً لأن المنسوجات الحريرية كانت أغلى بكثير. من الصعب أحياناً التمييز بين القطع الموشَّاة في المنزل على يد النساء وتلك التي صنعها الرجال في الورشات من أجل التجارة. يدل نموذج التوشية هذا على أنه صُنع بشكل مهني، وكاحتمال أرجح، في مشغل، لأن النموذج وثيق الصلة بتصاميم مشابهة اكتشفت على أشغال المخمل في القرن العاشر- الحادي عشر /السادس عشر- السابع عشر.

هذه القطعة الكتانية المُطرَّزة بخيوط حريرية ملوِّنة نافرة، ربما كانت تستخدم غطاءً لديوان، أو وجهَ لحاف، أو ستارة معلقة لباب. كان الحصول على مثل هذه القطع المُطرَّزة بسخاء، والمتأثِّرة بالمخامل، أيسر من اقتناء الأقمشة الحريرية الخالصة.
keywords: أثاث منزلي؛  تجارة؛ زخرفة نباتية.

en.name: Embroidered linen.
description:
An embroidered textile thought to have served either as a cover for a divan (low sofa seat); a quilt facing; or as a hanging such as a curtain for a door. It is made up of three vertical lengths of linen sewn together and embroidered. The composition of wavy stems, leaves and tulips is inspired by AH 10th- and 11th- / AD 16th- and 17th-century Ottoman velvets, brocades and woven silks. The silk-thread colours of red, green, blue and yellow are typical of the time; the stitch used is a regular darning stitch with the length of four counted threads over the linen, and one under it. Red dominates the composition, covering most of the stems, all of the tulips, and some of the leaves. The blue is used on the leaves and the green is used to embroider the bases of the tulips and some of the stems. The yellow, which has largely faded, is used to fill in some of the gaps between all the other colours in the shapes of strokes and small buds. This textile has a border designed with a row of smaller red tulips and green stems with blue leaves, and yellow strokes and buds which alternate in their leaning, bending once to the right and once to the left.  
  
Silk embroidery of the AH 11th / AD 17th century was a cheaper option for those who wanted to enjoy sumptuous textiles, given that woven-silk fabrics were much more expensive. It is sometimes difficult to distinguish between embroideries made by women at home and those worked by men in workshops for the trade. The pattern on this embroidery indicates that it was most probably made professionally in a workshop, because the pattern relates strongly to similar designs found on AH 10th- and 11th- / AD 16th- and 17th-century velvets.

This boldly embroidered linen textile with coloured silk threads may have been used as a cover for a divan, a quilt facing, or a hanging such as a curtain for a doorway. Lavishly embroidered pieces that are influenced by velvets, like this one, were relatively more affordable than woven-silk fabrics.
keywords: Domestic furnishing; floral decoration; commerce
materials: Linen embroidered with coloured silk threads.
tags: Linen embroidered with coloured silk threads.

es.name: Lino bordado.
description:
Tejido bordado que probablemente sirvió para cubrir un diván, como funda de edredón o para colgar como cortina de una puerta. Está formado por tres piezas verticales de lino cosidas y bordadas con una composición de tallos ondulantes, hojas y tulipanes inspirada en los terciopelos, brocados y sedas otomanos de los siglos X-XI / XVI-XVII. Los colores de los hilos de seda son típicos de este periodo: rojo, verde, azul y amarillo; con puntadas regulares de cuatro hilos de largas por encima del lino y uno por debajo. Domina la composición el color rojo, utilizado en la mayoría de los tallos, en todos los tulipanes y en algunas hojas; el azul se emplea para las hojas; el verde, para bordar el arranque de los tulipanes y algunos de los tallos; finalmente, el amarillo, muy desteñido en la actualidad, para rellenar los huecos entre los demás colores con trazos y pequeños capullos. Forma el borde una hilera de tulipanes rojos más pequeños y tallos verdes con hojas azules; lo completan trazos y capullos amarillos de inclinación alterna, una vez hacia la derecha y otra hacia la izquierda.  
Los bordados con hilos de seda del siglo XI / XVII eran una opción más barata que las telas de seda para aquellos que gustaban de los tejidos suntuosos. A veces es difícil distinguir entre los bordados hechos por las mujeres en sus casas y los fabricados por hombres en talleres para el comercio. La factura de este bordado indica que probablemente se realizó en un taller, ya que la composición es muy similar a las de terciopelos de los siglos X-XI / XVI-XVII.

Tejido de lino llamativamente bordado con hilos de seda de colores que probablemente sirvió para cubrir un diván, como funda de edredón o para colgar como cortina de una puerta. Tejidos como este, magníficamente bordados e inspirados en los terciopelos, eran económicamente más asequibles que las telas de seda.
dates: Siglo XI de la Hégira / XVII d. C.
keywords: mobiliario doméstico; decoración floral; comercio
materials: Lino bordado con hilos de seda de colores.
tags: Lino bordado con hilos de seda de colores.

fr.name: Panneau de lin brodée.
description:
Textile brodé qui a pu servir de couverture de divan, de housse d'édredon ou de rideau de porte. Il se compose de trois bandes verticales de lin cousues et brodées. La composition de tiges sinueuses, de feuilles et de tulipes s'inspire des velours, brocards et tissages de soie ottomans des Xe-XIe siècles H (XVIe-XVIIe siècles J.-C.). Les couleurs des fils de soie rouges, verts, bleus et jaunes sont typiques de l'époque. Le point utilisé est un point de reprise à quatre fils par-dessus et un par-dessous. La couleur rouge, appliquée à la plupart des tiges, à toutes les tulipes et à certaines feuilles, domine la composition. Le bleu est utilisé pour les feuilles et le vert pour le pied des tulipes et certaines tiges. Le jaune, en grande partie passé, remplit certains vides entre les autres couleurs et dessine des brins et de petits bourgeons. La bordure est constituée d'une rangée de tulipes rouges plus petites à tiges vertes et feuilles bleues, et de traits et bourgeons jaunes à l'inclinaison alternée, se courbant une fois à droite, une fois à gauche.  
La broderie de soie du XIe/XVIIe siècle était une production économique destinée aux amateurs de textiles somptueux qui ne pouvaient s'offrir des tissus de soie beaucoup plus coûteux. Il est parfois difficile de distinguer entre les broderies faites par des femmes à la maison et celles d'hommes employés dans des ateliers commerciaux. Le motif de cette broderie montre qu'il est probablement de confection professionnelle, car il se rapproche beaucoup de ceux de velours des Xe-XIe siècles H (XVIe-XVIIe siècles J.-C.).

Ce tissu de lin vigoureusement brodé de fils de soie colorée a pu servir de couverture de divan, de housse d’édredon ou de rideau de porte. Les pièces somptueusement brodées qui sont influencées par les velours, comme celle-ci, étaient relativement plus abordables que les étoffes tissées de soie.
dates: XIe siècle de l’Hégire (XVIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: objets domestiques ; décoration florale ; commerce
materials: Lin brodé de fils de soie de couleur.
tags: Lin brodé de fils de soie de couleur.

en.name: *Medjmouaï teçavir* (Collection de costumes)
short_description: Popular postcard from Turkey showing the costume worn by various people, according to occupation, activity, etc. At this time Turkish financial officials worked under European management.
keywords: costume; diplomacy; fashion; court life; economy; finance; Ottoman; Tercüman; travel; traveller; Orientalism

en.name: Madrasa al-‘Adiliyya
description:
One of Nur al-Din later monuments, this *madrasa* was founded in 568/1172 but its construction was interrupted by Nur al-Din’s death in 569/1174. It was not until the reign of the Ayyubid al-Malik al-‘Adil in 592/1196 that construction was resumed and finally completed by Al- ‘Adil’s son, al-Malik al-Mu‘azzam, who spent a further four years preparing the mausoleum for his father and instating a *waqf* or endowment for the upkeep of the *madrasa* in perpetuity. By 620/1223 it was finally complete. It is one of the best surviving examples of an Ayyubid madrasa in Damascus, made of large and perfectly measured blocks of stone.  
The portal is unique in Ayyubid architecture, flaunting skilled stone carving that betrays a strong northern influence, probably the work of Aleppine architects. There is a frame of bracketed stone moulding around the entry, and rows of *ablaq* stone blocks. The overhanging vault is decorated with a pair of square-based *muqarnas* domes hidden behind a hanging pendant keystone and tri-lobed arches.  
The entrance leads through a cross-vaulted vestibule similar to that of Madrasa Nur al-Din, into an immense central courtyard with a newly restored fountain. The northern *iwan* to the left features a barrelvaulted ceiling. Straight ahead is a narrow *iwan* flanked by four cells used as student accommodation. A long prayer-hall with five entry bays and a central *mihrab* is accessible to the right. The northwestern corner features a small chamber made of large limestone blocks, a socalled *khalwa* used as a place for meditation or prayer in seclusion. Dominating the south-eastern corner of the  
*madrasa* is al-Malik al-‘Adil’s grand mausoleum. The mausoleum is a spacious domed chamber with a pair of windows overlooking each side of the street corner in order to invite the blessings of passers-by. Aleppine architectural techniques can be seen in the usage of squinches which carry the dome, as opposed to the local style of using load-bearing drums.

cs.name: Schodiště
description: Kamenné samonosné schodiště zdobí skulptury andílků držících jednotlivé složky rodového znaku a prezentujících alegorie smyslů. Kartuše ve výplni parapetu obsahují výjevy z Vergiliovy Aeneidy. Monumentální schodišťovou halu uzavírá freska s výjevem Představení trojského koně Odysseem. Vstupní prostor prezentuje rod jako ochránce křesťanství a podporovatele umění.
artist: Johann Christian Pröbstl, Josef Tadeáš Rotter (1701 Opava – 1763 Brno)

en.name: Staircase
description: The stone cantilever staircase is decorated with sculptures of *putti* holding components of the family's coat of arms and representing allegories of the Senses. Cartouches in the parapet feature scenes from Virgil's *Aeneid*. The monumental staircase hall closes with a fresco of Odysseus presenting the Trojan horse. The entrance space portrays the family as protectors of Christianity and patrons of the arts.
artist: Johann Christian Pröbstl, Josef Tadeáš Rotter (1701 Opava – 1763 Brno)

en.name: Dress
short_description: This dress of al-Druze (Druse) women is made of a long grey with green and silver brocade, pursed narrow sleeves, wide, open square shaped chest, pursed at the middle and wide at the bottom with ruffles and a cotton liner. This object illustrates the variegated social composition and demographic changes in the Jordanian territory in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. The al-Druze tribes migrated from Syria (Hawran) to north east Jordan in the early twentieth century because of their support for the Syrian revolution against the French occupation. The traditional Druse and other Jordanian costumes were influenced by the local trade and economic activities: as illustrated in this case, they were often made of silk textiles, produced in Syria and traded to Jordan and Palestine.
holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
keywords: Brocade dress; ruffles; cotton liner
materials: Silk, cotton; hand woven Syrian silk fabric (brocade)
partner: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery

en.name: Madrasa al-Muqaddamiyya
description: Muhammad Ibn al-Muqaddam, a Kurdish military commander in the service of Nur al-Din, patronised the construction of Madrasa al-Muqaddamiyya in 563/1168. Only the portal and parts of the mosque, particularly the *mihrab*, remain of the original construction, making it difficult to determine the original plan. The portal, an outstanding example of northern Syrian stonework and capped by a cross vault, is framed by a tri-lobed arch. The *mihrab*, which is located in the middle of a typical tripartite sanctuary, is in fact the earliest of a long tradition of marblereveted *mihrabs* in Syria. Two freestanding columns with simplified Corinthian capitals support a slightly pointed arch, flanked by a simple knot design made of overlapping stone-courses in different colours. A wide continuous moulding frames the columns and separates the niche of the *mihrab* from its hemispherical conch.

en.name: Sidi Jomni Madrasa
description:
Founded by the Muradites in the 11th–12th/end of the 17th century, the Sidi Jomni Madrasa is one of those rare institutions created in Jerba by central government. The purpose of it, within the framework of a political system based on a centralisation of power, was to spread the Malekite cult, the sect to which the majority of the country’s population subscribed. This politic was pursued and consolidated during the Husaynite era through the construction of the Mausoleum of Shaykh Ibrahim al-Jomni in 1133/1721, and the various other religious foundations built on his behalf.  
A monument more or less urban in look, it comprises a *madrasa* surrounded by all the buildings from which it once gained a revenue: a *hammam*, two bread ovens and three *funduq*s. The *madrasa* opens out onto the south-east and is composed of ground-and first floors. Through a rectangular hallway, one reaches a square courtyard onto which on one side opens the prayer hall, and on the remaining three sides there is a gallery sheltering the entrance doors to the students' rooms. A staircase runs from the courtyard to the gallery on the first floor, where there is another row of rooms. The ceilings of the galleries rest on arcades and pillars, and rainwater-pipe drains are incorporated into the walls. The oratory, square in plan, is modest in size, without a minaret, like the classic Jerbian mosques; a simple external staircase was used, from which to announce the hour of prayer. The interior is covered by four vaults supported by arches and pillars; the wall of the *qibla* consists of two *mihrab*s that bear witness to an extension carried out later.  
The Sidi Jomni Mausoleum occupies the north-eastern corner of the building and is marked on the outside by its dome covered in varnished green tiles. The square room, with its eye-pleasing dimensions, is covered by a superb dome built of cylindrical ceramic shapes; it is supported, thanks to a circular base, by three arches cut from local stone, and the whole rests on four second-hand marble columns surmounted by Corinthian capitals featuring three levels of sculpted and pierced acanthus leaves. The transition from square to circle was made possible with the aid of four corner squinches in the form of fluted scallops, framed by three circumscribed arches made of cut stone. Between every squinch, square windows light the room, each of which is flanked by small columns surmounted by Hafsid capitals. The dome has been carefully decorated with motifs engraved into stucco, representative of cypresses and rosaries. This monument demonstrates the introduction of architectural elements which until then had been foreign to the island – the closed courtyard, the upper floor, as well as the decoration, which was quite sought-after – without excluding, however, the presence of local imprints, visible in the isolation of the prayer hall and in the shape of the arches.

es.name: Medersa Sidi Yomni
description:
Fundada por los muradíes entre los siglos XI-XII/f. XVII, la *medersa yomniya* es una de las más curiosas instituciones creadas por el poder central en Yerba. La intención era, dentro del marco de una política de centralización del poder, difundir el rito malikí, seguido por la mayoría de la población del país. Esta política fue seguida y consolidada en época husseyní con la construcción del mausoleo del jeque Ibrahim el-Yomni en el año 1133/1721 y a través de las diferentes fundaciones piadosas hechas en su beneficio.  
Monumento más bien urbano, comprende la *medersa*, rodeada de todos los edificios de los cuales obtenía beneficios, ya sea el *hammam*, dos hornos de pan y tres *funduq*s. La *medersa* se abre hacia el Sudeste y comprende la planta baja y la primera planta. A través de un vestíbulo rectangular se accede a un patio cuadrado sobre el cual se abre, a su vez, la sala de oración y el *kuttab* sobre un lado. Sobre los otros tres lados corta una galería donde se encuentra la entrada de las celdas de los estudiantes. Una escalera que parte desde el patio desemboca en una galería en el piso elevado, sobre la cual se abre otra serie de celdas. La cobertura de las galerías reposa sobre arcadas y pilares. Las conducciones de aguas pluviales están integradas en los muros. De plano cuadrado, el oratorio es de modestas dimensiones, sin alminar, como las mezquitas clásicas de Yerba. Una escalera simple exterior sirve para llamar a la oración. El interior está cubierto por cuatro bóvedas sostenidas por arcos y pilares; el muro de la *qibla* comprende dos *mihrab*s que testimonian la existencia de una ampliación más tardía.  
El mausoleo de Sidi Yomni ocupa el rincón noreste del edificio y está señalado en el exterior por su cúpula, cubierta con tejas vidriadas verdes. La sala cuadrada, de bellas dimensiones, está rematada por una soberbia cúpula, construida a base de piezas cilíndricas de cerámica. Se soporta, gracias a una base circular, por cuatro arcos tallados en la piedra. El conjunto reposa sobre cuatro columnas reutilizadas de mármol y coronadas con capiteles corintios en tres niveles, con hojas de acanto esculpidas y caladas. El paso del cuadrado al cilindro se ha efectuado aquí con la ayuda de cuatro trompas de ángulo en forma de concha acanalada, enmarcadas por tres arcos circunscritos en piedra tallada. Entre las conchas, se abren unas ventanas cuadradas que den luz a la sala, flanqueadas con columnas coronadas por capiteles hafsíes. La cúpula está ciudadosamente decorada con motivos grabados en estuco, que representan cipreses y rosas. Este monumento muestra la introducción de elementos arquitectónicos extranjeros en la isla, como son el patio cerrado, el primer piso y su rebuscada decoración. Tampoco se puede excluir la presencia de la marca local, perceptible en el aislamiento de la sala de oración y la forma de los arcos.

fr.name: Médersa Sidi Jomni
description:
Fondée par les Mouradites au XIe-XIIe/f. XVIIe siècle, la médersa Joumniya est l’une des rares institutions créées par le pouvoir central à Jerba. L’objectif était, dans le cadre d’une politique de centralisation du pouvoir, de répandre le rite malékite, rite de la majorité de la population du pays. Cette politique fut poursuivie et consolidée à l’époque husseinite par la construction du mausolée du cheikh Ibrahim el-Jomni en 1133/1721 et par les différentes fondations pieuses à son profit.  
Monument d’allure plutôt citadine, il comprend la médersa entourée de tous les édifices dont elle tirait jadis les revenus: un hammam, deux fours à pain et trois fondouk. La médersa ouvre sur le sud-est et comprend un rez-de-chaussée et un étage. Par un vestibule rectangulaire, on accède à une cour carrée sur laquelle ouvre la salle de prière sur un côté, sur les trois autres côtés une galerie abritant l’entrée des cellules des étudiants. Un escalier qui part de la cour aboutit à la galerie de l’étage sur laquelle ouvre une autre série de cellules. La couverture des galeries repose sur des arcades et des piliers, les conduites des eaux pluviales sont intégrées dans les murs. De plan carré, l’oratoire est de dimensions modestes, sans minaret, telles les mosquées jerbiennes classiques; un simple escalier extérieur servait à l’annonce des heures de prière. L’intérieur est couvert de quatre voûtes portées par des arcs et des piliers; le mur de la *qibla* comprend deux *mihrab*s qui témoignent d’une extension plus tardive.  
Le mausolée de Sidi Jomni occupe le coin nord-est du bâtiment et il est signalé à l’extérieur par son dôme couvert de tuiles vernissées vertes. La salle carrée, de belles dimensions, est couverte d’une superbe coupole construite en poteries cylindriques; elle est portée, grâce à une base circulaire, par quatre arcs taillés dans la pierre locale, l’ensemble repose sur quatre colonnes en marbre de réemploi, surmontées de chapiteaux corinthiens à trois niveaux de feuilles d’acanthe sculptées et ajourées. Le passage du carré au cercle a été effectué à l’aide de quatre trompes d’angle en forme de coquilles cannelées, encadrées de trois arcs circonscrits en pierres taillées. Entre les coquilles, des fenêtres carrées éclairent la salle, elles sont flanquées chacune de colonnettes surmontées de chapiteaux hafsides. La coupole est soigneusement décorée de motifs gravés sur stuc, représentant des cyprès et des rosaces. Ce monument montre l’introduction d’éléments architecturaux étrangers à l’île: la cour fermée, l’étage, ainsi que la décoration assez recherchée mais sans exclure la présence de la marque locale perceptible dans l’isolement de la salle de prière et la forme des arcs.

en.name: Castle
description:
The Castle was built in the reign of D. Dinis in 1304; and the extremely well documented construction was the work of João Simão.  
Besides the *enceinte* that sheltered the early settlement, it also had a house for the *alcaide*, or governor, during the Manueline era when it was regularly used, and it has remained largely the same up to the present time.The keep was remodelled after 1485, when work was also carried out to adapt the curtain walls next to the gateways, most notably the one around the parade ground, which was given wide crenellations.

de.name: Chorfenster
description: Zur Auszeichnung des Chors gestaltete Kleinhans hier an den Seitenwänden dreiteilige geschweifte Fenster in der Art Dominikus Zimmermanns. Das Fenster wird als Ornament in der Fläche eingesetzt, die ursprüngliche Form des antiken dreiteiligen Thermenfensters wird völlig aufgelöst und überspielt. Da die übrigen Fenster nur einfache Rundbogenform aufweise, fällt der Kontrast im Chor besonders deutlich aus.

en.name: Choir window
description: For the decoration of the choir Kleinhans designed three-part curved windows in the style of Dominikus Zimmermann set into the side walls. The window functions as an ornamental feature, the original form of the antique thermal window is deconstructed and enhanced. As the remaining windows are only in the form of semi-circular arches, the contrasting character of the choir is especially marked.

en.name: Transport plan of Beirut
short_description: This map shows a plan of transport terminals in Beirut in 1891.
keywords: Transportation; Trade; Tracks

en.name: Diadem
description: Joaquin Sorolla travelled with his family to Tetouan in February 1919; there they bought all types of souvenirs of that exotic lands. Thanks to this travel the Sorolla Museum keep a small collection of Berber jewellery. Among the highlights is this headband or diadem, jewellery that represents the typical combination of silver and multiple enamel colours. It would look placed on the front of a woman and is complemented with bracelets, earrings, pins and necklaces, of which the Museum has also other pieces.
keywords: North Africa; Silver; Costume; Souvenir

ar.name: إناء يعرف باسم
description:
إناء قاعدته حلقية الشكل، سطحه الداخلي إنسيابي، حوافه منفرجة قليلاُ. صورت على الإناء شخصية أنثوية بشكل جانبي، عينها لوزية وجاحظة جداً تشغل أعلى الوجه. تتسم شفتها المكتنزة وأنفها بدقة رسمهما؛ وينتهي شعرها الطويل والمعقود بجدائل منسدلة بضفائر تصل حتى الركبتين. ترتدي هذه المرأة الواقفة زياً من قماش تزينه الحواشي ومخطط باللون البني. وتحمل هذه الشخصية بيدها كأساً وبالأخرى غصناً لوردة مرسومة بأسلوب فني طبيعي، وتحيط بها أربع وردات مجردة لها شكل مروحة. كما يوجد على جانبيها إطاران زخرفيان، يحتوي كل واحد منهما على نقيشة كتابية يرجح أن تكون عبارة "المٌلك".  
أخذ الخزف الإفريقي (التونسي) يولي أفضلية خاصة للتصويرات الحية، والتي كانت تنم عن تأثير رافدي أكيد، وذلك بعد قيام دولة الفاطميين، ويرجح أن يكون لهذا الأمر صلة بالمذهب الشيعي، الأكثر تسامحاً تجاه التصويرات الإنسانية من مذهب الامتثاليين المالكيين.  
يتميز الوجه بوجود عين كبيرة الحجم، ويشكل هذا الجانب عاملاً مشتركاً بين كافة التصويرات الحية الإفريقية (التونسية) في ذالك العصر تقريباً، سواء أكانت منحوتة او مقولبة أو مرسومة. ويبدو أن جذورها ضاربة في الماضي الإفريقي السحيق. وبالمقابل، يبقى طراز ثوب سيدة صبرة طرازا رائجاً منذ العصر الأموي، وقد بقي مستمرا طوال الفترة العباسية في منطقة بلاد الرافدين.
يمثل هذا الصحن ذو القاعدة الحلقية واللون الأخضر منظرا جانبيا لشخصية أنثوية؛ يتميز الوجه بتواجد عين لوزية وفم لحيم وأنف رقيق جدا؛ وتذكر الصورة الجانبية بالأشكال الإفريقية (التونسية).
dates: النصف الثاني من القرن 4 الهجري/القرن 10 الميلادي.
place: عثر عليها خلال تنقيبات في موقع صبرة المنصورية التي كانت تتوفر على ورشات للخزفيات أو في القيروان.
keywords: زخرفة تصويرية؛ امرأة؛ خزف  مطلي بالمينا؛ زيريّ.

en.name: The ‘Lady of Sabra’ plate.
description:
Round-based plate. It has a low, upstanding rim, slightly curved and sloping outwards. On the plate is drawn a female figure in profile with a large almond-shaped eye. The full mouth and the delicate nose are very finely drawn.  
The long hair starts in a pony-tail and ends in plaits hanging down to the knees. The figure is standing, wearing a brown-striped dress covered in fringes. She holds a glass in one hand and in the other a flower drawn in a naturalistic manner. The figure is surrounded by four stylised, fan-shaped flowers and by two rectangular shapes each containing a eulogy, probably ‘al-Mulk’ (Sovereignty).  
As from the advent of the Fatimids, Ifriqiyan ceramics began to show a preference for the figurative, showing a definite Mesopotamian influence. This trend is undoubtedly connected with the attitude of Shi'ite dogma towards the representation of the human form, more tolerant than that of the Malikite conformists.  
The face, with its huge eyes, is a common denominator of almost all human Ifriqiyan figures of the period, whether carved, modelled or painted, and seems to go back to a distant, Roman, North African past. By contrast, the style of the Lady of Sabra's dress had been in fashion since the Umayyad era and lasted right through the Abbasid period.

This green bowl has a round base and depicts a female silhouette. The face is identified by an almond-shaped eye, a full mouth and an extremely fine nose. The profile is reminiscent of Ifriqiyan figures.
dates: Hegira, second half of the 4th century / AD 10th century.
place: Kairouan or Sabra al-Mansuriyya, which both had potteries.
keywords: Figurative decoration; women; Zirid; figurative representation

es.name: Cuenco llamado “Dama de Sabra”.
description:
En este cuenco de base anular, pared curva y bordes levemente acampanados figura un perfil femenino. Un ojo almendrado y muy prominente invade la parte superior del rostro; la boca carnosa y la nariz resaltan por su delicado trazado. La larga cabellera atada en una cola de caballo termina en unas trenzas que caen hasta las rodillas. De pie y vestida con un atuendo de rayas marrones y cubierto de flecos, la dama lleva una copa en una mano y, en la otra, la rama de una flor dibujada con gran naturalismo. Cuatro flores estilizadas en forma de abanico lucen a su alrededor. Dos cartuchos con la inscripción de un elogio, probablemente *al-Mulk* (‘la soberanía, el poder’) se exhiben a cada lado del personaje.  
Con la llegada de los fatimíes, la cerámica ifriqí empezó a desarrollar un interés especial por las representaciones animadas, lo que evidencia una incuestionable inspiración mesopotámica. Ello se debe a que el dogma shií era más tolerante respecto a las representaciones humanas que los conformistas malikíes.  
En el rostro destaca la presencia de un ojo sobredimensionado. Esta característica, cuyo origen bien pudiera remontarse a un lejano pasado africano, constituye un denominador común en la mayor parte de las representaciones animadas ifriqíes de la época, tanto esculpidas como modeladas o pintadas. En cambio, el estilo del vestido de la dama de Sabra estaba en boga desde la época omeya, y perduró en Mesopotamia durante el periodo abbasí.

En este cuenco, de base anular y color verde, puede verse el perfil de una representación femenina que recuerda el de figuras de Ifriqiya. El rostro destaca por la presencia de un ojo almendrado, una boca carnosa y una nariz extremadamente fina.
dates: Segunda mitad del siglo IV de la Hégira / X d. C.
place: Kairuán o Sabra al-Mansuriya, que contaban con talleres de alfarería.
keywords: Decoración figurativa; mujeres; zirí

fr.name: Coupe dite “dame de Sabra”.
description: Coupe à base annulaire et à paroi carénée ; les bords sont légèrement évasés. Sur la coupe figure un personnage féminin de profil ; l'œil en amande et très globuleux occupe le haut du visage, la bouche charnue et le nez se distinguent par la finesse de leur tracé. Les longs cheveux en queue de cheval se terminent par des tresses descendant jusqu'aux genoux. La femme debout est vêtue d'un costume en tissu à rayures brunes et couvert de franges. Le personnage tenant d'une main un verre et de l'autre la branche d'une fleur dessinée avec un certain naturalisme est entouré de quatre fleurs stylisées en éventail et flanqué de deux cartouches comportant chacun une eulogie, probablement “al-Mulk” (la souveraineté). Dès l'avènement des Fatimides, et sans doute en rapport avec le dogme chiite, plus tolérant à l'égard des représentations humaines que les conformistes malékites, la céramique ifriqiyenne commençait à vouer une prédilection particulière aux figures animées dénotant une influence mésopotamienne certaine. Le visage se distingue par la présence d'un œil surdimensionné. Cet aspect constitue un dénominateur commun entre presque toutes les représentations animées ifriqiyennes de l'époque, qu'elles soient sculptées, modelées ou peintes, et semble plonger ses racines dans un lointain passé africain. En revanche, le style de la robe de la dame de Sabra était en vogue dès l'époque omeyyade, et perdure en Mésopotamie tout au long de la période abbasside.

Cette coupe à base annulaire et de couleur verte représente le profil d'une silhouette féminine. Le visage se distingue par la présence d'un œil en amande, une bouche charnue et un nez extrêmement fin. Le profil rappelle les figures ifriqiyennes.
dates: seconde moitié du IVe siècle de l’Hégire (Xe siècle J.-C.).
place: Kairouan ou Sabra al-Mansuriyya qui disposaient d’ateliers de poterie.
keywords: Décoration figurative; femmes; zirides
partner: Musée des arts islamiques de Kairouan

en.name: Palazzo Miti Zagnoni Raffi
description: The three houses core of the future residence before 1648 developed in the usual way with their front on the via Emilia; they had wells and gardens and they were probably on several levels. Rifurbishing the building took to a complete rearrengment of spaces. Was added a monumental staircase, the small central court was made into an icehouse and on the first floor was built an hall of honour with a great fireplace. Some traces of the fifteenth-century buildings are visible: an archway, some pictorical decorations. They are good quality decorations testifing of the good economical position of the former owners of the house, the Dal Pero Sassatelli. The senteenth-eighteenth-century refurbishing took to a complete redecoration of the interiors: fireplaces, overdoors and three fresco ceilings on the first floor commissioned to the Rolli brothers around 1680. In the first room the central scene depicts “Dawn expelling Night”, in the second one is represented the “Glory of the Miti family” while in the third one there is a sleeping female figure and a quotation from the Song of Songs. The façade, the last work made at the beginning of the eigthteenth-century in order to complete the remodelling of the three building into one residence, was made by the architects Lorenzo and Cosimo Mattoni from Como, who built in Imola many churches and residences.

This building is among the most significant residences in Imola; it stands on the via Emilia, a few meters from the main square. The palace was remodelled from 1648, when it was purhcased by the Miti family; the works were finished around 1722. The palace was built over three houses dating to the fifteenth-century. Today it houses the Confederazione Generale del Lavoro (CGIL); it is possible to visit it. The first floor was decorated at the end of the seventeenth-century by the Bolognese brothers Rolli, with scenes celebrating the Miti family.
history: Tommaso was the first of this family of landowners to move to Imola at the end of the sixteenth century. Fabrizio Miti, canon of the cathedral of Imola, bought in 1648 from countess Vittoria Dal Pero Sassatelli three adjoning houses on the via Emilia, for 7000 scudi. From that date to 1722, when Diamante Miti marries Giorgio Zagnoni, the Mitis worked to unite the three houses and finally unifing them with an imposing façade on the Via Emilia. The palace was inherited in 1722 by the Zagnoni family who sold it in 1794 to the brothers Andrea and Giuseppe Raffi, from a rich family of Faenza. After many trasfers of property the building was bought in 1978 by a trade union (CGIL) to house its offices.
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: Palazzo Miti Zagnoni Raffi
description: Le tre case nucleo della futura residenza prima del 1648 si svilupparono con la fronte sulla via Emilia; avevano pozzi e giardini ed erano probabilmente su più piani. La ristrutturazione dell'immobile costrinse ad un totale riallestimento degli spazi. Si aggiunse uno scalone monumentale, il cortile centrale fu trasformato in ghiacciaia e al primo piano fu costruito un salone d'onore con un grande camino. Sopravvivono alcune tracce degli edifici del XV secolo: un portico e alcune decorazioni pittoriche.  Sono decorazioni di una certa qualità che attestano la buona posizione economica dei precedenti proprietari delle case, i Dal Pero Sassatelli. La ristrutturazione del XVII secolo portò ad una completa ridecorazione degli ambienti: camini, sovapporte e tre soffitti affrescati al primo piano furono commissionati ai fratelli Rolli attorno al 1680. Nella prima sala la scena centrale rappresenta *L'Alba che scaccia la Notte*, nella seconda è rappresentata la *Gloria della famiglia Miti,* mentre nella terza è dipinta una figura femminile con una citazione dal *Cantico dei Cantici*. La facciata, l'ultima opera eseguita alla fine del XVIII secolo per completare la ristrutturazione dei tre edifici in uno solo, fu eseguita dagli architetti Lorenzo e Cosimo Mattoni da Como, che costruirono ad Imola molte chiese e palazzi.

Questo edificio è uno dei palazzi più significativi di Imola; si trova sulla via Emilia, a pochi metri dalla piazza principale della città. Fu ristrutturato a partire dal 1648, quando venne acquistato dalla famiglia Miti; i lavori terminarono attorno al 1722. Il palazzo fu costruito su tre case precedenti, risalenti al XV secolo. Oggi è sede della Confederazione Generale del Lavoro (CGIL); è possibile visitarlo. Il primo piano fu decorato alla fine del XVII secolo con scene che celebrano la famiglia Miti da due pittori bolognesi, i fratelli Rolli.
history: Tommaso fu il primo della sua famiglia di proprietari terrieri a trasferirsi Imola, alla fine del XVI secolo. Fabrizio Miti, canonico della cattedrale di Imola, acquistò nel 1648 dalla contessa Vittoria Dal Pero Sassatelli tre case adiacenti sulla  via Emilia, per la somma di 7000 scudi. Da allora fino al 1722, quando Diamante Miti sposò Giorgio Zagnoni, i Miti cercarono di unire le tre case e finalmente le unificarono con una imponente facciata sulla Via Emilia. Il palazzo fu ereditato nel 1722 dalla famiglia  Zagnoni che lo vendette nel 1794 ai fratelli Andrea e Giuseppe Raffi, membri di una ricca famiglia di Faenza. Dopo vari passaggi di proprietà l'edificio fu acquistato nel 1978 da un'organizzazione  sindacale (CGIL) per ospitare i propri uffici.

en.name: Water Carrier’s Portable Water Jug
short_description: This large ovoid ewer consists of a metal top and ceramic base. From the hemispherical shoulder rises a tall, waisted cylindrical neck with central collar. The mouth is covered by a bulbous, domical lid. The ewer has a strong, angular handle of roughly square section and a tall, obliquely rising body spout, which is connected to the neck by a curved tube and tapers towards the prominent, slightly waisted mouth section. The entire upper part of the ewer is decorated with incised horizontal bands of plaiting, abstract floral decoration, pseudo-inscriptions and running animals. The spout shows a dense system of punched, arched lines and incised decorative bands near its base. The undecorated ceramic base of the ewer is secured by netting created from fibre ropes. Thicker ropes of the same material, probably used for carrying the ewer, are attached. A ewer identical to this one appears in Ludwig Deutsch’s painting of the Al-Azhar mosque (SH_66).
type: Copper alloy and ceramic water ewer with fibre rope netting
holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department
dates: Hegira late 13th – early 14th century / AD late 19th – early 20th century
materials: Engraved and punched sheet copper alloy; ceramic base; fibre rope

ar.name: شمعدان
description: الشمعدان ذو شكل الجرس والبروفيل المقعر يشير للمعيار العالي للمشغولات المعدنية التي وصل إليها الحرفيون المسلمون. والتزيين المزخرف بالفضة الدمشقية يتألف من 11 شخصا في وضعيات مختلفة الذين يحملون أدوات عديدة تمثل الأعمال الموسمية.
dates: القرن السابع الهجري / القرن الثالث عشر الميلادي
keywords: شمعدان ، دمشقي
partner: متحف الفنون الشرقية (مؤسسة المتاحف في تورينو)

en.name: Candlestick
description: The candlestick with its bell-shaped, concave profile is indicative of the high standard of metalworking reached by Islamic craftsmen. The decoration, embellished by silver damascening, consists of 11 figures in different poses holding various instruments representing seasonal tasks.
keywords: Candlestick; damascened
partner: Museum of Oriental Art (Fondazione Torino Musei)

it.name: Candelabro
description: Il candelabro con corpo campiforme e porfilo concavo, testimonia l'alto livello raggiunto dagli artigiani islamici nella lavorazione dei metalli. La decorazione, impreziosita dall'ageminatura in argento, è costituita da undici personaggi in differenti atteggiamenti, rappresentanti i lavori dei mesi.
keywords: Candelabro; bronzo; incisione; ageminatura; calligrafia
partner: MAO Museo d'Arte Orientrale (Fondazione Torino Musei)

en.name: *Botijo* (*càntir*)
description:
Inverted piriform, blown glass *botijo* (pitcher) with spiral moulding. Decorated with strands of crimped glass. Conical, near vertical neck and spout, with vertical, ring-shaped handle of circular cross-section, topped with a bird-shaped ornament.  
  
The *botijo* (càntir in Catalan) is a vessel for holding and drinking water. Along with the *porrón* (porró) and the *almorraja* (almorratxa), it is one of most typical Catalonian glass forms. High quality glass was made in Catalonia “a la façon de Venise” until the 17th century. Paste quality deteriorated beginning in the 18th century and glass became more folkish in nature. Throughout its evolution, the formal imagination exploded, allowing for a plethora of adornments applied to the surfaces of these pieces.
keywords: Blown glass; folk style; Catalonia

es.name: Botijo (*càntir*)
description:
Botijo con depósito piriforme invertido, de vidrio soplado con moldeado helicoidal. Decorado con cordones de vidrio rizado. Gollete y vertedor cónicos casi verticales y asa anular vertical de sección circular rematada con un apéndice en forma de ave.  
  
El botijo (càntir en catalán) es un recipiente para contener y consumir agua. Constituye, junto con el porrón (porró) y la almorraja (almorratxa), una de las formas más características de los vidrios catalanes. En Cataluña se realizó vidrio de gran calidad “a la façon de Venise” hasta el siglo XVII. A partir del siglo XVIII tiende a empeorar la calidad de las pastas y el vidrio asume un carácter popular. En su evolución, la fantasía de las formas se dispara, admitiendo gran número de accesorios aplicados a la superficie.
keywords: Vidrio soplado; popular; Cataluña
materials: Vidrio soplado; marcado en molde, pinzado

en.name: Langenthal vase
description: The amphora-shaped flower vase was produced in the porcelain factory of Langenthal (Canton of Bern) founded in 1906. The vase featuring large, stylized flowers with an Asian touch was hand-painted in 1924 by Fernand Renfer, the company’s artistic director. Its modernistic look is inspired by the style called Art Deco which spread from France in the wake of the famous Parisian Exposition internationale des Arts décoratifs et industriels modernes. Renfer’s entry into the Langenthal factory in 1920 marked the beginning of an extremely creative phase in the 1920s and 1930s with an output of top-quality and aesthetically highly appealing ware. During the same period the enterprise also joined the design association Swiss Werkbund and regularly employed artists as designers. The vase was part of a major private collection of early Langenthal porcelain, which the Swiss National Museum was able to acquire in 2007.
keywords: vase; amphora shape; porcelain; Porcelain Factory Langenthal; painted

de.name: Kath. Pfarrkirche St. Michael in Berg am Laim, ehem. Kurkölnische Erzbruderschafts-, Ritterordens- und Hofkirche
names: St. Michael in Berg am Laim
description: Idealkonzepten des Schloss- und Klosterbaus folgt das mittige Einfügen des Kirchenbaus zwischen die beiden symmetrischen Flügelbauten der Josephsburg. Schon die pompöse doppeltürmige und konvex vorgewölbte Fassade signalisiert höfischen Anspruch. Das dezent mit noblem Stuck verzierte Innere ist als szenographische Abfolge von vier Teilräumen konzipiert: Auf ein Vestibül folgen zwei in der Größe abnehmende, dafür im Gliederungsaufwand gesteigerte Zentralräume, wovon der Mitgliederzahl und Standeshierarchie gemäß der grössere der Erzbruderschaft und der kleinere, mit Säulenpomp und Hoforatorien versehene dem Ritterorden zugedacht ist; den Abschluß des Raumprospekts bildet ein als Säulenbaldachin gestaltetes queroblonges Presbyterium. Eine ähnliche Steigerung im architektonischen Aufwand beherrscht auch die Altarausstattung. Cuvilliés d.Ä. sind die eigenwilligen flachen Rundgewölbe zu verdanken, die im Erzbruderschaftsraum vor den Obergadenfenstern schirmartig die vier kapriziösen Nebenaltäre überfangen und dadurch gemeinsam mit den Pilasterpfeilern den Mangel an Kapellenraum und Säulenarchitektur kompensieren.

Schon von weitem kündet die pompöse Doppelturmfassade vom einstmals hohen Rang der Michaelskirche in Berg am Laim, indem Sie nicht nur dem Kölner Kurfürsten und Erzbischof Clemens August als Hofkirche, sondern auch einem adeligen Ritterorden als Ordenskirche diente. Das Innere prägt eine eindrucksvolle, von Johann Michael Fischer gestaltete Raumszenographie gepaart mit einer höfisch noblen Ausstattung im Rokokostil, geschaffen von den seinerzeit besten Münchner Kräften: Stuck und Fresken von Johann Baptist Zimmermann (1680-1758) sowie Altäre von Johann Baptist Straub (1704-1784).
artist: Kurfürst Clemens August, Erzbischof von Köln (reg. 1723-1761)

Architektur der Doppelturmfassade: Philipp Jakob Köglsperger (geb. 1707)  
Architektur des Kircheninneren: Johann Michael Fischer (1691-1766);  
Architektonische und künstlerische Beratung, Entwurf zur Stuckierung: François de Cuvilliés d.Ä. (1695-1768)  
Stuck und Deckenfresken: Johann Baptist Zimmermann (1680-1758)  
Altäre: Johann Baptist Straub (1704-1784)  
Hochaltarblatt: Andreas Wolf (1652-1716)
history: Der aus dem Haus Wittelsbach stammende Kölner Kurfürst und Erzbischof Clemens August besaß in Berg am Laim nahe der kurbayerischen Residenzstadt München ein kleines Schloss namens Josephsburg, um bei seiner in Bayern regierenden Verwandtschaft standesgemäß residieren zu können. An der Schlosskapelle bestand seit 1693 eine St. Michaels-Erzbruderschaft, die rasch angewachsen war, so dass Clemens August sich entschloss, ihr eine grössere „Haupt- und Mutterkirche“ zu errichten; außerdem gründete er einen adeligen Ritterorden. Nach der Grundsteinlegung am 7. Oktober 1738 war zunächst der Münchner Hofmaurerpolier Philipp Jakob Köglsperger mit dem Bau betraut, der die Grundmauern legte und die Fassade begann, danach plante der berühmte bürgerliche Baumeister Johann Michael Fischer das Innere der Kirche im aufgehenden Mauerwerk neu. Als Bauinspektor fungierte zudem der kurbayerische Hofarchitekt François de Cuvilliés d.Ä., um für ein höfisches Ambiente zu sorgen.
keywords: Bruderschaftskirche; Hofkirche; Hochaltar; Rokoko-Skulptur; Deckenmalerei

en.name: Catholic Parish Church St. Michael in Berg am Laim, formerly Electorate of Cologne Archbrotherhood-, Order of Knights- and Court Church
names: St. Michael in Berg am Laim
Court church of the Prince Elector of Cologne and his Knight’s Order St. Michael
description: The central insertion of the church building between the two symmetrical wings of Josephsburg castle follows ideal concepts of palace  and monastery construction. Even the ostentatious double-towered and bulging façade signalises courtly aspirations. The interior, discretely decorated with noble stucco, is conceptualised as a scenographical sequence of four partial spaces : two centralised ones of decreasing size, but with an increasing number of sections follow a vestibule. Intended for use according to the number of members and hierarchy level, the larger served the archbrotherhood while the smaller one, decorated pompously with columns and provided with court oratories, served the order of knights. A transverse oblong presbytery designed as a columned canopy forms the completion of the interior backdrop. A similar increase in architectural effort also dominates the altar features. Cuvilliés the Elder is to thank for the individualistic flat round vaults in the archbrotherhood room which, in front of the clerestory windows, serve like umbrellas as canopies for the four side altars. In this way, together with the pilaster pillars, they compensate for the lack of chapel space and columned architecture.

Even from afar, the ostentatious double-towered façade bears witness to the once high rank of St. Michael’s Church in Berg am Laim. It served not only as Court Church for the Cologne Elector and Archbishop Clemens August, but also as an Order Church for a noble order of knights. The interior is characterised by an impressive scenography of space designed by Johann Michael Fischer paired with courtly and noble furnishings created by Munich’s top talent of the time: stucco and frescoes by Johann Baptist Zimmermann (1680–1758) and altars by Johann Baptist Straub (1704–84).
type: Ecclesiastical Architecture (Court-, Brotherhood- and Order of Knights Church)
artist: Elector Clemens August, Archbishop of Cologne (gov. 1723–61)
history: In Berg am Laim, near the Electorate of Bavaria’s capital of Munich, Cologne Elector and Archbishop Clemens August of the house Wittelsbach owned a small castle called Josephsburg. This allowed him the ability to reside according to his social status with his relatives ruling in Bavaria. At the castle chapel, an archbrotherhood of St. Michael had existed since 1693 and grew so quickly that Clemens August decided to erect for it a larger “Main- and Mother Church”. Furthermore, he founded a noble order of knights. After the laying of the foundation stone on 7 October 1738, court masonry foreman  (Hofmaurerpolier ) Phillip Jakob Köglsperger from Munich was tasked with the construction. He laid the foundation walls and began the façade, after which the famous bourgeois architect Johann Michael Fischer redesigned the church interior together with its above-ground walls. Bavarian court architect François de Cuvilliés the Elder served as building inspector in order to ensure a courtly ambience.
partner: University of Munich, Institute of Art History

en.name: La Gare de Hidjaz, Damas (The Hijaz Station, Damascus)
description: The Hijaz Railway Station was designed by the Spanish architect Fernando de Aranda (1878–1969). Raised at the Ottoman court in Istanbul, where his father directed the Imperial Military Band, Aranda settled permanently in Damascus following the deposition of Sultan Abdülhamid II in 1909. The station was designed within the broader Hijaz Railway project directed by Heinrich August Meissner Pasha (1862–1940), the German civil engineer and Chief Engineer of the Hijaz Railway. Although Aranda never obtained formal architectural qualifications and could not officially sign his projects, he became one of Damascus's most influential architects, designing the Hijaz Railway Station alongside numerous public and private buildings that shaped the city's early twentieth-century urban landscape.
keywords: Hijaz Railway; Damascus; railway station; Travel; Transport

en.name: Portrait of 'Abd Allah al-Bustani
short_description: 'Abd Allah al-Bustani was born in Debbeye (al-Chouf district) in December 1854, and studied at the National School of Butrus al-Bustani until 1873. He first started teaching in the villages of 'Abeyh and Damur, and then moved to Cyprus, where he published a newspaper. He later returned to Lebanon and taught at the Sagesse College for ten years, and then at the Patriarchal College for 14 years. He wrote many plays, of which only one survives today. His most notable work, however, was the dictionary "al-Bustan". He died in February 1930.

en.name: Hermitage of the Camaldolese Order
description:
The hermitage has a rectangular layout and consists of 17 monk's cells, a U-shaped *foresteria* and the original church tower. The complex is surrounded by a wall; there are two smaller gates to the west and a central gate decorated with vases and the coat of arms of the Monte Corona Congregation. An inscription on the keystone of the middle gate reads “1746”. The monk's cells are arranged in three rows along a longitudinal axis; the façade of each cell is decorated with the coat of arms of its founders. The cells also have a uniform layout consisting of four rooms: a living room, house chapel, workshop and pantry and a garden. The east wing of the convent building, emphasised with an ornate gate, is a floor higher than the two side wings. The north wing used to house the library, while the renowned refectory was situated in the south wing. The refectory is topped by three vaults and holds several captivating wall paintings of scenes such as the *Last Supper* (by Gergely Vogl), the *Life of Saint Romuald*, and the figures of Hungarian saints placed in between stately stuccoes, which were presumably modelled on Pilgram's drawings.  
Only the tower has survived from the original Church of St. John of Nepomuk, the young Pilgram's masterpiece; the murals of which are associated with Franz Anton Maulbertsch. After King Joseph II dissolved the Camaldolese order in 1782, several precious pieces of furniture and ornaments disappeared from the church, some of them taken to other churches. For example, the vestry furniture and *lavabo* with baldachin, made by János György Mes, were taken to the parish church of Tata, and the choir pews, made by Franz Xaver Seegen, are found today in the Greek Catholic Church in Komárom.

Hungarian hermitages, established in the 17th and 18th centuries (in Zomborhegy, Lánzsér (Landsee) and Lehnic, Majk) belong to the Congregation of Monte Corona, a branch of the monastic order the Camaldolese (Kamalduli), which was established by St. Romuald in the 11th century. Those involved in the foundation of the hermitage in Majk were László Radossányi, who by then had been the head of a hermitage in Kahlenberg since 1731, and Count József Esterházy of Galánta. The former encouraged the foundation of the monastery while the latter donated his land in Majkpuszta to the order in 1733. The building complex, which is surrounded by a wall, still stands and comprises 17 monk's cells. The convent building and the Church of St. John of Nepomuk represent life as it was for the 'silent monks' in Central Europe.
artist: Count József Esterházy (1682–1748); László Radossányi (?–1764); József Hartvig; Baron János Hunyadi; Countess Erdődy Józsefné, née Erzsébet Berényi; László Szörényi (1709–1752); Count Zsigmond Berényi; Baranyay family of Bodorfalva; Count Ferenc Gyulai; Borbála Falusi; József Cziráky; Lajos Lengyel; Count Imre Esterházy; Count Ferenc Esterházy (1715–1785); Count János Esterházy; Ottó Egkh

Architectural design: Franz Anton Pilgram (1699–1761); Painters: Franz Anton Maulbertsch (1724–1796), Gergely Vogl, Franz Xaver Seegen; sculptors: Károly (Karl) Bebó (1712–1779), Lajos Gode and his assistant Franciscus Arcularius, József Sartory, Bechert József, Mes János György; gate: Lipót Toll
history:
In 1733 Count József Esterházy donated his land at Majkpuszta to the Camaldolese order. Franz Anton Pilgram was commissioned to design the building complex according to the standards of the order. The first hermitage was finished in 1736, and by 1770, 17 monk's cells were completed. The convent was built between 1746 and 1752, and the foundation stone of the church was laid in 1753. The wall surrounding the hermitage was completed in 1756. Several renowned masters were involved in the decoration of the building complex. The murals in the refectory of the *foresteria* (convent building) are associated with Gergely Vogl, and the drawings for the stuccoes are by Pilgram. The murals, now destroyed, were painted by “Dominus Maulpercs Viennensis” alias Franz Anton Maulbertsch. Károly Bebó carved the altar of St. John of Nepomuk in the vestry between 1760 and 1763. Other sculptural decorations were created by Lipót Toll (the gates), and the “three sculptors from Pozsony (Bratislava)”: Lajos Gode, his disciple, Franciscus arcularius (furniture of the chapter house and of the vestry), and József Sartory (sculptures and, stone vases); Franz Xaveer Seegen (the pews); János György Mes (*lavabo*); József Bechert (coat-of-arms of the hermitage cells commissioned by the Esterházy-family).  
Today the hermitage is managed by the National Trust of Monuments for Hungary.
keywords: Religious orders, Camaldolese order, monastery, library, church, Franz Anton Pilgram, Franz Anton Maulbertsch, Gergely Vogl, Franz Xaver Seegen, Károly Bebó, Lajos Gode, Franciscus, József Sartory, József Bechert, János György Mes, Lipót Toll, Count József Esterházy, László Radossányi, József Hartvig, Baron János Hunyadi, Countess Erdődy Józsefné Erzsébet Berényi, László Szörényi, Count Zsigmond Berényi, Baranyay family of Bodorfalva; Count Ferenc Gyulai, Borbála Falusi, József Cziráky, Lajos Lengyel, Count Imre Esterházy, Count Ferenc Esterházy, Count János Esterházy, Majk

ar.name: مولانا شمس الدين محمد عصار التبريزي، مهر ومشتري (ملحمة رومانسية عن صداقة الأمير مهر مع الشاب مشتري)
description: أتمّ مولانا شمس الدين محمد عَسّار التبريزي (تاريخ. 784هـ / 1382–1383م) هذه الملحمة الرومانسية التي تتناول صداقة الأمير مِهر والفتى مُشتري (مِهر ومُشتري) سنة 778هـ / 1377م. وقد اقتُنيت هذه المخطوطة لصالح المكتبة الوطنية النمساوية سنة 1677م في القسطنطينية على يد بيتر لامبك مقابل 30 دوقية ذهبية و15 كروزر. ونُسخت المخطوطة بخط النستعليق على يد الناسخ هداية الله نحو 977–988هـ / 1570–1580م، ويُرجَّح أنه أُنجز في شيراز، إيران. وبحسب المؤرخ التركي في القرن السادس عشر مصطفى عالي، فإن هداية الله كان من أصفهان، وتتلمذ على يد الخطاط معزّ الدين محمد أمين من كاشان. وتحمل أربعة مخطوطات أخرى مزوّدة بمنمنمات، أُنتجت بين 1564 و1584م، توقيعه. ومن الناحية الأسلوبية، يمكن ربط اللوحات الثماني كاملة الصفحة بالإنتاج الفني لمدينة شيراز، حيث يُرجَّح أن المخطوطات أُنجزت بين 1570 و1580م. ويزداد ترجيح تأريخه إلى أواخر القرن السادس عشر عند الفحص الدقيق للتراكيب التصويرية في مجمل المخطوطة؛ من حيث تحوير المناظر الطبيعية والأشكال المعمارية، ومنظومة الألوان، والظهور المحدود لتاج الحيدري (التاج الصفوي/العمامة ذات العصا) الذي خرج من حيّز الاستخدام خلال هذه الفترة.
artist: شمس الدين بن غياث الدين الحافظ الكرماني
keywords: ملحمة; معراج; لوحة; رومانسية; الصفويون
materials: حبر، ألوان مائية معتمة وذهب على الورق. خط  نستعليق مزخرف. 14 سطرًا في الصفحة الواحدة.
