en.name: Church of the Virgin
description:
This church shows two different stages of building. The first began on 1st April 1356, at the beginning of the frontier war with Castile, when the Prior of the Holy Sepulchre in Calatayud was Fray Domingo Martínez de Algaraví and his commander in Tobed was Fray Juan Domingo. In this first stage, the chancel and the first two sections of the nave were built. The work must have been finished three years later, since on 3rd June 1359 the Archbishop of Saragossa, don Lope Fernández de Luna, gave his arbitral verdict against the pretensions of the Episcopal jurisdiction of Tarazona in favour of the Priors of the Holy Sepulchre of Calatayud. The sentence adjudicated to the latter the ownership of the church built in Tobed and the altars built in its sanctuary in honour of the Virgin, St John the Baptist and St Mary Magdalen and the corresponding income from them.  
The last part of the foot of the church was built in the second stage, which was started in 1394, the year when Pope Benedict XIII was elected, and his arms decorate the keystone of the vault in this section and the ceiling of the upper choir. From the formal characteristics of this last part, it can be supposed that Mahoma Rami was the master craftsman. The chronology of this last part is corroborated by the information that on 8th August 1385 the Canons of the Holy Sepulchre of Calatayud decided to dedicate all the income and donations from the sanctuary of Tobed to the finishing of the building, since “*the work is not yet completed in its building*”.  
The church’s magnificent west façade and end wall was hidden partially until 1984 by the Town Hall building, which adjoined it. The present state of the façade, which is comparable in its decoration of brick and applied ceramics only to the exterior wall of the *parroquieta* of San Miguel in the Seo in Saragossa, is the result of the restoration begun in 1985 by the architect Úrsula Heredia.  
The Church of the Virgin in Tobed is the best example of the architectonic model of the fortified church in Aragon. The building has one single nave with a rectangular chancel and triple chapels at the head. The nave has three sections, all covered with simple ribbed vaulting, alternating with other shorter spans, which are covered with pointed barrel vaulting and counterbalanced on the outside by buttress towers. Between these at ground level, the side chapels, three on each side of the nave, are covered with pointed barrel vaulting. Above the side chapels and the three chapels at the head of the chancel is a gallery or tribune that opens to the outside through pointed arcades to form a passage similar to a military parapet, which is accessible from the interior of the church through the buttress towers.  
Structurally speaking, this is a very solid building, perfectly reinforced both lengthwise and crosswise by the pointed barrel vaulting, which is linked together by the buttressing towers. The interior area has a unity that conserves the original Mudéjar decoration. This, seen in the painted brick design and the painting on the walls, in the vaulting and plasterwork on the windows and *oculos* – not forgetting the decorated wood of the keystones of the vaults and that of the *alfarje*, or flat wooden ceiling of the upper choir, at the end of the nave. With this profusion of ornamental elements, an effect is achieved of Mudéjar interior space that has altered very little over the years.  
This same spatial effect can be perceived in the other Mudéjar interiors in this itinerary.  
From the outside, in contrast to the decorative interior, the building has a compact and unornamented appearance – except for the west façade, built in the second phase as we saw above, when the war with Castile had already been forgotten – which gives it an extreme military air. This military appearance is emphasised by the buttress towers, four on each side of the nave, and by the open passageway with pointed arches between the towers, like a parapet or sentry walkway, which, from the outside, appears more appropriate for a fortress than for a church.  
To judge from the successful spread of this model throughout the whole of Aragon, represented so magnificently in the Church in Tobed, and which will be found throughout the itinerary, it was seen as a satisfactory way to solve the technical and functional problems of architecture at the time.

es.name: Iglesia de la Virgen
description:
La fábrica de esta iglesia corresponde a dos etapas constructivas. La primera se inicia el 1 de abril de 1356, al comienzo de la guerra fronteriza con Castilla, siendo prior del Santo Sepulcro en Calatayud Fray Domingo Martínez de Algaraví y su comendador en Tobed Fray Juan Domingo. En esta primera etapa se edificaron el presbiterio y los dos primeros tramos de la nave. La obra debió concluir tres años después, ya que el 3 de junio de 1359 el arzobispo de Zaragoza don Lope Fernández de Luna dictó una sentencia arbitral contra las pretensiones de la jurisdicción episcopal de Tarazona y a favor de los priores del Santo Sepulcro de Calatayud. La sentencia adjudicaba a estos la propiedad de la iglesia edificada en Tobed y los altares construidos en las capillas de su cabecera en honor de la Virgen, San Juan Bautista y Santa María Magdalena, así como las rentas correspondientes.  
El último tramo de los pies se construyó en una segunda etapa, a partir de 1394, año de la elección del pontífice Benedicto XIII, cuyas armas decoran la clave de la bóveda de este tramo y la techumbre del coro alto.A juzgar por las características formales de este último tramo, se puede pensar que Mahoma Rami fue el maestro de obras. La cronología de este último tramo está corroborada también por la noticia de que el 8 de agosto de 1385 los canónigos del Santo Sepulcro de Calatayud decidieron adscribir todas las rentas y donaciones del santuario de Tobed al perfeccionamiento de su fábrica, que “no era acabada la de obrar”.  
La magnífica fachada occidental de la iglesia, que cierra este tramo, permaneció semioculta hasta el año 1984 por el edificio de la Casa Consistorial, que se había adosado a la misma. El estado actual de la fachada, solo comparable por su decoración en ladrillo y cerámica aplicada al muro exterior de la parroquieta de San Miguel en la Seo de Zaragoza, es resultado de la restauración efectuada a partir de 1985 por la arquitecta Úrsula Heredia.  
El santuario de la Virgen en Tobed constituye el máximo ejemplo del modelo arquitectónico de iglesia-fortaleza en Aragón. Se trata de una fábrica de nave única, con el presbiterio rectangular y triple capilla en la cabecera. La nave consta de tres tramos que van cubiertos con bóveda de crucería sencilla y alternan con otros tramos más cortos, cubiertos con cañón apuntado y contrarrestados al exterior por torres-contrafuerte. Entre estas se alojan en planta baja las capillas laterales, tres a cada lado de la nave, cubiertas con bóveda de cañón apuntado. Por encima de las capillas laterales y de las tres capillas del presbiterio discurre una galería o tribuna que se abre al exterior mediante arquerías apuntadas, un ándito a modo de adarve militar al que se accede desde el interior de la iglesia a través de las torres-contrafuerte.  
Estructuralmente es un edificio muy sólido, que queda perfectamente trabado tanto en sentido longitudinal como transversal por las bóvedas de cañón apuntado que atan las torres-contrafuerte. El interior es espacio unitario, que conserva la decoración original mudéjar, tanto la agramilada y pintada de muros y bóvedas como la labrada de las yeserías de ventanas y óculos, sin olvidar la madera decorada de las claves de las bóvedas y la del *alfarje* o techumbre plana del coro alto, a los pies de la nave. Con esta profusión de elementos ornamentales se consigue un efecto de espacio interior mudéjar que ha sido poco alterado a lo largo del tiempo. Este mismo efecto espacial puede percibirse en otros varios interiores mudéjares del recorrido.  
En contraste, desde el exterior la fábrica ofrece un volumen compacto y desornamentado—si exceptuamos la fachada occidental, levantada en una segunda etapa, como se ha dicho, cuando la guerra de frontera con Castilla estaba ya olvidada—, que le da un aspecto muy militar. Este aire castrense es acentuado por las torres-contrafuerte, cuatro a cada lado de la nave, y por la tribuna abierta en arcos apuntados que hay entre las torres, a modo de adarve o paseador militar, cuyo aspecto externo es más propio de fortaleza que de iglesia.  
A juzgar por su éxito y por la difusión que tuvo en todo el territorio aragonés, el modelo representado con tanta magnificencia por la iglesia de Tobed, con el que volveremos a encontrarnos a lo largo del recorrido, supo resolver de un modo satisfactorio los problemas técnicos y funcionales de la arquitectura de la época.

ar.name: الزاوية المحمدية.
description:
تتكون الزاوية من قسمين: الأول عبارة عن قبو مستطيل بُني تحت الأرض، ويضم صخرة طبيعية غير منتظمة الشكل؛ والقسم الثاني عبارة عن غرفة مستطيلة المسقط بُنيت على مستوى سطح الأرض، ويغطيها قبة ضحلة كبيرة تستند على أربعة عقود مدببة. ويبلغ طول الغرفة 8.10 م وعرضها 6.90 م. وتبلغ سماكة جدران المبنى حوالي 90 سم. تقع أرضية الغرفة على مستوى أرضية سطح قبة الصخرة، وفُرشت ببلاط حجري مصقول كبير الحجم، يبلغ حجم بعضه حوالي 44 سم × 1.44 سم. ومبنى الزاوية مستقل، له أربع واجهات ظاهرة غير محجوبة. وبُنيت جدرانه وواجهاته من الحجر الأبيض متنوع الحجم، يبلغ حجم بعض قطعه حوالي 30 سم × 20 سم.  
الواجهة الشرقية هي واجهة المبنى الرئيسية، وتطل على قبة الصخرة المشرفة، ويبلغ طول هذه الواجهة 9.90 م وارتفاعها 4 م. فُتح في هذه الواجهة باب عرضه 94 سم وارتفاعه 1.83 سم يؤدّي إلى داخل الزاوية. ويعلو هذا الباب عتب حجري يقع على ارتفاع مدماك واحد منه لوحة كتابية تأسيسية ورد فيها تاريخ إعادة بناء الزاوية. وعلى ارتفاع أربعة مداميك حجرية من قمة هذه اللوحة، تنتهي مداميك الواجهة الشرقية وكذلك الواجهات الثلاثة الأخرى، بدون إطار أو كورنيش كما هو مألوف. تقع قبة المبنى الضحلة مباشرة فوق السطح، وغطي كل من القبة والسطح ببلاط حجري صغير، وتوّجت القبة بهلال حجري قصير.  
تتميز عمارة هذه الزاوية بالبساطة وقلة الزخرفة، وهي تعبير صادق عن عمارة القرن 12/18التي سادت في مدينة القدس.

تقع الزاوية المحمدية على بعد بضعة أمتار شمال غرب قبة الصخرة، وتتكوَّن من قبو مستطيل، بُني تحت الأرض، وغرفة مستطيلة المسقط، بُنيت على مستوى سطح قبة الصخرة، وتعلوها قبة ضحلة كبيرة، تستند على أربعة عقود مدببة، ويعلوها هلال حجري. تتميز عمارة هذه الزاوية بالبساطة، وقلّة الزخرفة، وهي تعبير صادق عن عمارة القرن 12 الهجري/18 الميلادي، التي سادت في مدينة القدس. بُنيت على الأغلب كخلوة لرجال الحكم، والشخصيات الهامة، التي أرادت مجاورة المسجد الأقصى، والاعتكاف فيه.
artist: رعى البناء محمد باشا، وهو والي القدس.  وقد أعاد بناء الزاوية في عام 1112/ 1701 بعد اندثار قبة كانت تقع في الموقع وتحمل اسم
keywords: زاوية؛ قبة، قبة الشيخ محمد الخليلي؛ مسجد النبي.

en.name: Zawiya al-Muhammadiyya.
description:
The *zawiya* is composed of two sections: a rectangular barrel-vaulted hall built underground (a basement) in which there is a vault built of natural rock of an uneven shape. The second section is a room that is rectangular in design, and which is built at ground level of the Dome of the Rock. This room is covered by a large shallow dome that is supported by four tapered arches. The room measures 8.10 m x 6.90 m, and the walls are around 90 cm thick. It is paved with large well dressed stones, each of which is around 44 cm x 1.44 cm. The *zawiya* is detached and has four facades. The interior walls are built of white stones of various sizes, some of which are about 30 cm x 20 cm.  
The eastern, principle façade overlooks the Dome of the Rock. It is 9.90 m long and 4 m high, and accommodates an entrance portal of 94 cm wide and 1.83 cm high. The portal leads into the interior of the *zawiya*. The entrance is topped by a stone lintel that is located at the height of a single stone course. A panel inscription appears above the lintel, stating the date the *zawiya* was restored. At the height of four stone courses from the apex of this panel, the stone course belonging to the eastern façade ends, as do the other three facades. The shallow dome of the building is located directly on top of the building, without a drum. The entire dome and the surface are covered with small stone tiles, and the dome is crowned by a small stone crescent.  
The *zawiya* is distinctive for its simplicity and lack of ornamentation. It is typical of the architecture of AH 12th- / AD 18th-century Jerusalem.

The *zawiya* is located several metres northwest of the Dome of the Rock. It is composed of a rectangular vaulted room built underground and a rectangular room built at the ground level of the Dome of the Rock. It is topped by a large shallow dome that is supported by four pointed arches and surmounted by a stone crescent. The architecture of this *zawiya* is distinguished by its simplicity and lack of decoration. It is an expression of the prevailing architectural style that dominated Jerusalem in the AH 12th / AD 18th century. It was probably built as a place of seclusion for men in governance.
artist: Muhammad Pasha, governor of Jerusalem, sponsored the building. The zawiya was rebuilt in AH 1112 / AD 1701 after the mausoleum including its dome (*qubba*), which bore the name “al-Hadi al-Amin”, an allusion to the Prophet Muhammad, was destroyed. This site is also connected to Sheikh Muhammad al-Khalili – indeed another name for the building is Qubbat al-Sheikh Muhammad al-Khalili – who was a scholar and ‘ulama, and a Sufi of Jerusalem in the AH 12th / AD 18th century.
keywords: Zawiya; dome

es.name: Zawiya al-Muhammadiyya.
description:
La *zawiya* se compone de dos partes: una sala rectangular subterránea con una bóveda de cañón construida con piedra natural de forma irregular, y una sala rectangular construida a la altura de la planta baja de la Cúpula de la Roca. Esta sala está cubierta por una gran cúpula no muy profunda que descansa sobre cuatro arcos. Mide 8,10 × 6,90 m de ancho, sus muros tienen unos 90 cm de grosor y está pavimentada con piedras cuidadosamente cortadas de 44 × 1,44 cm. La *zawiya* es un edificio independiente con cuatro fachadas; las paredes interiores están construidas con piedras blancas de distintos tamaños, algunas de ellas de 30 × 20 cm. La fachada principal es la oriental, que da a la Cúpula de la Roca; mide 9,90 m de largo y 4 m de alto y alberga una puerta de entrada a la *zawiya* de 94 cm de ancho y 1,83 m de alto. La entrada está rematada con un dintel de piedra que alcanza la altura de una sola hilera de sillares; encima del dintel se aprecia un panel con una inscripción que indica la fecha de restauración de la *zawiya*. La altura total de esta fachada, al igual que la de las otras tres, alcanza cuatro hileras de sillares por encima del panel. La cúpula que corona el edificio carece de tambor y está decorada con pequeñas losas de piedra; en la cúspide presenta un pequeña media luna de piedra.  
Esta *zawiya* se caracteriza por su sencillez y ausencia de decoración. Es un ejemplo típico de la arquitectura jerosolomitana del siglo XII / XVIII.

Esta *zawiya* se encuentra a unos metros al norte de la Cúpula de la Roca. Consta de dos salas rectangulares: una subterránea, cubierta con una bóveda; otra al nivel del suelo, cubierta con una gran cúpula poco pronunciada que reposa sobre cuatro arcos apuntados y que está rematada con una media luna de piedra. La arquitectura de esta *zawiya* se caracteriza por su sencillez y por la ausencia de decoración. Refleja el estilo arquitectónico de la Jerusalén del siglo XII / XVIII. Probablemente la usaron los gobernantes como lugar de retiro.
artist: Muhammad Paşa, gobernador de Jerusalén. La *zawiya* fue restaurada en 1112 / 1701, después de la destrucción de su cúpula, que se llamaba Al-Hadi al-Amin en alusión al profeta Muhammad (Mahoma). Este edificio también está relacionado con el *shayj* Muhammad al-Jalili, erudito, ulema y sufí de Jerusalén del siglo XII / XVIII.
keywords: Zawiya; cúpula.

fr.name: Zawiya al-Muhammadiyya.
description:
Cette *zawiya* à quatre façades se compose de deux parties. La première est une salle rectangulaire souterraine à voûte en berceau, dans laquelle se trouve également une voûte irrégulière creusée dans le roc, la seconde une salle rectangulaire, au niveau du rez-de-chaussée du Dôme du Rocher. De 8,10 x 6,90 m de surface, elle est recouverte d'une importante coupole soutenue par quatre arcs brisés. Ses murs en pierres blanches de diverses dimensions (20 x 30 cm pour certaines) mesurent 90 cm d'épaisseur. Elle est pavée de dalles en pierre soigneusement taillées, d'environ 44 x 144 cm chacune.  
La façade principale à l'est donne sur le Dôme du Rocher. Elle mesure 9,90 m de long sur 4 m de haut et possède une porte d'entrée de 1,83 cm de haut et 94 cm de large, surmontée d'un linteau de pierre de hauteur équivalente à celle des pierres qui l'entoure. Au-dessus, légèrement en creux, un panneau épigraphié donne la date de la restauration du bâtiment. La façade s'arrête quatre lits de pierre plus haut. La coupole entièrement recouverte de petites tuiles de pierre est directement posée sur la toiture, sans tambour. à son sommet s'élève un petit croissant en pierre.  
Cette *zawiya* est remarquable par sa simplicité et l'absence de toute ornementation. Elle est caractéristique de l'architecture de la Jérusalem du XIIe siècle H (XVIIIe siècle J.-C.).

Cette *zawiya* est située à quelques mètres au nord-ouest du Dôme du Rocher. Elle se compose d’une salle rectangulaire voûtée creusée dans le roc et d’une seconde salle rectangulaire au niveau du rez-de-chaussée du Dôme du Rocher. Elle est recouverte d’une importante coupole soutenue par quatre arcs brisés et surmontée d’un croissant de pierre. L’architecture de cette *zawiya* est remarquable par sa simplicité et l’absence de toute ornementation. Elle est représentative de l’architecture de la Jérusalem du XIIe siècle H (XVIIIe siècle J.-C.). Elle fut probablement construite comme lieu de retraite pour les dirigeants.
artist: Muhammad Pacha, gouverneur de Jérusalem, a commandité la construction de ce bâtiment, qui fut reconstruit en 1112 H / 1701 J.-C. après la destruction d’une qubba qui se trouvait à cet emplacement et qui portait le nom de “al-Hadi al-Amin”, une allusion au prophète Mohammad. Le lieu est également lié au cheikh Muhammad al-Khalili, l’un des érudits, oulémas et soufis de Jérusalem au XIIe siècle H (XVIIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Zawiya ; dômes

ar.name: بلاط كايومارس ، صفحة من الشهنامة (كتاب الملوك) لشاه طهماسب
description: إن شعر الفردوسي الملحي (الشهنامة /كتاب الملوك) اكتمل في عام 1010 وهو يسرد تاريخ كل الشاهات الإيرانيين (الملوك) حتى الغزو العربي لبلاد فارس في عام 642 ميلادي و اتباع البلاد للإسلام. وإن جزءا كبيرا من  الشعر يركز على الملوك الأسطوريين قبل التاريخ وبعضهم حكموا لمئات السنين وأسسوا المعرفة البشرية بكل شيء من النار إلى الحياكة. ووفقا للفردوسي فإن الفكرة الدقيقة للملك نشأت مع الملك كايومارس الذي حكم لمدة ثلاثين عاما والذي سعى لإقامة مملكة سلام التي ارتدى فيها الرجال أثوابا مرقطة كالفهود وكانت تدجن الحيوانات البرية . وفي هذا المفهوم الطوباوي كان لدى كايومارس عدوا سريا واحدا هو الشرير أهريمان الذي قاده حسده ليغري ولده ديف الأسود لقتل سياماك ابن كايومارس وقبل حدوث الاغتيال حذر الملك سوروش كايومارس من غدر أهريمان.
keywords: كايومارس ، غويمارس ، شهنامه ، شهناما ، ملوك ، كتاب الملوك ، صفحة ، لوحة ، عمل على الورق ، أعمال على الورق
materials: لون مائي غير شفاف ، حبر ، وذهب على الورق

en.name:
The court of Kayumars  
Folio from the *Shahnameh* (Book of Kings) of Shah Tahmasp
description: Firdausi’s epic poem the *Shahnameh* (Book of Kings), completed in 1010, recounts the history of all of Iran’s shahs (kings) up to the Arab conquest in 642 AD and the country’s adoption of Islam. A large part of the poem focuses on prehistoric, legendary kings, some of whom ruled for hundreds of years and established man’s knowledge of everything from fire to weaving. According to Firdausi, the very idea of kingship originated with King Kayumars, who ruled for thirty years, overseeing a peaceable kingdom in which men wore leopard-skin robes and wild animals grew tame. In this utopia Kayumars had one secret enemy, the evil Ahriman, whose envy drove him to incite his own son, the Black Div, to murder Siyamak, the son of Kayumars. Before the assassination took place, the angel Surush warned Kayumars of Ahriman’s plot.
artist: Attributed to Safavid master Sultan Muhammad
keywords: Kayumars; Guymars; Shahnameh; Shanama; kings; book-of-kings; folio; painting; work-on-paper; works-on-paper
materials: Opaque watercolour, ink, and gold on paper
tags: Opaque watercolour, ink, and gold on paper

en.name: Musée de Cherchell. Fragments found in the excavations.
names: Taken from *L'Algerie Phtographiée*, vol. 2, Province d'Alger
short_description: The French established two museums in Algeria after the conquest: one in Algiers (1838), and another in Cherchell (1840). The latter was overshadowed by the reputation of the former and lacked subsidies. A report from 1855 describes abandoned collections, to which the objects found during an 1856 excavation were soon added. This image, dating from 1856, highlights both the richness of the works presented to the Musée de Cherchell and their inadequate conservation. A new museum, built in 1908, allowed the collections to be stored in better conditions.
keywords: Antiquities; Museums; Algeria

fr.name: Musée de Cherchell. Fragments trouvés dans les fouilles
names: Extrait de L'Algérie photographiée (tome 2) : Province d'Alger
short_description: Deux musées sont créés par la France en Algérie, au lendemain de la conquête : Alger (1838), Cherchell (1840). Le second souffre de l’importance accordée au premier et manque de subsides. Un rapport de 1855 signale des collections à l’abandon auxquelles viennent bientôt s’ajouter, en 1856, les objets trouvés lors d’une nouvelle campagne de fouilles. Cette photographie, datant de 1856, souligne donc à la fois la richesse des œuvres présentes au musée de Cherchell et les insuffisances de leur conservation. Un nouveau musée, construit en 1908, permettra d’abriter dans de meilleures conditions les collections.
keywords: Antiquités; musée; Algérie

ar.name: طبق.
description: طبق مستدير صغير من عجينة الكوارتز (فريت) ذو حافة مقلوبة وقاعدة منخفضة حلقية. زخرفة الطبق زهرية كثيفة تتضمن الورود الحمراء والخزامى الزرقاء النضرة بتفاصيل حمراء، وأزهار أخرى زرقاء وحمراء على أغصان ذات أوراق خضراء تنبثق من باقة مورقة، وتتوضع ورقة كبيرة مسننة من النوع المعروف باسم الساز بشكل قطري عبر الأزهار المرسومة بشكل طبيعي، وهي ملونة بالأزرق من الخارج أما من الداخل فهي على شكل حبات الخرز المتتالية باللونين الأبيض والأحمر. الحافة مزينة بحدود متموجة منفذة بالأزرق والأسود. تظهر أوراق الساز بشكل متكرر في الخزف الإزنيقي المتأخر العائد للقرن الحادي عشر/ السابع عشر إلا أن أصوله تعود إلى الأسلوب الزخرفي الذي تطور في القرن التاسع/ الخامس عشر في إيران ثم تم استعماله على القطع من جميع المواد خلال الفترة العثمانية.

هذا النمط من الصحون، بتشكيلته الزهرية الفعالة، المُنفَّذة بالأزرق، والأخضر، والأسود، والأحمر القرمزي المُميَّز، بحاشيته "الصازية" المكتنزة وبحافته المموجة النازلة، مثال أنموذجي للخزفيات المُنتجة في ازنيق، خلال الفترة من أواخر إلى أوائل القرنين العاشر والحادي عشر الهجريين/ السادس عشر والسابع عشر الميلاديين، على التوالي.
holder: المتحف الملكي، المتحف الوطني في اسكتلندا NMS.
dates: أواخر القرن العاشر- أوائل الحادي عشر/ أواخر السادس عشر- أوائل السابع عشر.
keywords: إزنيق؛ ورقة ساز.
materials: عجينة كوارتزية (فريت) بألوان سوداء وزرقاء وخضراء، وطبقة قرميدية اللون تحت التزجيج، وفوقها طبقة شفافة من التزجيج.

en.name: Dish.
description: A circular stone-paste (fritware) dish with a shallow well, everted rim and low circular foot-ring. The dish has a busy floral composition, incorporating red roses, fleshy blue tulips with red detailing, and other blue and red flowers on stalks with green leafage, rising from a leafy tuft. A large serrated so-called *saz* leaf, rendered in blue with a white and red beaded centre, is placed obliquely across the naturalistically drawn flowers. The rim is decorated with a debased wave border, executed in blue and black. The *saz* leaf occurs repeatedly in later Iznik wares of the AH 11th / AD 16th-century but its origins lie within a decorative style developed in AH 9th- / AD 15th-century Iran and then subsequently adapted to all media within Ottoman art.

This type of dish, with its busy floral composition rendered in blue, green, black and the characteristic bole-red, its fleshy *saz* leaf and its debased wave border, is a typical example of the ceramics produced in Iznik during the AH late 10th–early 11th centuries / AD late 16th–early 17th centuries.
dates: Hegira, late 10th– early 11th century / AD late 16th– early 17th century.
keywords: Iznik; saz leaf
materials: Stone-paste (fritware), black, blue, green and bole-red underglaze, over which a clear glaze.
tags: Stone-paste (fritware), black, blue, green and bole-red underglaze, over which a clear glaze.

es.name: Plato
description:
Plato de pasta de piedra (frita) poco hondo, ala pronunciada y pie anular bajo. La tupida composición floral incluye rosas rojas, carnosos tulipanes con detalles en rojo y otras flores azules y rojas que salen de tallos con hojas verdes que crecen de un manojo de hojas. El centro lo ocupa una hoja de *saz* dentada, dibujada oblicuamente respecto al resto de los elementos. El ala se decora con grupos de olas en azul y negro.  
Los orígenes del uso de la hoja de *saz* como motivo decorativo hay que buscarlos en el Irán del siglo IX / XV. Posteriormente, el arte otomano la utilizaría en diferentes materiales y se haría muy popular en las piezas cerámicas de Iznik de finales del siglo XI / XVI.

Este plato, con su tupida composición floral en azul, verde, negro y bol rojo, las carnosas hojas de *saz* y las olas del ala, es un ejemplo característico de la producción cerámica de Iznik de finales del siglo X y principios del XI (finales del XVI-principios del XVII d. C.).
dates: Finales del siglo X-principios del XI de la Hégira / finales del XVI-principios del XVII d. C.
keywords: Iznik; hoja de saz
materials: Pasta de piedra (frita) pintada en negro, azul, verde y engobe de bol rojo bajo vidriado claro.
tags: Pasta de piedra (frita) pintada en negro, azul, verde y engobe de bol rojo bajo vidriado claro.

fr.name: Plat.
description: Plat en céramique frittée à bassin creux, bord retourné et piédouche rond de faible hauteur. Il est orné d'une riche composition florale réaliste à base de roses rouges, de tulipes bleues et charnues à rehauts rouges et de fleurs bleues et rouges sur tiges à feuillage vert s'élevant d'une touffe de feuilles. Une importante feuille *saz* dentelée bleue à la partie centrale ornée de disques blancs à point rouge est disposée en oblique parmi les fleurs. L'aile est décorée d'une bordure vagues-et-rochers simplifiée exécutée en bleu et blanc. La feuille *saz* apparaît de façon répétée dans les productions tardives d'Iznik au XIe siècle H (XVIe siècle J.-C.). Elle est issue d'un style décoratif mis au point au IXe siècle H (XVe siècle J.-C.) en Iran et adapté à tous les types de supports par l'art ottoman.

Ce type de plat, avec sa composition florale animée rendue en bleu, vert, noir et le caractéristique rouge d’Iznik (bol arménien), sa feuille *saz* charnue et sa bordure simplifiée de vagues-et-rochers est un exemple typique des céramiques produites à Iznik fin Xe-début XIe siècle H (fin XVIe-début XIIe siècle J.-C.).
dates: Fin Xe-début XIe siècle de l’Hégire (fin XVIe-début XVIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Iznik ; feuille saz
materials: Céramique frittée, décor peint noir, bleu, vert et rouge d’Iznik (bol arménien) sous glaçure transparente.
tags: Céramique frittée, décor peint noir, bleu, vert et rouge d’Iznik (bol arménien) sous glaçure transparente.

en.name: Sant'Agostino in San Michele
description: The church has a simple slender gabled façade with side capitals holding a frieze framing the central window. There is only a portal. The wall still bears signs of the older structure including a gable frieze and a closed arch which is part of a portico once standing at the side of the portal. The church has one nave with three chapels on each side. Each chapel is framed by columns with Corinthians capitals and between the columns are wooden confessional boxes. Above each confessional opens a niche hosting allegorical figures (*Mercy*, *Charity*, *Justice*, *Humility*, *Penitence*, and *Wisdom*) moulded in stucco. *St. Michael Defeating the Devil* is made of the same material. All the sculptures are works of the Bolognese sculptor Angelo Gabriello Piò (1690–1770), who was aided by his son Domenico. He often collaborated with architects like Dotti, Ambrosi and Viaggi, because of his skill in mixing sculptural decoration and architecture. We have no documentary evidence but Piò was probably summoned to Imola to work in Sant'Agostino about 1750.

The façade of the church bears many traces of its older history: the rose window and the corbel freeze go back to the twelve-century. In 1354 the church passed to the Augustinan Fathers who started a complete remodelling. Further enlargements followed in the fourteenth and sixteenth centuries, leading to the present building. The stucco decoration inside the church was moulded by the Bolognese sculptor Angelo Gabriello Piò who made it about 1750. Piò worked in strict contact with Domenico Morelli, the Ticinese architect who rebuilt the church starting from 1747.
artist:
Architects: Domenico Morelli and Cosimo Morelli (1732–1812); sculptors: Angelo Gabriello (1690–1770) and Domenico Piò (1715–1801).  
Angelo Piò started as a pupil of the Ferrarese Andrea Ferreri. In 1712 he entered the workshop of Giuseppe Maria Mazza, who changed the sculptural language of Bologna in the second half of the seventeenth-century. He worked with Camillo Rusconi in Rome. Upon returning to Bologna he became a member of the local Accademia Clementina. He worked intensely and exclusively for Bologna and its province beginning in the thirties.
history:
The church of Sant'Agostino flanks the via Emilia and opens on the via Marsala. The original church was built in the mid fourteenth-century. The Augustinian fathers, living outside Porta Piolo decided to relocate to inside the town walls. They moved into an already extant church, the Romanesque San Michele documented from the twelve-century. Preserving the former name in the parish church intitulation, they decided to rebuild it. The building was enlarged in the fourteenth-and fifteenth-centuries. The present church was remodelled by two architects, Domenico and Cosimo Morelli from Ticino and working in the Legazione Pontificia. Domenico, father of Cosimo, planned the structure of the church starting from 1747, as shown in the original documents. In 1767 his son changed the presbiterium and the apsis, partially changing his father's design. Construction ended in 1769. Cosimo Morelli worked alongside his brother Luigi and the masters Trifogli and Diabene, a sign of the well-organised équipe work in Ticinese workshops.  
On the counter façade, above the main door, stands a group with the *Archangel Michael Defeating the Devil*. On the sides, between columns, are the statues of *Mercy*, *Charity*, *Justice*, *Humility*, *Penitence*, *Wisdom*.  
In 1798 the parish church of Sant'Agostino became subsidiary; It was reopened in 1826 as parish church.
keywords: Angelo Gabriello Piò; Domenico Piò; Barocchetto; Baroque sculpture; Allegories; Augustian order; Domenico Morelli; Cosimo Morelli; Trifogli; Diabene; *St. Michael*; Religious; Stuccowork; Architectural sculpture
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: S. Agostino in S. Michele
description: La chiesa presenta una semplice e snella facciata a capanna con lesene laterali e capitelli che sostengono un fregio che incornicia la finestra centrale. C'è un unico portale. La parete reca ancora i segni di una struttura anteriore come il fregio a mensoline e gli archi ciechi, parte di un portico che un tempo fiancheggiava il lato del portale. La chiesa è a navata unica, con tre cappelle per lato. Ogni cappella è incorniciata da colonne con capitelli corinzi, tra cui sono posti i confessionali in legno. Sopra i confessionali si aprono delle nicchie che contengono figure allegoriche (*Misericordia, Carità, Giustizia, Umiltà, Penitenza, Sapienza*) modellate in stucco. Il *S. Michele che sconfigge il demonio* è modellato nello stesso materiale. Tutte le scultire sono opera dello scultore bolognese Angelo Gabriello Piò (1690–1770), aiutato qui dal figlio Domenico. Piò collaborò spesso con architetti come Dotti, Ambrosi e Viaggi, grazie alla sua capacità di mescolare la scutura decorativa con l'architettura. Non abbiano documenti che lo provino, ma Piò venne probabilmente convocato a Imola per lavorare in S. Agostino attorno al 1750.

La facciata della chiesa reca numerose tracce della sua storia precedente: il rosone e il fregio a mensole risalgono infatti al XII secolo. Nel 1354 la chiesa passò ai Padri Agostiniani che ne iniziarono una completa ristrutturazione. Ampliamenti successivi seguirono nei secoli XIV e XVI, portando all'attuale edificio. La decorazione in stucco all'interno fu eseguita dallo scultore bolognese Angelo Gabriello Piò, nel 1750 circa. Piò lavorò in stretto contatto con Domenico Morelli, l'architetto ticinese che ricostruì la chiesa a partire dal 1747.
artist:
Architetti: Domenico Morelli e Cosimo Morelli; scultori: Angelo Gabriello e Domenico Piò.  
Angelo Piò iniziò come allievo del ferrarese Andrea Ferreri, nel 1712 entrò nella bottega dello scultore bolognese Giuseppe Maria Mazza, che rinnovò il linguaggio architettonico a Bologna nella seconda metà del XVII secolo. A Roma lavorò con Camillo Rusconi e quando tornò a Bologna divenne membro dell' Accademia Clementina. Dagli anni trenta lavora intensamente ed esclusivamente per Bologna e la sua provincia.
history:
La chiesa di S. Agostino fiancheggia la via Emilia e si apre su via Marsala. L'edificio originario fu costruito a metà del XIV secolo, dopo che gli Agostiniani che avevano vissuto fuori Porta Piolo decisero di trasferirsi dentro le mura cittadine, occupando una chiesa già esistente, la romanica S. Michele, documentata dal XII secolo. Essi decisero di farla ricostruire, matenendone il nome nell'intitolazione parrochiale. L'edificio fu ampliato tra i secoli XIV e XV; la chiesa attuale fu ristrutturata da due architetti ticinesi che lavoravano nella  Legazione Pontificia, Domenico e Cosimo Morelli. Domenico, padre di Cosimo, progettò la struttura della chiesa a partire dal 1747, come dimostrano i documenti, e nel 1767 suo figlio modificò il presbiterio e l'abside, intervenendo sul progetto del padre. I lavori terminarono nel 1769. Assieme a  Cosimo Morelli lavorarono suo fratello Luigi e i capimastri Trifogli e Diabene, un esempio del lavoro di squadra ben organizzato delle botteghe ticinesi.  
Sulla controfacciata, al di sopra della portale d'ingresso, sta il gruppo dell'*Arcangelo Michele che sconfigge il Demonio* mentre sulle pareti, tra le colonne, sono poste le statue della *Misericordia*, della *Carità*, della *Giustizia*, della *Umiltà*, della *Penitenza* e della *Sapienza*.  
Nel 1798 la parrochciale di S. Agostino divenne sussidiale; solo nel 1826 fu di nuovo riaperta come chiesa parrochiale.
keywords: Angelo Gabriello Piò; Domenico Piò; Barocchetto; Scultura barocca; Allegorie; Ordine Agostiniano; Domenico Morelli; Cosimo Morelli; Trifogli; Diabene; S. Michele; Religioso; Stucco; Scultura architettonica

en.name: Sidi ‘Abdallah Ibn Djafar Mosque
description:
The mosque of Tafessera is now called Sidi Abdallah Ibn Djafar, because oral tradition has it that the mosques of the Beni Snous were founded by order of Abdallah Ibn Djafar, nephew of the caliph Ali and companion of Okba ben Nafi. It can be accessed through a courtyard whose left portion serves as a *mossalla* (occasional place of prayer) with its carved *mihrab* (niche) in the enclosing wall. At the back are the latrines, which were provided with running water via a small channel from a spring behind the surrounding wall.  
  
The plan of the mosque is square, divided into three *balatas* (naves) perpendicular to the *qibla* (East-facing wall) and into three bays. The square-based pillars are connected by horseshoe arches. A double-sloped tiled roof, over cedar beams, covers the naves. The dome in front of the *mihrab* is covered by a four-sided tiled roof. The minaret evokes mosques of the Abdalwadid period in its proportions, but not in its decoration, which is reduced to a few projecting bricks. These bricks and the entire minaret are whitewashed in lime.  
  
The horseshoe arch of the *mihrab* rests on two columns surmounted by capitals in the form of a pyramid. The whole is made of masonry covered with lime mortar. The arch of the *mihrab* is surmounted by a slightly protruding bowed band. Another bowed band encloses the former. Surrounding the latter is a three-sided square frame.  
  
In the wall facing the *mihrab* are two niches that were partially decorated with motifs whose origin remains unclear. Initially the arch of the right niche was devoid of these lobes in relief; the right angle at the top of the frame did not have any decoration.

fr.name: Mosquée Sidi Abdellah Ben Djafar
description:
La mosquée de Tafessera porte le nom de Sidi Abdellah Ben Djafar. La tradition orale veut que les mosquées des Beni Snous aient été fondées sur ordre d'Abdellah Ben Djafar, neveu du calife Ali et compagnon de Okba Ben Nafi. On accède à la mosquée par une cour dont la partie gauche sert de *mossalla* (lieu de prière occasionnel) avec son *mihrab* creusé dans le mur d'enceinte et, au fond, les latrines, qui étaient alimentées en eau courante par un petit canal venant de la source située juste derrière le mur d'enceinte.  
  
Le plan de la mosquée est carré, il est divisé en trois *balatat* (nefs) perpendiculaires au mur de la *qibla* et en trois travées. Les piliers à base carrée sont reliés entre eux par des arcs outrepassés. Des doubles-pentes en tuiles canal, sur des nappes de rondins en thuya, couvrent les *balatat*. La coupole au-devant du *mihrab* est couverte par une toiture en tuiles canal à quatre pentes. Le minaret évoque ceux des mosquées de la période abdalwadide par ses proportions, mais non par son décor, qui se résume à quelques saillies en briques enduites à la chaux, comme, du reste, le minaret tout entier.  
  
L'arc outrepassé du *mihrab* repose sur deux colonnes surmontées de chapiteaux en tronc de pyramide. L'ensemble est en maçonnerie recouverte d'un mortier de chaux. Cet arc du *mihrab* est surmonté d'un bandeau en arc lobé légèrement saillant. Un autre bandeau en arc, non lobé, encadre le précédent. Sur ce dernier repose une bande horizontale, en saillie de la même épaisseur que les deux arcs, perpendiculaire à deux bandes verticales formant ainsi l'encadrement de la face du *mihrab*. Dans cet encadrement, les écoinçons, les bandes des arcs et les bandeaux verticaux et horizontaux étaient dépourvus de tout décor. Dans le mur qui fait face au *mihrab* se trouvent deux niches qui étaient partiellement décorées de motifs dont l'origine reste mal définie. Initialement, l'arc de la niche de droite était dépourvu de ces lobes en relief ; l'angle droit en haut de l'encadrement ne portait pas de décor.

en.name: Figures in Turkish style
description: In these two porcelain figures, it is showed through the clothes, and combined with the Rococo style of the bases. Produced by many European manufactures at the time, this kind of objects could be easily found in rooms as the *fumoir*, usually decorated in an Orientalist style to recreate exoticism.
keywords: Production of applied art in Europe in the Islamic mode; Turkish influence
materials: Moulded; enamelled, painted and gilded porcelain

ar.name: زبدية.
description: زبدية خزفية من عجينة كوارتزية بيضاء ملونة تحت التزجيج بالبني والأزرق والأخضر والأحمر. ومن الناحية التقنية فإن الزخارف الملونة على شكل فارس ما هي إلا تقليد لنوع من الخزف الإيراني المعروف باسم خزف "ميناي" الذي يعني حرفياً "المطعم بالمينا"، وهي تقنية يتم فيها دهن بعض الألوان فوق التزجيج ثم تثبيتها بطريقة الشي. تأثر الخزافون السوريون بالتطورات في إيران إلا أن المعرفة بتقنية العمل بالمينا على الخزف نقصتهم، فقاموا بتقليد الأسلوب. وتقلد هذه الزبدية نوع التصميم المستعمل على خزف ميناي مع تلوين تحت التزجيج باستعمال ألوان براقة مشابهة للمينا. وعلى الجهة السفلى من الزبدية، هناك كتابة غير مقروءة.

وعاء مُزخرف برسم فارس يمتطي جواده، والمستوحى من فن الفخار الإيراني. كان مثل هذا النوع من الفخار المطلي بالمينا، يُصدَّر من إيران إلى سوريا، حيث قام الفخاريون بتقليد هذا النوع، مُستخدمين الفخار المُزجَّج، بدلاً من طليه بالمينا.
keywords: فروسية.
materials: خزف من عجينة كوارتزية بيضاء ملونة تحت التزجيج بالبني والأزرق والأخضر والأحمر.

en.name: Bowl.
description: A stone-paste ceramic bowl painted in brown, blue, green and red underglaze. Technically, the colourful decoration of a horseman imitates a type of Iranian ceramic known as *mina‘i* ware, ‘mina‘i’ meaning literally enamelled, a technique in which some of the colours were painted over the glaze and then fixed by firing. The Syrian potters were influenced by developments in Iran but lacked the technical knowledge of working with enamels on ceramics. They therefore imitated the style. This bowl mimics the type of design employed on minai wares with underglaze painting in similar bright colours to enamel. There is an illegible inscription on the underside of the bowl.

The colourful decoration of the horseman on this ceramic bowl imitates a type of ceramic that originated in Iran. Enamelled ceramics, or *mina'i* ware, were exported from Iran to Syria, where potters imitated the style using underglaze painting rather than enamels.
keywords: Horsemanship
materials: Stone-paste ceramic painted with brown, blue, green and red underglaze.
tags: Stone-paste ceramic painted with brown, blue, green and red underglaze.

es.name: Cuenco
description:
Cuenco de pasta de piedra pintado en marrón, azul, verde y rojo bajo vidriado. Técnicamente, la colorida decoración que representa a un jinete imita la cerámica iraní *minai*, que literalmente quiere decir “esmaltado”. Se trata de una técnica en la que algunos colores se aplican sobre el vidriado y se fijan con la cocción.  
La cerámica iraní influyó en los alfareros sirios, pero estos carecían de los conocimientos técnicos del esmaltado, así que se limitaron a copiar el estilo. Este cuenco imita el tipo de diseño de la cerámica *minai*, pero con la pintura bajo vidriado en colores brillantes que recuerdan el esmalte. Bajo el pie hay una inscripción incomprensible.

La colorida decoración con un jinete en este cuenco la de un tipo de cerámica originada en Irán. La cerámica esmaltada o *minai* se exportaba de Irán a Siria, donde los alfareros la imitaban utilizando pinturas bajo vidriado en vez de esmaltes.
dates: Siglo VII de la Hégira / XIII d. C.
keywords: equitación
materials: Pasta de piedra pintada en marrón, azul, verde y rojo bajo vidriado.
tags: Pasta de piedra pintada en marrón, azul, verde y rojo bajo vidriado.

fr.name: Coupe.
description: Coupe en céramique frittée à décor peint sous glaçure en brun, bleu, vert et rouge. Techniquement, le dessin très coloré du cavalier imite un type de céramique iranienne appelé *minaï* – signifiant littéralement “émaillé” –, technique dans laquelle certaines couleurs sont peintes sur la glaçure avant d'être fixées par une nouvelle cuisson. Les potiers syriens étaient influencés par les développements des arts décoratifs iraniens mais manquaient des connaissances techniques nécessaires pour émailler les céramiques. Ils en imitèrent donc simplement le style. Cette coupe reproduit le type de dessin employé sur les poteries *minaï* à peinture en sous-glaçure au moyen de couleurs vives similaires à celles de l'émail. Une inscription illisible figure sous le pied de la coupe.

Sur cette coupe, la décoration fortement colorée du cavalier imite un type de céramique originaire d'Iran. Les céramiques émaillées dites *minai* étaient exportées d'Iran en Syrie, où des potiers imitaient ce style en remplaçant les émaux par une peinture rouge sous glaçure.
dates: VIIe siècle de l’Hégire (XIIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Équitation
materials: Céramique frittée, décor peint sous glaçure en brun, bleu, vert et rouge.
tags: Céramique frittée, décor peint sous glaçure en brun, bleu, vert et rouge.

en.name: Basilica dei santi Bartolomeo e Gaetano
description:
The church has a Latin cross plan with three naves, separated by slender fluted columns with ionic capitals.  
The central nave ceiling is decorated with the *Vision of St. Gaetano* by Giacomo Alboresi, framed by the imposing illusionistic baroque decoration painted by Angelo Michele Colonna and Agostino Mitelli.  
The minor naves are covered with small domes and the side square chapels with vaulted ceilings are a personal reinterpretation of the plan of the Chiesa del Gesù in Rome.  
In the side chapels of the right nave we find some very important examples of baroque painting such as the *Apparition of the Angel to St. Charles Borromeo* by Ludovico Carracci. The frescoes on the walls, the dome and the pendentives of the third chapel are by Angelo Michele Colonna. The *Annunciation* is by Francesco Albani; *Two Angels* by Domenico Canuti and a fresco with *Saint Gaetano in Glory and four Prophets* are by Burrini and Chiarini.  
Over the transept hovers the great round dome decorated with the *Coronation of St. Gaetano and the Fathers of the Latin Church* by Antonio and Giuseppe Rolli. The same painters also worked on the apse with the *Glory of St. Gaetano* and on the vaults of the left transept.  
In the high chapel Marcantonio Franceschini and Luigi Quaini, helped by Enrico Haffner for the quadratura, painted three frescoes.  
Among the left nave chapels is worth noting the *Madonna del Suffragio* by Guido Reni, donated in 1663 by Canon Matteo Sagaci, twice stolen and recovered, and a *St. Michael* by Giuseppe Rolli.  
Linked to the church are a small crypt under the presbiterium, decorated with frescoes, and a sixteenth- century oratory dedicated to the Immaculate Conception and St. Gaetano. The oratory holds an old fresco of the Madonna and Child attributed to Lippo di Dalmasio, moved here in 1871 from a former church located next to the tower Garisenda.

The reference to the academic tradition created by Guido Reni and the following Baroque renovations are perfectly exemplified in this church by the works of some of the major representatives of the new wave such as Angelo Michele Colonna, Giacomo Alboresi, Agostino Mitelli, Giovanni Antonio Burrini, Marcantonio Chiarini, Antonio and Giuseppe Rolli.  
The lunettes created by Cignani for the external portico were greatly celebrated from the beginning by his contemporaries. The decorations and paintings in the church are still just as impressive today, thanks to their illusionistic perspective and strong theatricality.
artist: Giovan Battista Natali; Agostino Barelli; Giuseppe e Antonio Rolli; Angelo Michele Colonna; Giacomo Alboresi; Agostino Mitelli; Giovanni Antonio Burrini; Marcantonio Chiarini
history:
A long oral tradition mentions a church built here in the fifth- century by Bishop St. Petronius for the early Bolognese faithful. However, the first written documents which have been found date it to 1288. The primitive church was dedicated to St. Bartholomew and its façade overlooked Piazza di Porta Ravegnana. The church was part of a monastery of Cluniac monks.  
In 1516, the prior Giovanni Gozzadini commissioned from Andrea Marchesi, known as Formigine, a project for his residence and the refurbishing of the church. With only the sandstone portico finished, the work was interrupted the following year, when Gozzadini was assassinated.  
In 1627 the Theatine Fathers took charge and started the work anew following first a project by Giovan Battista Natali and later one by the architect of the Bolognese Senate Agostino Barelli. These new plans moved the façade from the square to the nearby street, Strada Maggiore. The Fathers put together the title of St. Bartholomew with that of their founder, St. Gaetano and commissioned from Marcantonio Franceschini and Luigi Quaini the decoration of the ten lunettes under the original 1sixteenth- century portico.
keywords: Religious architecture; baroque painted decoration; quadratura
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: Basilica dei SS. Bartolomeo e Gaetano
names: Basilica dei santi Bartolomeo e Gaetano
description:
La chiesa ha pianta a croce latina e alzato a tre navate, divise da snelle colonne scanalate sormontate da capitelli ionici.  
La volta della navata centrale è dipinta con la *Visione di San Gaetano* di Giacomo Alboresi, entro l'imponente decorazione barocca a quadrature prospettiche di Angelo Michele Colonna e Agostino Mitelli.  
Le navate laterali inquadrano otto cupole illuminate da lanterne e otto cappelline rettangolari con volta a botte, rivisitando il principio basilicale romano della chiesa del Gesù.  
Nelle cappelle di destra hanno particolare rilevanza: l' *Apparizione dell'angelo a San Carlo Borromeo* di Ludovico Carracci; gli affreschi alle pareti, nella cupoletta e nei pennacchi della terza cappella di Angelo Michele Colonna; l' *Annunciazione* di Francesco Albani; *Due angeli* di Domenico Canuti e l'affresco *San Gaetano in gloria e quattro profeti* di Burrini e Chiarini.  
Al di sopra dell'incrocio dei bracci del transetto si erge la grande cupola circolare decorata, con l' *Incoronazione di S. Gaetano* e i *Padri della Chiesa Latina,* da Antonio e Giuseppe Rolli, che realizzano anche la cappella absidale con la *Gloria di San Gaetano* e le volte del transetto sinistro.  
Nell'abside si trovano inoltre tre affreschi di Marcantonio Franceschini e Luigi Quaini su quadratura di Enrico Haffner.  
Nelle cappelle di sinistra si segnala la *Madonna del Suffragio* di Guido Reni, donata nel 1663 dal Canonico Matteo Sagaci, due volte sottratta e altrettante restituita, e il *San Michele* di Giuseppe Rolli.  
Alla chiesa sono collegati due suggestivi ambienti. Una piccola cripta affrescata sotto il presbiterio e l'oratorio cinquecentesco dell'Immacolata Concezione e S. Gaetano, che conserva una antica immagine della *Madonna* *col Bambino* attribuita a Lippo di Dalmasio, già collocata in una chiesina accanto alla torre Garisenda e qui spostata nel 1871.

Il distacco dalla tradizione accademica reniana e il conseguente rinnovamento barocco si esprimono magnificamente in S. Bartolomeo e Gaetano grazie all’operato comune di alcuni tra i maggiori esponenti della nuova corrente: Angelo Michele Colonna, Giacomo Alboresi, Agostino Mitelli, Giovanni Antonio Burrini, Marcantonio Chiarini, Antonio e Giuseppe Rolli.  
Le lunette ideate dal Cignani per il portico esterno furono già dai contemporanei fortemente applaudite e ammirate, i decori e le pitture all’interno stupiscono ed emozionano per l’effetto di illusionismo prospettico e la forte teatralità.
artist: Giovan Battista Natali; Agostino Barelli; Giuseppe e Antonio Rolli; Angelo Michele Colonna; Giacomo Alboresi; Agostino Mitelli; Giovanni Antonio Burrini; Marcantonio Chiarini.
history:
Anche se la tradizione parla di una chiesa eretta nel V secolo da S. Petronio, nel luogo in cui si riunivano i cristiani bolognesi, la prima documentazione certa sull’edificio si ha solo nel 1288, e testimonia che era dedicato a S. Bartolomeo, aveva la facciata posta su piazza di Porta Ravegnana ed era annesso a un monastero cluniacense.  
Nel 1516 il priore Giovanni Gozzadini commissiona, ad Andrea Marchesi detto il Formigine, il progetto del suo Palazzo del Priorato e la ristrutturazione del tempio, ma assassinato un anno dopo sarà realizzato solo il portico in arenaria.  
Così nel 1627 i padri Teatini devono riprendere le ristrutturazioni, su disegno di Giovan Battista Natali e poi dall’architetto del Senato bolognese Agostino Barelli. Prevedono un nuovo orientamento della chiesa su Strada Maggiore, uniscono al titolo di S. Bartolomeo quello del loro fondatore S. Gaetano e commissionano a Marcantonio Franceschini e Luigi Quaini l’esecuzione di dieci lunette nel portico del Formigine.
keywords: architettura religiosa; decorazione barocca; quadrature prospettiche

ar.name: عتب باب.
description: القطعة عبارة عن عتب باب كانت تعلو بوابة في إحدى الغرف الواقعة في الزاوية الشمالية الغربية من قصر أم الوليد الأموي. تغطي واجهة العتب طبقة من الجص حفر عليها بالنحت البارز صورة فهد يطارد غزالاً. تذكّرنا هذه القطعة بأنواع الحيوانات التي كانت تجوب المنطقة خلال الفترة الأموية، و كانت تشارك في لعبة الصيد التي كان يمارسها البلاط الأموي كنوع من التسلية. وتترك هذه القطعة لدى الناظر انطباعاً قوياً بصفتها لوحة أكثر من كونها نحتاً على الحجر.

عارضة كانت ذات يوم تُزيِّن قمة بوابة أحد القصور الأموية، في أم الوليد. والمشهد المُنفَّذ بالجصِّ النافر الخفيف، يصوِّر فهداً يطار ظبياً، تذكيراً بالحيوانات البرية التي كانت منتشرة في الأرياف، أيام الحقبة الأموية.
keywords: أعمال الحجر؛ أعمال النحت؛ حياة البلاط؛ صيد.

en.name: Door lintel.
description: A lintel that once adorned the top of a doorway of an Umayyad palace at Umm al-Walid. Worked in shallow stucco relief, this rare object appears to be more one-dimensional like a painting, than a two-dimensional work in relief. The scene depicts a panther chasing a gazelle, a reminder of the wild animals that once roamed the countryside during the Umayyad period, creatures that were game to courtly hunts organised for amusement.

es.name: Dintel de puerta
description: Dintel que coronaba una de las puertas de un palacio omeya en Umm al-Walid. Este curioso objeto, que presenta un relieve en estuco poco profundo, parece tener una sola dimensión, como un cuadro, en lugar de las dos dimensiones características de los relieves. La escena representa a una pantera cazando a una gacela, y evoca a los animales salvajes que poblaban el campo en época omeya y eran las presas de las jornadas de caza que la dinastía organizaba como pasatiempo.

Dintel que adornaba la parte superior de la entrada de un palacio omeya de Umm al-Walid. La escena, realizada en bajorrelieve sobre estuco, representa a una pantera persiguiendo a una gacela, escena que evoca a los animales salvajes que habitaban la zona durante el periodo omeya.
dates: Siglo II de la Hégira / VIII d. C.
keywords: Vida en la corte; caza; relieve; trabajo en piedra.

fr.name: Linteau de porte.
description: Linteau ornant jadis le haut d'un passage de porte dans un palais omeyyade à Oum al-Walid. Fin travail d'incision sur stuc, ce rare panneau fait davantage penser à une peinture qu'à une sculpture. La scène représente une panthère poursuivant une gazelle, rappel de la présence des animaux sauvages qui peuplaient les campagnes pendant la période des Omeyyades et étaient l'objet de chasses organisées pour la distraction de la cour.

en.name: *Valahian Caravan*
short_description: In Wallachia and Moldavia transportation of merchandise by land was done similarly to the Arab and Ottoman world, but using big carts pulled by horses instead of camel caravans. Both the vehicle and a group of carts travelling together for commercial purposes were called "chervan”, a term derived from the Turkish word "kervan", meaning "caravan". The lithograph, depicting a carriage drawn by 12 horses and followed by a second vehicle, was printed in Vienna and its legend (*Wallachian carriage*) is written below the image in German, Hungarian and French.

en.name: *Capture of Francis I, King of France*
description:
The famous series of seven Flemish tapestries depicting the Battle of Pavia, which are displayed in a large room in the Museum of Capodimonte, entered the public collections as part of the 1862 bequest of Alfonso d’Avalos, who donated his family’s collection to the National Museum of Naples.  
Produced to be given to Emperor Charles V by the Estates-General of Brussels, on the occasion of the latter’s meeting in Brussels in 1531, the decorative series of tapestries was designed to celebrate the victory of the imperial troops over those of the French, under the command of Francis I. This victory, which occurred on 24 February 1525, was fought in the environs of the Visconti Park, at the gates of Pavia.  
Woven in Brussels, the tapestries were produced using designs by Bernard van Orley (now in the Louvre in Paris) in the workshop of William Dermoyen (or Van der Moyen), identified thanks to the presence of a weaver’s mark on the border of two tapestries in the series. Furthermore, the presence of the mark has allowed the years in which the series was produced to be established: that is, after 1528, the year in which a decree required tapestry workers to “sign” their products, and by the start of 1531, given that the tapestries would be presented to the Emperor in the March of that year.  
Recently, an interpretation of the entire cycle has been proposed that aims to recreate sequentially the landscape depicted in the seven tapestries as a single, panoramic, overview (Paredes 2014).  
The central episode represented in the tapestry is the capture of Francis I. After having passed through the copse, depicted high up on the left, and after having fought bravely on the muddy terrain, unfavourable to the heavy French cavalry, the King is captured following a shot from an arquebus that wounds his horse.  
Francis I is depicted in the foreground while three cavaliers from the enemy formation, La Motte de Noyers, the German Nicolas von Salm and the Count of Montmartin – as indicated by the abbreviated text that tends to be included on the horses’ tack and armour – help him to get to his feet. On the left is depicted the Viceroy of Naples, Charles de Lannoy, identified by the letters “VISSEROV” on the blade of his sword, while he dismounts from his horse to accept the surrender of the King.  
Behind him a horseman raises the imperial standard, on which one can distinguish the double-headed eagle and Hercules’ pillars with the motto “PLUS OVLTRE”. In the centre of the tapestry, the man on a horse, who is wearing a dark outfit, on which stands out the white cross that indicates that he is on the side of the French, is Henry II, King of Navarre, captured in battle; in the distance, on the right, among the horsemen who have just come out of the copse, appears Charles III, Duke of Bourbon, identified by the word “BOURBON” on the reins, as well as by the presence of French *fleurs-de-lis* on the horse’s peytral.  
In the foreground, on the ground, there is the arquebus with which Francis I’s horse was hit. This is also a symbol of the new way of fighting in battle and the end of the cavalry: the use of firearms, striking from a distance, allowed the less courageous to prevail.
artist: William Dermoyen atelier on a cartoon designed by Bernard van Orley

materials: Wool, silk and cotton; gold and silver thread

it.name: Cattura del re di Francia Francesco I
description:
La celebre serie dei sette arazzi fiamminghi della Battaglia di Pavia, esposti in una grande sala del museo di Capodimonte, entra nelle raccolte pubbliche con il legato testamentario del 1862 di Alfonso d’Avalos che dona al Museo Nazionale di Napoli la collezione di famiglia.  
Realizzata per essere donata dagli stati Generali di Bruxelles all’imperatore Carlo V, in occasione della riunione degli stessi a Bruxelles nel 1531, la serie decorativa intendeva celebrare la vittoria delle truppe imperiali su quelle francesi, comandate da Francesco I, avvenuta il 24 febbraio del 1525, e combattuta nella zona del Parco Visconteo, alle porte di Pavia.  
Tessuti a Bruxelles, gli arazzi sono stati realizzati su disegni di Bernard van Orley (oggi a Parigi, Musée du Louvre), nell'atelier di William Dermoyen ( o Van der Moyen), identificato grazie alla presenza del marchio del tessitore sulla bordure di due arazzi della serie. Inoltre, proprio la presenza del marchio ha permesso di stabilire gli anni di realizzazione del ciclo: cioè dopo il 1528, anno in cui un editto imponeva agli arazzieri di firmare i loro prodotti, ed entro l'inizio del 1531, dato che verrà donato nel mese di marzo all'imperatore.  
Recentemente è stata proposta una lettura d’insieme del ciclo, tesa a ricostruire in sequenza il paesaggio rappresentato nei sette arazzi in un’unica, e panoramica, visione d’insieme (Paredes 2014).  
L'episodio centrale raccontato nel panno è quello della cattura di Francesco I. Dopo aver attraversato il boschetto, rappresentato in alto a sinistra, e dopo essersi battuto valorosamente in un terreno fangoso, sfavorevole per la pesante cavalleria francese, il re viene catturato a seguito di un colpo di archibugio che ferisce il suo cavallo.  
Francesco I è raffigurato in primo piano mentre tre cavalieri dello schieramento nemico, La Motte de Noyers, il tedesco Nicolas von Salm e il conte di Montmartin - come suggeriscono le scritte abbreviate, inserite per lo più su finimenti e armature - lo aiutano a rialzarsi. Sulla sinistra, è raffigurato il viceré di Napoli Charles de Lannoy, identificato dalla scritta “VISSEROV” sulla lama della spada, mentre scende da cavallo per accettare la resa del re.  
Dietro di lui un cavaliere innalza lo stendardo imperiale, dove si riconoscono l'aquila bicipite e le colonne d'Ercole con il motto “PLUS OVLTRE”. Al centro dell'arazzo, l'uomo a cavallo in abito scuro, su cui spicca la croce bianca che indica l'appartenenza francese, è Enrico II d'Albret, re di Navarra, catturato in battaglia; sullo sfondo, a destra, tra i cavalieri appena usciti dal boschetto figura Carlo III di Borbone, identificato dalla scritta "BOURBON" sulle redini, nonché per la presenza dei gigli francesi sulla pettiera del cavallo.  
In primo piano, a terra, vi è l'archibugio con il quale è stato abbattuto il cavallo di Francesco I, simbolo anche del nuovo modo di fare battaglia e la fine della cavalleria: l'utilizzo delle armi da fuoco, colpendo da lontano, permettevano al meno prode di prevalere.
holder: Museo e Real Bosco di Capodimonte
artist: Atelier di William Dermoyen su disegni di Bernard van Orley
materials: Lana, seta, cotone colorato con fili d'oro e d'argento

en.name: Church of San Facundo y San Primitivo
description:
The church of San Facundo and San Primitivo shows a new kind of roof with a complete ornamental system in wood for the choir, the chapels and the tribune. The gothic sanctuary, which is polygonal and covered with a half ceiling, eight sided and of polychromed strapwork has its twin in Santo Tomás de Revellinos and at least partly seems to repeat the same solution as in the ceiling of the convent of Santa Clara in Tordesillas. The whole church also has a very special type of roof on a structure of columns typical of this district of Campos. The ceiling of pinewood, unpainted, eightsided and studded is in the form of chamfers which make diminishing rhomboid and octagonal shaped squinches. The whole is decorated with strips worked in wood and floral motifs of a Renaissance provenance. The system of transition between the central nave and the side aisles is reminiscent of Mazuecos de Valdeginate, and the workmanship and resulting shapes are not very different from those of Santos Justo y Pastor in Cuenca de Campos.  
In the first span of the nave on the epistle side there is the chapel of the Virgen del Castillo, probably by Juan Carpeil, since the same structural and decorative solutions appear as those already mentioned in VIllamuera de la Cueza. An upper choir displaced to the side of the church with heads of animals and heraldic risers referring to Castilla establishes another relationship with the work in Santa María in Becerril de Campos.

es.name: Iglesia de San Facundo y San Primitivo
description:
La iglesia de los Santos Facundo y Primitivo conjuga un nuevo tipo de techumbre con un completo sistema ornamental en madera para el coro, las capillas y la tribuna. La cabecera gótica, poligonal y cubierta con media techumbre ochavada de lacería polícroma, tiene su correlato en Santo Tomás de Revellinos y, al menos en parte, parece repetir la solución de la techumbre de la iglesia del convento de Santa Clara de Tordesillas. Además, todo el templo lleva un tipo de cubierta muy especial sobre una estructura columnaria de las habituales en la comarca de Campos. La techumbre de madera de pino sin pintar, ochavada y ataujerada, es de formas achaflanadas que constituyen pechinas de rombos y octógonos en disminución. Toda ella se decora con verduguillos labrados en madera y temas florales de procedencia renacentista. El sistema de transición entre la nave central y las laterales recuerda a Mazuecos de Valdeginate, y la labra y formas resultantes no están muy lejos de la de los Santos Justo y Pastor, en Cuenca de Campos.  
En el primer tramo de la nave de la epístola se alza la capilla de la Virgen del Castillo, obra probable de Juan Carpeil, pues repite las soluciones estructurales y decoraciones ya mencionadas en Villamuera de la Cueza. Un coro alto desplazado en un lateral del templo con cabezas de animales y tabicas heráldicas alusivas a Castilla establece otro parentesco con la obra de Santa María de Becerril de Campos.

en.name: Postal map
short_description: The network of routes for sending messages and transporting troops and supplies was carried out with a relay system, established in the 16th century in the Ottoman Empire. The messengers, who conveyed dispatches throughout the country, were identified as the Tatars. Private or personal correspondence was not a part of that relay system; it was built to fulfil governmental needs. Because of this reason the *reaya* (public) created an alternative postal method by using caravans, pilgrims, and private couriers called *ulaks*. The *Tanzimat* Decree, which was the declaration of process included reformation, modernization and westernization in 1839, proved that the Ottoman Empire was focused on its policy of changing governing to be more like modern Western European-style administrative practices.
keywords: architecture; Vedat Tek; postal service; communication

en.name: Water jar
description: This piece belongs to a set that came from a Turkish shipwreck in the Red Sea, in the Gulf of Aqaba, near Sharm al-Sheikh, during the second quarter of the 18th century. The precise origin of these ceramics is not known, but these water jars are similar to those still used in Egypt today. After the Ottoman conquest, Sultan Selim I deported Egyptian craftsmen from various trades to Istanbul. As a result, ceramics declined irremediably, and production was limited to utilitarian objects such as this one, whose designs are incomparable to those produced from the 9th to the 15th centuries.

fr.name: Gargoulette
description:
Cette pièce appartient à un ensemble qui proviendrait de l'épave d'un vaisseau turc naufragé en mer Rouge, dans le golfe d'Aqaba, près de Sharm al-Sheikh, durant le second quart du XVIIIe siècle J.-C. L'origine précise de ces céramiques n'est pas connue, mais ces gargoulettes sont proches de celles encore utilisées aujourd'hui en Égypte.  
Après la conquête ottomane, le sultan Sélim Ier fit déporter à Istanbul des artisans égyptiens sélectionnés parmi différents corps de métier. Dans ce contexte, la céramique déclina de façon irrémédiable et sa production se limita à des objets utilitaires comme celui-ci dont les décors sont bien éloignés de ceux produits du IXe au XVe siècle J.-C.

en.name: *Moors of Tetouan*
description:
This painting was made around 1863 when the author travelled to Morocco with Mariano Fortuny. The reason for his travel was to paint the characters and picturesque garments as the way of life of the people from Morocco.  
His experiences can be seen in his paintings and drawings.  
During his travels he bought exotic artworks as Egyptian sarcophagi.  
Harem and markets are considered a genre painting in Orientalism.
keywords: North Africa; Orientalism; Travelling

en.name: Bottle
description: The decoration was made by cutting away the outer layer of glass. The pattern, characteristic of early Abbasid art, was first developed for stucco reliefs that decorated buildings in the capital of Samarra. The bottle’s stylized birds and entwined, abstract vegetal ornaments are motifs that frequently appear in the art of the period.

cs.name: Kaple sv. Kříže
description: V dostavbě zámku pokračoval a obdélnou kapli v jižním křídle dokončil dvorní architekt, školený ve Vídni a v Římě. Plastickou výzdobu s Kladením Krista do hrobu na hlavním oltáři, Madonou Starobrněnskou a Smrtí sv. Františka na bočních oltářích vytvořil dvorní sochař Johann Stern, bratr malíře Josefa. Portál kaple podle Grimmova návrhu zhotovil brněnský kameník Joachim Günther.

en.name: Chapel of the Holy Cross
description: A court architect who trained in Vienna and in Rome continued the construction of the chateau and completed the rectangular chapel in the south wing. The relief decorations, with the *Laying of Christ in His Grave* on the high altar, and the *Madonna of Old Brno* and the *Death of St. Francis* on side altars, were created by court sculptor Johann Stern, brother of the painter Josef Stern. The chapel portal, designed by Grimm, was executed by the Brno stonemason Joachim Günther.
artist: František Antonín Grimm (1710–1784, Brno), Johann Stern, Joachim Günther

ar.name: عناصر من سوار
description: هذا السوار يتضمن حلقات مطلية بالمينا ويوجد ثمانية فواصل صغيرة وعنصرين بشكل الجرس التي تشكل الإبزيم (المشبك). والحلقات الأربع مطلية بالمينا وتحمل صور لطائر بجهة اليمين ، وآخر بجهة اليسار وورقة ثلاثية وشكل غير محدد. والألوان الرئيسية هي البرتقالي – الأصفر غير الشفاف والأصفر الشاحب وأحمر شمع الختم والأزرق الملكي نصف الشفاف والأخضر. والمينا أيضا قد احتل مكانه في جدران الخلية الذهبية والتي هي رقيقة جدا وغير ملحومة بما خلفها. وكل العناصر هي مشكلة بشكل صندوق ومحددة بمجموعات من الحبيبات.

en.name: Elements of a bracelet
description: This bracelet comprises four enamelled roundels, eight small spacers and a two bell-shaped elements that form a clasp. The four roundels are respectively enamelled with depictions of a bird facing right, another facing left, a trefoil and an undefined motif. The main colours are opaque orange-yellow, pale yellow, sealing–wax red, translucent royal blue and green. The enamel also holds in place the gold cell walls, which are very thin and not soldered to the backing. All the elements are box-constructed and bordered by clustres of granules.
