en.name: Dish
description: During the first half of the sixteenth century, artists of the royal design atelier of the Ottoman court developed a new decorative style characterized by its bright colours and naturalistic depiction of flowers. The floral composition on this dish with its tulips, carnations, and roses in red and blue on a white background is typical of the production of the Ottoman imperial kilns in the city of Iznik. Similar patterns of floral designs were used on textiles, carpets, book illuminations, and tiles, including some splendid examples in the Aga Khan Museum’s collection. The consistency of the Ottoman floral style helped establish a distinctive and singular visual brand for the Ottoman Empire and its arts. It is during this period that tulips caught Europe’s attention when they were first introduced there by Ogier Ghiselin de Busbecq, the Austrian ambassador to the Ottoman court.
keywords: Dish; ceramic; floral; tulip; Fritware; underglaze-painted

en.name: Carafe
description: This carafe, in a design known as the 'Well Spring', by the painter and writer Richard Redgrave (1804-1888), later Surveyor of the Queen's Pictures, was one of the designs made for Summerly's Art Manufactures. Summerly's Art Manufactures was a company founded by the educator Henry Cole in 1847, using the pseudonym Felix Summerly, hoping to promote public taste by recruiting well known artists to design functional objects. Redgrave made this design in 1847 and it was soon sold to A. J. F. Christy of the Stangate Glassworks in Lambeth, who produced it until 1850.

ar.name: أداة لخلع الأضراس.
description: القطعة عبارة عن أداة تشبه الملقاط تنتهي بحافة كانت في الأصل تشبه أسنان المنشار تمكن الطبيب من الإمساك بضرس المريض وهو متآكل. ويوجد حول وسطها حلقة معدنية تتحرك مع حركة الأداة. وحيث أن المسلمين الأوائل برعوا في الطب والجراحة بما فيها طب الأسنان، فإنهم ابتكروا العديد من الأدوات التي ساعدتهم على إتمام العمليات الجراحية المختلفة ومنها هذه الأداة. وقد كانت العمليات الجراحية تتضمن استخدام التخدير العام، فاستعملت مثلاً الاسفنجة المخدرة التي كانت توضع في عصير الحشيش والأفيون وست الحسن ثم تجفف في الشمس، ووقت الحاجة ترطب وتوضع على أنف المريض فتمتص الأنسجة المخاطية للمريض المواد المخدرة ليذهب المريض في نوم عميق يحرره من ألم العملية الجراحية. وكانت أدوات الجراحة تخضع لعمليات التعقيم حتى لا تنتقل العدوى من مريض لآخر، وخاصة في مجال جراحة الأسنان حيث يسهل انتشار العدوى. وقد توصل أبو بكر الرازي (251 – 313 هـ / 865 – 925 م) إلى تحضير مادة الكحول واستخدامها في تعقيم الأدوات الجراحية.

لم تقتصر براعة العرب المسلمين على تشخيص المرض، ووصف العلاج، بل تعدّى ذلك إلى ابتكار آلات تساعدهم على ممارسة الجراحة، بصفة عامة، وجراحة أمراض الفم، بصفة خاصة، كما استخدموا أنواعاً مختلفة من وسائل التخدير، وقاموا بتعقيم أدواتهم الجراحية.
keywords: أداة جراحة؛ طب؛ علوم؛ مستشفى؛ نحاس، نحاس مصبوب.

en.name: Implement to remove teeth.
description:
An implement similar to a pair of pliers that originally would have terminated with a saw-like edge, to facilitate a dentist in pulling, for instance, a septic tooth. The metal ring around the middle of the instrument would have moved and facilitated the doctor in manoeuvring the instrument, thus allowing him a better grip on the tooth. The early Muslims excelled in medicine and surgery, including dental medicine, and they created a number of instruments, which assisted them in carrying out different surgical operations, one of which is this.  
Surgical operations included the use of general anaesthesia. For example an anaesthetic sponge was used; soaked in hashish oil, opium and belladonna; it was then dried in the sun. When the time came it was moistened and placed on the nose of the patient where the tranquilizing substances were absorbed by the patient's tissues sending him into a deep sleep, and thereby ensuring that he remained free from pain during surgery. Surgical instruments were subjected to processes of sterilisation in order that infection would not be transferred from one patient to another, especially in dentistry where the spread of infection was more likely. At this time Abu Bakr al-Razi (AH 251–313 / AD 865-925) had already arrived at the discovery of the preparation of alcohol which was used in the sterilisation of surgical instruments.

Not only did Muslim physicians excel in diagnosis and treatment but they also invented tools that would help surgery in general and dentistry in particular. They used different kinds of anaesthetics and sterilised their surgical tools.
keywords: surgical instrument; surgery; medicine; sciences; hospital; cast copper

es.name: Extractor de dientes.
description:
Instrumento parecido a unas pinzas que quizá tuviera originalmente el extremo con dientes de sierra para facilitar a los dentistas la tarea de extraer, por ejemplo, una muela infectada. Es posible que el anillo de metal que se aprecia hacia la mitad del instrumento se desplazara para que resultase más sencillo de manejar y el médico pudiera agarrar mejor el diente. Los musulmanes, desde siempre, destacaron en la medicina y la cirugía, incluida la odontología, e inventaron varios instrumentos, como este, que les servían para realizar intervenciones.  
En las operaciones también se utilizaba anestesia general. Uno de los métodos empleados era una esponja anestésica empapada en aceite de hachís, opio y belladona que se dejaba secar al sol. Llegado el momento, se humedecía y se colocaba en la nariz del paciente, que absorbía las sustancias tranquilizantes y quedaba profundamente dormido, de modo que no sentía dolor durante la operación.  
El instrumental quirúrgico era sometido a procesos de esterilización para no contagiar infecciones entre pacientes, sobre todo en las intervenciones odontológicas, donde el contagio era más probable. En esta época, Abu Bakr al-Razi (251-313 / 865-925) ya había descubierto la preparación de alcohol, que se usaba para esterilizar el instrumental quirúrgico.

Los médicos musulmanes destacaron en el diagnóstico y el tratamiento de enfermedades y, además, inventaron instrumental quirúrgico que resultaba especialmente útil en la cirugía dental. Empleaban distintos tipos de anestesia y esterilizaban los instrumentos.
dates: Siglo III de la Hégira / IX d. C.
keywords: instrumento quirúrgico; medicina; ciencias; hospital; cobre fundido.

fr.name: Instrument pour l’arrachage des dents.
description:
Instrument semblable à une paire de tenailles, initialement terminé par une bordure en dents de scie et que l'on pouvait utiliser pour l'arrachage des dents. L'anneau de métal central est mobile pour permettre une meilleure prise de la dent. Les musulmans excellèrent très tôt dans les domaines de la médecine et de la chirurgie, y compris l'art dentaire, et créèrent un certain nombre d'instruments pour accomplir les différentes interventions mises au point.  
Les opérations chirurgicales faisaient déjà appel à l'anesthésie générale. On se servait alors d'une éponge imbibée d'un mélange d'huile de haschich, d'opium de ray-grass, de jusquiame et de belladone, mise à sécher au soleil puis humidifiée et placée sur le nez du patient pour l'insensibiliser. Les instruments étaient stérilisés pour éviter la transmission des infections, en particulier en dentisterie où le problème était évident. à cette époque, Abou Bakr al-Razi (251-313 H / 865-925 J.-C.) avait déjà découvert une préparation d'alcool utilisée à la stérilisation des instruments chirurgicaux.

Les médecins musulmans n'excellaient pas seulement dans le diagnostic et dans le traitement, ils inventaient également des instruments qui devaient aider la chirurgie en général et la dentisterie en particulier. Ils utilisaient différentes sortes d'anesthésiques et stérilisaient leurs instruments chirurgicaux.
dates: IIIe siècle de l’Hégire (IXe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Instruments chirurgicaux ; médecine ; sciences ; hôpitaux ; fonte de cuivre

en.name: Bosra Citadel
description:
As a major stronghold in the region and the palatial residence for the Ayyubid regent, the citadel became the focal point of the Islamic city. It was a Roman theatre transformed into a military structure by a series of constructions carried out during a period of more than 150 years. The initial period of alterations began under Gumushtagin in 481/1088, who built the two towers on top of the rectangular 9 m x 8 m stairwells flanking the scaena of the theatre, and consequently closed all the openings to the outside. Around 60 years later, the last Burid ruler of Damascus, Abu Sa‘id Abaq (534–49/1140–54), resumed the fortification extensions. He built the tower on the south-west façade of the cavea in 542/1147–8 in anticipation of a Crusader attack, as is evident from his epithet in the inscription: “qatil al-kafara wal-mushrikin”, “killer of the unbelievers and the polytheists”. These three towers from the first extension phase, covered in a simple and traditional way, have a flat roof of basalt-stone slabs supported by transverse arches.  
  
The second phase of fortification began with the Ayyubid ruler of Damascus, al-‘Adil Abu Bakr (r. 592–615/1196–1218). The towers, now erected at a considerable distance from the cavea proper, leave space for interior corridors and defence installations. Several antique structures from within the city must have been used for there is evidence of numerous spolia in this building phase. The additional towers, erected by al-‘Adil, are distinguished from earlier extensions by their considerably larger size, the construction technique of the outer walls and the barrel-vaulted roofs. The north-western tower measuring 22 m x 31 m was added in 599/1202–3, and was followed in 608–10/1211–13 by the two entrance towers. Passing these, the visitor finds himself in one of the defence alleyways around the theatre proper. Climbing the stairs one reaches the northern platform serving as an exhibition space for antique statues in front of tower. Together with tower, now accommodating the ethnographic collection, and tower that serves as archaeological museum, it belongs to the last, medieval, phase carried out to improve the citadel’s defences. All three towers are constructed in the splendid three-iwans mode, arranged around a central courtyard. Tower, since it is easy to reach from the entrance gate, might have served as a reception hall during the reign of al-Salih Isma‘il, who took up residence in the citadel.
keywords: Bosra; Bosra Citadel; Bosra Theatre; Ayyubid period
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Museums and Antiquities

de.name: Deckengemälde *Das letzte Abendmahl*
description: Die Kuppel über dem Chor stellt das letzte Abendmahl dar, den Ursprung des eucharistischen Sakraments. Eine nach oben geöffnete Scheinarchitektur in Gestalt eines ovalen Baus mit Arkadenöffnungen und umlaufender Pilastergliederung gibt den Rahmen des Geschehens ab, das oberhalb steiler Stufen auf einer wenig raumhaltigen Bühne präsentiert wird. Die eigentliche Abendmahlsszene mit Jesus zwischen den Jüngern an einem langgestreckten Tisch ist genrehaft erweitert. Die kühle Farbigkeit, die verhältnismäßig nüchterne Schilderung des Geschehens und die Strenge der Architektur sind deutliche Zeichen des Frühklassizismus, dem der an Martin Knoller  - insbesondere das Abendmahlsfresko in Neresheim - anknüpfende Keller weit deutlicher als die beiden anderen Freskanten verpflichtet war.

en.name: Ceiling painting *Last Supper*
description: The cupola above the choir depicts the last supper as the origin of the Eucharist sacrament. Illusionistic architecture, open at the top, in the form of an oval building with arcades, provides the setting for the scene which is presented on a narrow stage at the top of steep stairs. The scene of the Last Supper has genre-like additions. The cool colours, the relatively sober depiction of the scene and the austere architecture are clear features of the Early Classicism which Keller, drawing on Martin Knoller, was far more indebted to than the other two fresco artists.

This was then used in a publication (of exceptional quality and execution) entitled Description de l'Égypte, in which the observations and enquiries made by the military expedition in Egypt were collected. The collection comprises of 10 volumes of illustrations and 9 volumes of texts published betwen 1809 and 1826.

Les notes et dessins servent ensuite à une publication exceptionnelle de par sa qualité et son exécution, intitulée *Description de l'Égypte, ou Recueil des observations et des recherches qui ont été faites en Égypte pendant l'expédition de l'Armée française*. en.name: Villa Abdellatif
description:
The oldest document concerning this villa dates back to 1226 / 1715, and mentions its various owners, including Sid Abdellatif, the last one, who purchased it in 1209 / 1795.  
  
After being rented out, in 1905 the villa was made available to certain artists sponsored by the French Ministry of Fine Arts, who took advantage of their two years of study to reside there. Its ideal location in a lush setting halfway up the hill of the Hamma District provides views of the entire Algerian panorama from the gardens and the house.  
  
The access road to the villa is bordered on the right by an imposing building that housed studios for the artists boarding in the villa. Very high ceilings with skylights provided all the light needed for their work. This section includes necessary additions built to meet the new artistic mission of the villa.  
  
On the left, a small pavilion houses an ornamental pond that residents called the “women’s pool”. At the end of the road is the entrance to the residence, which is surrounded by a wall. The inner courtyard, bordered on its left by a gallery with a double row of arcades on fluted columns, extends the entire length of the wall and serves as a summer reception room.  
  
It faces the entrance to the residence, a large porch supported by twelve columns and housing an entrance door decorated with rivets and a bronze knocker. The rectangular vestibule has several long, dark, vaulted spaces that could be used as storage rooms or shops.  
  
The majestic staircase leads to a patio on the upper floor that has traditional galleries on all sides. These are lined with arcades of columns and decorated with faïence (glazed tiles). The tall doors open onto rooms with deep recesses and large windows that overlook the garden and the bay. This is a typical house of the Algerian *Fahs* (countryside): airy, open, with an inner courtyard and a summer pavilion in front of the house.  
  
The proximity of the Museum of Fine Arts of Algiers could only have made the prospect of lodging in this villa even more attractive to the sponsored artists

fr.name: Villa Abdellatif
description:
Le plus ancien document la concernant remonte à 1226/1715 et fait allusion à ses différents propriétaires dont le dernier, Sid Abdellatif, qui en fit l’acquisition en 1209/1795.  
  
Après avoir été louée, elle fut, en 1905, mise à la disposition des artistes peintres boursiers du ministère français des Beaux-Arts qui profitaient ainsi de leurs deux années d’étude pour résider dans cette villa au séjour enchanteur.  
  
Sa situation privilégiée dans un cadre de verdure et à mi-hauteur de la colline du quartier du Hamma lui permet de jouir, dans les jardins comme dans la maison, de l’entier panorama algérois.  
  
Le chemin d’accès à la villa est bordé sur sa droite par une imposante bâtisse qui abrite les salles servant d’ateliers de travail aux artistes pensionnaires de la villa. Des plafonds très hauts, à verrière, dispensent le maximum de lumière nécessaire à leurs travaux. Toute cette partie correspond à des adjonctions rendues nécessaires pour répondre à la nouvelle vocation de la villa.  
  
Sur la gauche, un petit pavillon abrite une pièce d’eau ornementale que les pensionnaires de la villa dénommaient le “bassin des femmes”.  
  
Au bout du chemin, on accède à l’entrée de la demeure, enclavée dans le mur d’enceinte. On se trouve alors dans la cour intérieure, bordée sur sa gauche par une galerie à double rangée d’arcades sur colonnettes cannelées qui occupe toute la longueur du mur et fait office de salon de réception d’été.  
  
Lui fait face le porche d’entrée de la demeure, sorte d’avant-corps de dimensions imposantes supporté par douze colonnes et abritant une porte d’entrée à clous et heurtoir de bronze.  
  
Le vestibule, rectangulaire, présente plusieurs salles voûtées, longues et sombres, pouvant faire office de caves ou de magasins.  
  
L’escalier majestueux mène au patio situé à l’étage qui présente, traditionnellement, les quatre galeries bordées d’arcades à colonnes et décorées de faïence. Les hautes portes donnent accès aux chambres à renfoncement marqué et largement percées de fenêtres ayant vue sur le jardin et la baie.  
  
Nous avons là l’exemple type de la maison du Fahs algérois, aérée, ouverte, avec cour intérieure et pavillon d’été devant la maison.  
  
La présence du Musée des Beaux-arts d’Alger, tout proche de la villa, ne pouvait qu’ajouter à l’intérêt du séjour des peintres dans la villa.

en.name: *The Blessed Franco Resurrecting a Child*
description:
This picture is part of a series hanging on three of the walls of the sacristy of the Carmelite church of Medicina, a town near Bologna. The cycle is well documented and so it is known exactly when each picture was hung on the wall. The attribution is certain: the architectural details were painted by Fra Ferdinando da Bologna, one of the best pupils of Ferdinando Bibiena. Originally, the figures were missing and the paintings were incomplete. In 1753, the Carmelite fathers asked the painter Nicola Bertuzzi from Ancona to complete Dal Buono architecture with the stories of the blessed Franco, who lived in the thirteenth-century.  
The picture of the *Miracle of the Resurrection of the Child* hangs above the entrance door of the sacristy. The scene takes place inside a great baroque church. The blessed Franco, with a penitential helmet on his head, answers the prayer of the little boy's mother and resuscitates him. The scene occupies the middle of the painting and is introduced by the wonder of a Carmelite brother, followed by a dog. The vivid description of the architectural details is made through a one-point corner perspective on the left. The luminosity of the central episode is emphasised by the dynamic lights and shades inside the scenography. In the background, Bertuzzi depicts some of the daily activities of the religious order such as confession and communion, that complete naturally the resurrection of the child. The culture of the Bibienas' is strongly evident, combined with the refined culture of Fra Ferdinando and the skilled work of Bertuzzi. The powerful scenic invention combines Bibienesque schemes with views of existing architecture reflective of the Carmelite Church of Medicina and the interior of the Cathedral of Ferrara. The decorative architecture, the vivid colours and the delicate lights are typical of a baroque taste moving towards Rococo.

This painting was commissioned by the Carmelite community of Medicina in 1751 to the Bolognese painter Vincenzo Dal Buono also known as Fra’ Ferdinando da Bologna, a pupil of Ferdinando Bibiena. Nicola Bertuzzi added the stories of the blessed Franco at a later time.  
In the middle of the picture, the blessed, with the penitential helmet on his head, is resuscitating a child. The lively description of architecture is seen through a corner perspective with a vanishing point on the left, a typical feature of the Bibienas’.
holder: Parish church of San Mamante, Medicina
artist: Fra Ferdinando da Bologna (Vincenzo Dal Buono) (1704, Bologna – 1784, Bologna), Nicola Bertuzzi (1710, Ancona – 1777, Bologna)
School of the Bibienas’; Bolognese Late baroque
keywords: Pendant; Carmelite; Religious; Fra Ferdinando da Bologna; Vincenzo Dal Buono; Nicola Bertuzzi; Bibiena; corner perspective; scenography

it.name: *Il beato Franco ottiene la resurrezione di un bambino*
description: La tempera fa parte delle tele collocate nelle tre pareti libere della sacrestia del Carmine di Medicina. Il ciclo è ben documentato tanto da rivelarci la data di collocazione *in situ* di ogni singolo quadro. L'attribuzione è quanto mai sicura, per le architetture si evidenzia la mano di Fra Ferdinando da Bologna, uno dei migliori allievi di Ferdinando Bibiena. Inizialmente le pitture furono consegnate non ancora ultimate, nell'attesa che un altro pittore le completasse con le figure. Ciò avvenne nel 1753, quando i padri carmelitani fecero ultimare le architetture del Dal Buono all'anconetano Nicola Bertuzzi, illustrando le storie duecentesche del Beato Franco. La tela con *Il miracolo della resurrezione del bambino* è collocata sopra la porta d'ingresso della sacrestia. L'episodio si svolge all'interno di una grande chiesa barocca, dove il Beato Franco, con in capo il casco penitenziale, esaudisce il desiderio della madre del piccolo e lo resuscita. La scena posta al centro della composizione è introdotta dallo stupore di un confratello carmelitano, seguito da un cane. La viva descrizione dei particolari architettonici  si costruisce attraverso una prospettiva angolare, con il punto di fuga verso sinistra. La luminosità invasiva dell'episodio centrale viene esaltata attraverso il dinamico gioco di luci e ombre che si svolge all'interno di una scenografia dilatata. Sullo sfondo il Bertuzzi ritrae alcune scenette caratteristiche dell'attività quotidiana dell'ordine come la confessione o la comunione, compendio naturale alla resurrezione del bimbo, delicata nella fascinazione dei gesti e perfettamente inserita nello spazio. La cultura dei Bibiena emerge prepotentemente anche se non mancano i caratteri autonomi che traspaiono dalla sofisticata cultura di Fra Ferdinando e dal sapiente accostamento dell'opera del Bertuzzi. La potente invenzione scenica degli schemi tradizionali della produzione bibienesca, simile a opere quali il *Gabinetto Reale* e l'*Atrio magnifico*, viene rimeditata attraverso un accattivante realismo pre-illuminista che sembra citare sia la stessa chiesa del Carmine che l'imponenza della cattedrale di Ferrara del Mazzarelli. La componente decorativa delle architetture e il vivace cromatismo si esplicano nella trattazione di una resa delicata e vivace delle luci in un gusto in parte ancora Barocco che transita verso il pieno Rococò.

La tela collocata sopra la porta d'entrata della sacrestia della chiesa olivetana del Carmine di Medicina, venne commissionata dalla comunità monastica locale nel 1751 al pittore bolognese Dal Buono Vincenzo meglio noto come Fra' Ferdinando da Bologna, allievo di Ferdinando Bibiena. La potente costruzione delle architetture dipinte, tipica dell'opera della famiglia di artisti e scenografi bolognesi dei Bibiena, emerge prepotentemente. Allo stesso tempo però l'invenzione creativa che caratterizza gran parte delle loro opere, tende a sposarsi, nella rappresentazione monumentale dell'interno di una chiesa gotica, con un realismo razionalista di matrice pienamente settecentesca. Le architetture del frate bolognese vennero successivamente completate con le storie del Beato Franco dal pittore anconetano Nicola Bertuzzi. La storia è rappresentata con un forte accento luministico soprattutto nel centro dove si narra la vicenda del Beato, che, cinto dal casco penitenziale, resuscita un bambino. Sullo sfondo si muovono le figure dei carmelitani intenti nelle quotidiane attività religiose. La scena viene introdotta dallo stupore di un monaco, seguito da un cane, la cui ombra scorciata si staglia sul pavimento. La viva descrizione dei particolari architettonici e la controllata trattazione delle figure, sono costruite attraverso una prospettiva angolare con un punto di fuga verso sinistra, caratteristica scenografica della produzione bibienesca.
holder: Sacrestia della chiesa carmelitana del Carmine, Medicina
artist: Fra Ferdinando da Bologna (Vincenzo Dal Buono) (1704, Bologna – 1784, Bologna); Nicola Bertuzzi (1710, Ancona – 1777, Bologna)
Scuola dei  Bibiena; Tardo barocco bolognese
keywords: Pendant; Carmelitani; Religioso; Fra Ferdinando da Bologna; Vincenzo Dal Buono; Nicola Bertuzzi; Bibiena; prospettiva d'angolo; scenografia

ar.name: زبدية مزججة بطلاء براق
description: القطعة هي وعاء للنبيذ مزينة بصورة لزوج وعليها أنخاب وتبريكات. وتقنية الإنتاج المستخدمة في هذه الزبدية هي الطلاء البراق مع الرسم فوق الزجاج. ومطلي داخل الزبدية العميقة زوج من الأشخاص الجالسين المستوحين من التذهيب الفارسي والشخص الأنثى تحمل كأسا. والشريط المحيطي الواقع على حافة الزبدية تحمل نقوشا التي تشير لشرب الخمر مما يؤكد وظيفة الزبدية.وهذا هو مثال ممتاز عن الخزف المزجج بواسطة الطلاء البراق المعدني والذي تطور في إيران. وفي أواخر القرن الثاني عشر فإن مواضيع مثل مشاهد الصيد والأشكال البشرية التي تشرب الخمر تظهر كتزيينات على القطع. والزبدية ذات القاعدة الحلقية العالية والتزيين التفصيلي المعقد في الجانب الخلفي هي نمطية للأوعية المنتجة في كاشان حيث ازدهرت صناعة الخزف ذو الطلاء البراق في هذه الفترة.والتأثيرات الذهبية المعدنية تتشكل بواسطة الطلاء بأكسيد الذهب والفضة والذي ينصهر خلال مرحلة الشي الثانية .ونصوص النقوش المكتوبة على الزبدية هي كالتالي :مباركة :المجد والسعادة والعظمة والفرح لا تبتعد عن مالك هذه الزبدية هذا الشعر من قبل مالك فخر الدين مبقرش غوري:أنت تقول : لماذا دموعك بلون الورود؟لأنك سألت فإني سأخبرك كيف كان ذلك :الدموع المصبوغة بالدم قد سكبت شغفا بك ولأن قلبي اهتاج فإن دموعي أصبحت تغلي.نخب :الله ، خالق العالم ، ليحمي مالك هذا الوعاء أينما ذهب . شعر  لشاعر مجهول: وجهك دائما أمام عيني أيها المحبوب ، افعل ما يبدو جيدا لكآه ، من الروح والعالم ، يالقلبي السعيد عندما يمكنك أن تراه فقط فمن يكون قد رآكشعر من أفضال الدين كاشاني:آه ، ياسيدي لا تتوقع المساعدة من أي أحد.لا تبحث عن الظل تحت غصن بلا أوراق يحوز المرء المجد عن طريق الرزانة والازدراء عبر الجشع كن سعيدا بمجدك وتجنب الجشع.( الترجمة من قبل محسى ناريماني)
keywords: سلجوقي ، خزف براق ، كاشان

en.name: Lustre glazed bowl
description:
The object is a wine bowl decorated with an image of a couple and with toasts and blessings. The technique used for producing this bowl is lustre with overglaze painting. Painted inside the deep bowl is a pair of seated figures, inspired by Persian illumination; the female figure holds a glass. The circumferential strip edging the bowl bears inscriptions which refer to wine drinking, confirming the vessel's function. It is an excellent example of ceramic glazed with metallic lustre, which was developed in Iran. In the late 12th century, subjects such as hunting scenes and human figures drinking wine appeared as decorations on objects. The bowl, with its high foot ring and the intricately-detailed decoration in the background, is typical for the wares produced in Kashan, where the lustre industry flourished in this period. The metallic, golden effect is created by painting with silver and copper oxide, which melts during the second firing. Excerpts from the inscriptions:  
Blessing:  
Honour and gladness, greatness and joy  
Be not distant from the owner of this bowl.  
Poem by Malek Fakhreddin Mubaraksah Guri:  
You said: Why were your tears the color of roses?  
Because you asked, I will tell you how it was:  
The blood-tinged tears surged up out of passion for you,  
And as my heart seethed, they boiled over.  
Toast:  
God, Creator of the World, protect the owner of this bowl wherever he goes.  
Poem by an unknown poet:  
Your face is always before my eyes.  
Beloved, do what seems right to you.  
Oh, soul and world, my heart is content,  
When it can only see him who has seen you.  
Poem by Afdaleddin Kashani:  
Oh Lord, do not expect help from any man!  
Do not look for shade under a branch without leaves.  
One wins honour through sobriety and contempt through greed.  
Be content with your honour and eschew contempt.
keywords: Seljuk; Lustre-Ceramic; Kashan
materials: Fritware; lustre painting on a tin glaze
tags: lustre painting on a tin glaze

en.name: Various hydraulic machines used in Egypt to water the land. The first method is constructed in a linear manner and provides the land with water whenever it is in need. Part of "Dyke A"
names: Illustrations taken from *Voyage d'Egypte et de Nubie*
short_description: The captain of the Danish Royal Marines Fréderic-Louis Norden (1708–1742) was sent to Egypt to draw monuments. His collection, *Voyage d’Égypte et de Nubie*, was published posthumously in 1755, and was added to in 1795 by the inclusion of scientific commentaries by Louis Langlès (1763–1824), founder of the École Spéciale des Langues Orientales and curator of oriental manuscripts at the Bibliothèque Impériale. This new edition, a product of Europen "Egyptomania", introduced some splendid new illustrations. In this particular page, the artist has focused on traditional hydraulic machinery.
keywords: Irrigation; dams; Egypt

en.name: Plan of Jerusalem
short_description: Plan of the area to the South of the Haram al-Sharif, Jerusalem, showing the location of the shafts dug by Lieut. Charles Warren, R.E., and his team to explore the topography of ancient Jerusalem. This work established the history of the development of the Old City of Jerusalem. While engaged in this work, Warren also carried out a major study of the economy of Jerusalem in the period 1867–1870, which was published in the SWP in 1884.

de.name: Der Krönungsmantel
description:
Der halbkreisförmig geschnittene Mantel aus rotem Samit (geritzte Seide) ist mit einer aufwendigen Goldstickerei versehen, die einen zentralen Palmbaum (=Lebensbaum) zeigt, zu dessen linker und rechter Seite sich spiegelbildliche Darstellungen eines Löwen befinden, der ein mit Sattel und Zaumzeug ausgerüstetes, also domestiziertes Kamel besiegt.  
Entlang der geraden Seite des Halbkreises ist der Mantel bordürenartig mit Perlen und Gold bestickt sowie mit 31 Emailplättchen (von byzantinischen Einflüssen geprägtes Zellenschmelzemail) besetzt. Die halbkreisförmige Kante des Mantels ist mit einer *Kufi*\-Inschrift in Gold bestickt. Ihr ist zu entnehmen, dass der Mantel 133/34 zur Regierungszeit des sizilianischen Königs Rogers II. in den königlichen Hofwerkstätten zu Palermo angefertigt wurde.  
Als Teil des normannischen Schatzes gelangte der Mantel auf dem Erbweg an die Hohenstaufer und wurde schließlich Bestandteil der Krönungsgewänder der Könige und Kaiser des Heiligen Römischen Reiches.
materials: Samit, Seide, Gold, Perlen, Email, Filigran, Edelsteine, Brettchenborte
tags: Samit, Seide, Gold, Perlen, Email, Filigran, Edelsteine, Brettchenborte

en.name: Coronation mantle
description:
The precious mantle embroidered with gold, pearls and cloisonné-enamelled plaques was part of the set of robes used at the coronations of the kings and emperors of the Holy Roman Empire. The semicircular edge of the mantle is decorated with a gold-embroidered *kufic* inscription. It reveals that the mantle was produced in AH 528/ AD 1133/34 during the reign of the Norman king Roger II of Sicily (AD 1095–1154) in the royal workshops in Palermo where among others Arabic artisans worked.  
Ancient motifs are depicted on the surface of the semicircular mantle: to both sides of a palm-tree (representing the tree of life) a lion triumph over a camel, which has a saddle and bridle and has thus been domesticated.
keywords: Siculo-Norman; textile; embroidery; workshop; royal manufacture; figurative decoration; tree of life; Sicily; Roger II

en.name: Mulay Idriss Mausoleum
description:
A large white village attached to the side of the Zerhun mountain, the mausoleumtown dominates the surrounding plateau and looks over towards the Roman ruins of Volubilis. It is a small town, famous because it holds the mausoleum of the prince who founded the first Muslim Moroccan dynasty. Mulay Idriss Ibn ‘Abd Allah, the fifth descendant of the Prophet’s son-in-law ‘Ali, escaping the wars fought between the Abbassids and the Umayyads in Arabia, came to Morocco, where he was welcomed as the descendant of the Prophet’s family. The local Berber prince of Walili, who had rallied himself behind Islam, called upon the tribes to follow the *shorfa* (sg. *Sharif*). But Mulay Idriss’ premature death in 176/793, without doubt the result of being poisoned on the orders of the Abbassid Caliph, did not leave him with sufficient time to give his dynasty the structure he would have wanted to give it. Before his death he had married a Berber called Kenza who was to bear him a son posthumously. He was called Idriss the Second and continued the work of his father.  
mausoleum with its own dome, became the place of a saint venerated by Moroccans. The monument remained more or less unchanged until the 11th/17th century, when the ‘Alawite Sultan Mulay Isma‘il gave the order to demolish it and to buy the neighbouring properties in order to add them to the mausoleum. Building works lasted nearly three years, from 1131/1719–1133/1721. Mulay Isma‘il ordained it with the Friday prayer, a sign of the importance which was given to the mausoleum and to Mulay Idriss Zerhoun’s town.  
In 1237/1822, the ‘Alawite Sultan Mulay ‘Abd al-Rahman took his turn at enlarging and embellishing the mausoleum: he bought the house next to the dome which stood between this monument and the *qaysariya*, and demolished it in order to build an even bigger and more beautiful mosque. The mausoleum of the saint was thus decorated again.  
The dome was embellished with gorgeous ceramics by the Grand *m‘allem* (an artisan who qualified in ceramics in Meknès) Ibn Makhluf during the reign of the Sultan Sidi Mohamed (1859–1873).  
Sultan Mohamed V (1927–1961) and his son King Hassan II (1929–1999) initiated the redecoration of the *Darih*, the mausoleum, and once again enlarged the mosque. To this day, Mulay Idriss is the object every year of a large pilgrimage which takes place on the occasion of the saint’s *Mussem*. Numerous tribes then come into the mausoleum to pray.  
The veil, richly decorated with golden embroidery, which covers up the saint’s catafalque, is changed once a year or once every two years amidst a religious ceremony in which the political and religious authorities of the country or of the region participate.  
It is a veritable celebration full of song, full of the odour of perfume and of sacrifices, and of the noise of gunfire, during which pilgrims fill the town in a long procession.

es.name: Mausoleo de Mulay Idris Zerhun
description:
La ciudad-mausoleo —un gran pueblo blanco incrustado en la montaña de Zerhun, célebre porque alberga la tumba del príncipe que fundó la primera dinastía marroquí musulmana— domina la meseta circundante y mira hacia las ruinas romanas de Volubilis.  
Mulay Idris Ibn Abdallah, quinto descendiente de Alí, yerno del profeta, vino a Marruecos huyendo de las guerras libradas en Arabia entre abbasíes y omeyas. Aquí fue acogido con los honores que le correspondían por su linaje, y el príncipe beréber de Walili, que se había adherido al Islam, hizo un llamamiento a las tribus para que siguieran al *cherif*. Pero la muerte prematura de Mulay Idris en el 176/793, sin duda envenenado por orden del califa abbasí, no le dejó tiempo para dar a su nueva dinastía la estructura deseada. Sin embargo, poco antes de morir había contraído matrimonio con una beréber de Kenza, quien le dio un hijo póstumo que, bajo el nombre de Idris II, continuaría su obra.  
La tumba de Idris padre, construida como mausoleo con cúpula, se convirtió en un lugar santo, venerado por los marroquíes. El monumento no cambió prácticamente nada hasta el siglo XI/XVII, cuando el sultán Mulay Ismail dio la orden de demolerlo y de comprar las propiedades vecinas para unirlas al mismo. Los trabajos duraron casi tres años (1131/1719-1133/1721). Mulay Ismail dispuso hacer allí la plegaria del viernes, lo que da muestra de la importancia que tenían el mausoleo y la villa de Mulay Idris Zerhun. En 1237/1822, el sultán alauí Mulay Abderrahman también la hizo ampliar y embellecer: compró la casa vecina, situada entre el monumento y la *qaysariyya*, y la derribó para edificar una mezquita todavía más grande y hermosa, a la vez que decoró de nuevo el mausoleo del santo.  
Posteriormente, en tiempos del sultán Mulay Mohamed (1859-1873), la cúpula fue adornada con bellas cerámicas del gran *m‘allem* (artesano cualificado) de Mequinez, Ibn Majluf.  
El sultán Mohamed V (1927-1961) y su hijo, el rey Hassan II (1929-1999) ordenaron rehacer la decoración del *Darih* (mausoleo) y agrandaron una vez más la mezquita.  
Todavía hoy numerosas tribus vienen a orar ante el mausoleo, con ocasión de la gran peregrinación que se celebra cada año el día del *Musem* (fiesta patronal) del santo. El manto —ricamente decorado con bordados dorados— que recubre el catafalco se cambia una vez al año o cada dos años, en una ceremonia en la que participan las autoridades políticas y religiosas del país o de la región. Es una verdadera fiesta llena de cantos, perfumes, sacrificios y salvas de fusil, durante la cual los peregrinos recorren la villa en procesión.

fr.name: Mausolée Moulay Idriss Zerhoun
description:
Gros village blanc accroché à la montagne du Zerhoun, la cité-mausolée domine le plateau environnant et regarde vers les ruines romaines de Volubilis. C’est une petite ville, célèbre parce qu’elle abrite le mausolée du prince ayant fondé la première dynastie marocaine musulmane. Moulay Idriss Ibn Abdallah, cinquième descendant d’Ali, gendre du Prophète, fuyant les guerres entre Abbassides et Omeyyades en Arabie, est venu au Maroc où il fut accueilli comme le descendant de la famille du Prophète. Le prince berbè- re local de Oualili, qui s’était rallié à l’islam, appela les tribus à suivre le Chérif. Mais la mort prématurée de Moulay Idriss, en 176/793, sans doute empoisonné par ordre du Calife abbasside, ne lui laissa pas le temps de donner à sa nouvelle dynastie la structure qu’il aurait voulu. Avant son décès il avait épousé une Berbère du nom de Kenza qui lui donna un fils posthume. Celui-ci portera le nom d’Idriss le second, et continuera l’oeuvre de son père.  
Le tombeau d’Idriss le père, construit en mausolée avec sa coupole, devint un lieu saint, vénéré par les Marocains. Le monument ne changea pratiquement pas jusqu’au XIe/XVIIe siècle, lorsque le sultan alaouite Moulay Ismaïl donna l’ordre de le démolir et d’acheter les propriétés avoisinantes pour les adjoindre au mausolée. Les travaux durèrent près de trois années, 1131/1719-1133/1721. Moulay Ismaïl y ordonna la prière du vendredi, signe de l’importance donnée au mausolée et à la ville de Moulay Idriss Zerhoun.  
En 1237/1822, le sultan alaouite Moulay Abderrahman le fit agrandir et embellir à son tour: il acheta la maison voisine à la coupole, entre ce monument et la *qaysariya*, et la fit démolir pour y édifier une mosquée encore plus belle et plus large. Le mausolée du saint fut alors décoré de nouveau.  
La coupole sera agrémentée de belles céramiques, au temps du sultan Sidi Mohamed (1859-1873), par le grand *m‘allem*, artisan qualifié de la céramique à Meknès, Ibn Makhlouf.  
Le sultan Mohamed V (1927-1961), et son fils, le roi Hassan II (1929-1999), firent refaire les décorations du *Dharih*, mausolée, et élargirent une fois de plus la mosquée.  
Aujourd’hui encore, Moulay Idriss est chaque année l’objet d’un grand pèlerinage à l’occasion du *Moussem* du saint. De nombreuses tribus viennent alors prier dans le mausolée.  
L’habit richement décoré de broderies dorées qui recouvre le catafalque du saint est changé une fois l’an ou tous les deux ans, accompagné de cérémonies religieuses auxquelles participent les autorités politiques et religieuses du pays ou de la région.  
C’est une véritable fête pleine de chants, de l’odeur du parfum et des sacrifices et du bruit des coups de fusils, pendant laquelle les pèlerins remplissent la ville, en une grande procession.

en.name: Wooden clogs
short_description: Wooden clogs such as these have a long history in the Middle East, emerging before the Middle Ages and remaining popular for centuries to come. They were made of a variety of woods, including walnut, apricot, willow, poplar, or beech. The wood was cut into wedge shapes then moulded around the foot of the wearer. Excess wood was then shaved off, the heel attached, and the wood painted and polished. Leather girdles in a variety of colours were fixed to the heel with special nails and the wood would often be decorated with mosaics of bone or seashells organised in geometric or floral patterns. Clogs were designed to be comfortable and resistant to water, and thus were usually worn at home, particularly by women. These shoes have a higher heel than usual and would be worn by brides so that they would appear taller than the other girls in the *hammam* (Turkish baths).
keywords: Shoes; Woodwork; Fashion

en.name: Flask
description: This glass flask is commonly referred to as a pilgrim flask, based on its association with similarly shaped vessels made in both leather and metal that were brought back by pilgrims returning from the Holy Land during the Crusades. Made of free-blown glass, this example has two flat sides — referred to in Italian documents as *botacio fracado, inghistera fracada* (in Venice, meaning “flat-sided bottle”) – with two small loop handles attached. The overall shape of this flask bears a strong resemblance to glass vessels made by the Mamluks during the seventh and eighth centuries AH / thirteenth and fourteenth centuries AD. Venice had long been on the receiving end of the Islamic glass industry, whether importing raw materials for glasswork or finished objects from Egypt and Syria. This particular flask takes inspiration in both its shape and enamel decoration from its Mamluk precursors, such as the small, flat-sided perfume sprinkler known as a *qumqum*. The flask’s enamel decoration, a technique which Mamluk glassworkers excelled in, was only taken up by Italian craftsmen around 864 AH / 1460 AD, when the island of Murano developed as Europe’s leading glass industry.
keywords: Glass; Flask; Free-blown; Enamelled; Renaissance

ar.name: صندوق عاج.
description: صندوق عاجي بزخارف سوداء وذهبية على جوانبه كلِّها ما عدا الجانب السفلي. رُسمت على الغطاء خمس رصائع دائرية الشكل، تحتوي على أسد وطاووسين وغزالين؛ يُرى بينها خمسة طيور تحمل أزهاراً. ويوجد على الجانب الأمامي رصيعتان من الأرابيسك، كما يوجد على كل من الجانبين والخلف رسوم متكررة لطيرين يطوقان رصيعة تحتوي على أسد. أُعيد تأطير الصندوق بقالب خشبي بعد أن ابتاعه السيد وليام بيريل. أما القفل والكتائف النحاسية المذهَّبة، الملحقة في الأصل، فتساعد على تدعيم هيكل الصندوق المصنوع من صفائح عاجية رقيقة معشَّقة بأوتاد من العظم. إن تصميم وأسلوب موضوع الرسوم نمطيان في هذا الطراز من الصناديق، ومستلهمان من تشكيلة من العناصر البيزنطية والإسلامية، وقد نفَّذها حرفيون مسلمون لبيعها إلى زبائن مسيحيين في صقلية النورمندية.

هذه العلبة، التي صنعها حرفيون مسلمون، لزبائن مسيحيين في صقلية النورماندية، مستوحاة من عناصر زخرفية بيزنطية وإسلامية مختلفة. وأعداد كبيرة من هذه العلب المثمَّنة، لمادتها من ناحية، ومستواها الفني من ناحية ثانية، ظلَّت باقية في عدد من الكنائس المسيحية، حيث كانت تستعمل أوانٍ للقربان المقدس.
keywords: تجارة؛ شكل حيواني؛ أرابيسك.

en.name: Ivory box.
description: An ivory box with black and gold decoration on all sides except for the underside. Painted on the lid are five circular medallions containing a lion, two peacocks and two gazelles; between them are five birds with flowers. On the front side are two medallions with arabesque decorations. On each of the two sides and on the back there is an arrangement of two birds that flank a medallion which contains a lion. The box was re-lined with a wooden frame after it was purchased by Sir William Burrell. The once gilded brass brackets and lock help support the structure of the box, which is made of thin ivory plates held together with bone pegs. Both the design and style of the painted motifs are typical of this type of box, inspired by a combination of Byzantine and Islamic elements, and made by Muslim craftsmen for Christian customers in Norman Sicily.

Made by Muslim craftsmen for Christian customers in Norman Sicily, this box is inspired by a combination of Byzantine and Islamic decorative elements. Valued for their material and artistic quality, many such boxes have survived in Christian churches where they were used as reliquaries.

es.name: Caja de marfil.
description:
Caja de marfil decorada en negro y dorado en todas sus caras excepto la inferior. En la tapa aparecen pintados cinco medallones con un león, dos pavos reales y dos gacelas; entre ellos hay cinco pájaros con flores. En el frente presenta dos medallones con decoración de arabescos. Ambos laterales y la parte posterior presentan la misma composición: dos aves que flanquean un medallón con un león en su interior. La caja fue reforzada con un alma de madera después que la adquiriera sir William Burrell. Sujetan la estructura herrajes y una cerradura, en latón y originalmente dorados. Las placas de marfil están unidas con estaquillas de hueso.  
Tanto el dibujo como el estilo de los motivos pintados son típicos de este tipo de cajas y se inspiran en una combinación de elementos bizantinos e islámicos. Artesanos musulmanes las fabricaban para clientes cristianos de la Sicilia normanda.

Caja fabricada por artesanos musulmanes para clientes cristianos de la Sicilia normanda. Su decoración se inspira en elementos bizantinos e islámicos. Estas cajas eran muy valoradas por su calidad artística y la de sus materiales. Se han conservado muchos ejemplos como este en iglesias cristianas, donde se utilizaban como relicarios.
dates: Siglo VI de la Hégira / XII d. C.
keywords: comercio; imaginería zoomórfica; decoración en arabesco.
materials: Placas de marfil pintadas; herrajes de cobre.

fr.name: Coffret.
description: Coffret en ivoire à décor noir et or appliqué sur toutes ses faces sauf le dessous. Sur le couvercle sont peints cinq médaillons circulaires contenant un lion, deux paons et deux gazelles, séparés par cinq oiseaux et des fleurs. Sur le devant figurent deux médaillons à décor d'arabesques. Sur les deux côtés et au dos, une composition à deux oiseaux flanque un médaillon contenant un lion. Ce coffret a été intérieurement doublé d'un cadre en bois après son acquisition par Sir William Burrell. Les ferrures et la fermeture, jadis dorées, renforcent la structure de l'ensemble composé de minces plaques d'ivoire tenues par des chevilles en os. La conception comme le style des motifs peints sont typiques des coffrets marqués par une combinaison d'éléments byzantins et islamiques que réalisaient des artisans musulmans pour des clients chrétiens de la Sicile normande.

Fabriqué par des ouvriers musulmans pour des clients chrétiens en Sicile normande, ce coffret est marqué par une combinaison d’éléments décoratifs byzantins et islamiques. Très appréciés pour leurs matériaux et leurs qualités artistiques, de nombreux coffrets semblables furent conservés dans des églises chrétiennes, où ils étaient utilisés comme reliquaires.

en.name: *Bust of Clement XII*
description:
Pietro Bracci produced a large number of works, mainly portraits. He was one of the most important late Baroque sculptors of the 18th century in Rome, and was involved in the creation of the Trevi Fountain. He was trained in the Baroque tradition based on the work of Gian Lorenzo Bernini and classical equilibrium.  
There is no documentary evidence linking the bust to the sculptor, nor any explicit references in the work-log that Bracci was in the habit of keeping after 1725, but the attribution is generally accepted by scholars.  
It is dated around the time of the pontificate of Clement XII Corsini, which lasted from 1730 to 1740, although it is possible that the bust was made after his death.  
The ageing face of the pope is sculpted faithfully, reproducing the lines infused with deep expressiveness and intelligence, key characteristics of the artist's portraits. The pontificate's vestments are finely decorated and tied at the chest, while the fur-trimmed cloak and underlying *mozzetta*  
(a short elbow length cape worn by Catholic clergy) are sculpted to achieve an elegant volume of folds that create a play of light and shadow.  
There are other busts of the pope, although full information is not available for all of them. Of particular interest is the one currently in Ravenna, which may have been intended for the pontificate's tomb in Laterano, and the bust of Clement XII, currently exhibited in the Galleria Nazionale di Arte Antica, which was acquired in 1927.  
The portrait of the pope in the Galleria Borghese was donated to the museum in 1910 by the Istituto dei Ciechi at the Baths of Diocletian.
Pietro Bracci follows the Baroque tradition seen in Bernini's psychological portrait, *Cardinal Scipione Borghese*. Bracci was one of the sculptors involved in the creation of the Trevi Fountain.
place: Istituto dei Ciechi (Institute of the Blind) at the Baths of Diocletian
keywords: Portrait; bust; marble; classical model; Bernini; talking portrait

it.name: *Busto di Clemente XII*
description:
Pietro Bracci ebbe una produzione molto vasta e rivolta soprattutto alla ritrattistica. Fu uno scultore tardo-barocco tra i più importanti del '700 romano (partecipò anche alla realizzazione della Fontana di Trevi); si formò su quella tradizione barocca che faceva capo a Gian Lorenzo Bernini, ma armonizzata ad una ricerca di equilibrio classico.     
Non vi sono notizie documentarie che accertino l'attribuzione di questo busto allo scultore, né riferimenti espliciti riportati nel diario di lavoro che Bracci dal 1725 era solito redigere, ma viene tradizionalmente accettata dagli studiosi. Per quanto riguarda la datazione si fa riferimento al pontificato di Clemente XII Corsini, durato dal 1730 al 1740, anche se non è da escludere che il busto possa essere stato realizzato dopo la morte del pontefice.  
Il volto anziano del papa è scolpito con l'intento di ottenere una resa realistica delle rughe permeata di profonda espressività e spessore psicologico, tratti peculiari della ritrattistica dell'artista. Il paramento del pontefice è decorato finemente e annodato all'altezza del petto, mentre la mantella con il bordo in pelliccia, la mozzetta sottostante, è scolpita ottenendo un elegante volume di pieghe che creano un gioco mosso di luci ed ombre.  
Esistono altri busti del papa e non su tutti si hanno notizie esaustive. Si ricordano la versione oggi a Ravenna, forse destinata in origine alla tomba del pontefice in Laterano e il busto di Clemente XII, oggi esposto alla Galleria Nazionale di Arte Antica, acquistato nel 1927.  
Il ritratto del papa appartenente alla Galleria Borghese fu donato nel 1910 al museo dall'Istituto dei ciechi presso le Terme di Diocleziano.
Pietro Bracci seguì la tradizione del ritratto barocco del *Ritratto del cardinale Scipione Borghese* di Bernini (ritratto psicologico). Bracci fu uno degli scultori della Fontana di Trevi.
place: Istituto dei ciechi presso le Terme di Diocleziano
keywords: Ritratto; busto; marmo; modello classico; Bernini; ritratto parlante

description: هذه البلاطة المستطيلة تصور منظر ذو طراز خاص لمكة مع الكعبة المغطاة بالأسود في وسط المشهد (المسجد الحرام) وهي جزء من مجموعة مواد أكبر مرتبطة بالحج والحج إلى مكة والمواقع في جوارها والتي كانت موضوعا مفضلا في المشاغل العثمانية وبالرغم من أن هذه البلاطة قد رسمت بمزيج ألوان تقليدي المستخدم في القرن السابع عشر في ورشات إزنيق فإن عرض عين الطائر المستوحى من الموروث الأوربي المصور هو مميز لأمثلة لاحقة مصنوعة في سراي (قصر) تكفور في إسطنبول وهو مشغل خزف عثماني أقل شهرة.

en.name: Ka`ba tile
description: This rectangular tile depicts a stylised view of Mecca, with the black-shrouded Ka‘ba in the centre of the *Masjid al-Haram*. It is part of a larger material corpus related to the Hajj, the pilgrimage to Mecca and sites in the vicinity, which was a favoured theme in Ottoman workshops. Although this tile is painted in the traditional colour palette used by seventeenth century Iznik workshops, the bird’s-eye view, inspired by the European pictorial tradition, is a characteristic of later examples made at Tekfur Sarayı in Istanbul, a less well-known Ottoman ceramic workshop.

en.name: Pavilion of the Ambassadors
description:
This pavilion, which is still called a dome, is a small building placed next to the first enclosure of the city. Known today as the “Dome of the Tailors”, a title which evokes one of its more recent uses, it was nevertheless known for long time as the Dome of the Ambassadors. This designation corresponds to the building’s primary function, as Mulay Isma‘il had decided to receive foreign ambassadors there who, among other things, had come to bargain to buy back Christian captives.  
Built on a large rectangular area of 6 m. x 8.2 m., the building joins onto a square whose sides measure 13.8 m. each. The entrance is covered by an overhanging porch which was added on afterwards. The monumental door is decorated with strips of *zellij* which form a geometric composition, and with friezes of sculpted wood. Here and there within the dome stands a small chamber, whose ceiling is surfaced with green tiles, and whose floor is chequered with *zellij* in a variety of colours, including blue, yellow, white and red.  
The interior of the dome, as large as it is harmonious, is made up of 10 arcades which face one another, bearing sculpted plaster motifs which have been partially restored. The pillars which support the arcades are covered in mosaics up to a height of 2 m. The base of the dome’s walls are themselves also decorated with mosaic and are crowned by a band of stucco on which is inscribed: “*Power belongs to Allah*”. This building is essentially esteemed for its conical dome whose interior structure is decorated with geometric and floral motifs.

es.name: Cúpula de los Embajadores
description:
Este pabellón es un pequeño edificio emplazado en la primera muralla de la villa. Aunque hoy día es conocido como Cúpula de los Sastres, nombre que evoca una de sus utilizaciones recientes, durante mucho tiempo fue la Cúpula de los Embajadores; designación que corresponde a sus primeras funciones, ya que Mulay Ismail lo eligió para recibir allí a los embajadores extranjeros que venían a tratar, entre otros asuntos, el rescate de los cautivos cristianos.  
Construido sobre un gran espacio rectangular (6 x 8,20 m), el edificio en sí es un cuadrado de 13,80 m de lado. La entrada cuenta con un porche añadido posteriormente. La monumental puerta está adornada con fajas de *zelish*, que forman composiciones geométricas, y con frisos de madera tallada. A cada lado de la cúpula hay una pequeña habitación con techo recubierto de tejas verdes; el suelo está solado con baldosas de diversos colores: azul, amarillo, blanco, rojo...  
El interior de la cúpula, grande y armoniosa, está constituido por diez arcadas con motivos labrados en yeso, parcialmente restaurados. Los pilares que soportan las arcadas están revestidos de mosaico hasta una altura de 2 m. Los bajos de las paredes también están embellecidos con mosaicos, coronados por una faja en estuco en la que se puede leer la inscripción: “El poder reside en Alá”.  
Lo que distingue especialmente a este edificio es su cúpula cónica, cuyo intradós está decorado con motivos geométricos y florales.

fr.name: Coupole des Ambassadeurs
description:
Ce pavillon, encore appelé coupole, est un petit édifice accolé à la première enceinte de la ville. Appelée aujourd’hui, “Coupole des Couturiers”, nom qui évoque une de ses utilisations récentes, elle fut longtemps connue sous le nom de Coupole des Ambassadeurs. Cette désignation correspond aux fonctions premières de l’édifice car Moulay Ismaïl choisit d’y recevoir les ambassadeurs étrangers venus traiter, entre autres, du rachat des captifs chrétiens.  
Construit sur un large espace rectangulaire, 6 m sur 8,20 m, le bâtiment s’inscrit dans un carré de 13,80 m de côté.L’entrée est surmontée d’un porche en saillie qui fut rajouté postérieurement. La porte monumentale est ornée de bandeaux en *zellige* formant des compositions géométriques, et des frises en bois sculpté. De part et d’autre de la coupole s’élève une petite chambre dont le plafond est revêtu de tuiles vertes; son sol est carrelé de *zellige* aux couleurs variées: bleu, jaune, blanc, rouge...  
L’intérieur de la coupole, aussi large qu’harmonieuse, est constitué de dix arcades qui se font vis-à-vis portant des motifs en plâtre sculpté, partiellement restaurés. Les piliers qui supportent les arcades sont couverts de mosaïque jusqu’à une hauteur de 2 m. Les soubassements des murs de la coupole sont eux aussi ornés de mosaïque et couronnés par un bandeau en stuc où l’on peut lire l’inscription: "*La puissance est à Allah*2.  
Cet édifice est essentiellement marqué par sa coupole conique dont l’intrados est décoré de motifs géométriques et floraux.

ar.name: إبريق بعروة.
description: قطعة من إبريق ذو عروة، حافته منفرجة ومنحنية، فتحته مستديرة، وعنقه على شكل مخروط مقلوب مبتور، ذي بروز مركزي تنبثق عنه، باتجاه الجسم، عروة عمودية مقطعها بيضوي. الإناء كروي وتخرج من كتفه قبضة أنبوبية حيوانية الشكل. توحي القطعة بأكملها بحيوان عنقه ضيق وطويل مثل جمل أو وحيد السنام، والذي قد تشكل حدبته عنق الإناء. زُين هذا الأخير بخطوط دقيقة نباتية الشكل، مدهونة بالأبيض على خلفية تميل إلى الحمرة.
فتحة وعنق إبريق يوحي شكله بحيوان ذي عنق ضيق وطويل مثل جمل أو وحيد السنام، قد تشكل حدبته عنق الإناء. زينت القطعة بخطوط رقيقة ذات طابع نباتي مدهونة بالأبيض فوق خلفية حمراء.

en.name: Water jug.
description: Fragment of a water jug with a curved everted rim, circular mouth and neck shaped as an inverted truncated cone with a central moulding, which is joined to the body by a vertical handle with an oval cross-section. The body is globular with a zoomorphic tubular spout rising from its shoulder. The overall design suggests the shape of an animal with a long narrow neck such as a camel or dromedary, whose hunched back forms the neck of the vessel. It is decorated with fine lines of white painted plant forms on a reddish background.

dates: Hegira end 5th – beginning 6th century / AD end 11th – beginning 12th century.
keywords: ceramic; water jug; zoomorphic

en.name: Parish Church of St. George and St. Euphemia
description:
The Parish Church of St. George and St. Euphemia is lit only through the windows of the chapels, this was in order that the height of both nave and aisles were equalised. In addition to the impact of local architectural tradition, the contemporaneous rebuilding of Udine Cathedral (1706–1735) designed by the Venetian architect Domenico Rossi, influenced this architectural solution. Similar approaches were applied by Giorgio Massari in the rebuilding of Koper Cathedral (1738) and Cividale (1766), indicating that they influenced each other.  
In the church, there are a number of high quality marble altars, five or six of which are decorated with the statues of the Venetian sculptor Alvise Tagliapietra and his workshop, and which judging from 19th century sources was his last commission. The Rovinj altars came at the end of prolific activity by this workshop, which some 20 years earlier had produced exceptionally high quality sculptures for another client from the Croatian side of the Adriatic at the Church of St. Chrysogonus, Zadar. Along with the statues of the two sanctuary altars in Rovinj – the High Altar and the Altar of St. Euphemia – the work of the Tagliapietra workshop includes the statues of *Our Lady of the Rosary* and *St. Nicholas* (jointly signed by Alvise and his son Giuseppe) and the reliefs of *St. Michael* *the Archangel* and *St. Peter* on side altars. As well as the traditional attribution to the Tagliapietra workshop, the sculptures of the left-hand altar in the sanctuary dedicated to the Holy Sacrament are thought to be the work of the Classicist-oriented Venetian sculptor, Giovanni Marchiori, who earlier, in 1737, had made the sculpture for the high altar of the nearby Church of St. Servulus, Buje. While the altars indicate the refined taste of the Rovinj commune as client, the overall impression of unity in the opulent Baroque furnishing is enhanced by the works of others: the stuccowork of G. Lattuga (1750), the stalls for the choir and congregation by G. Besenghi (known as “Napolachi”, also 1750), the organ by A. Barbini (1754) and the silver Baroque antependium by  A. Scarabella d'Este (1776).

The church is located at the highest point of the one-time islet on which the settlement of Rovinj developed, creating together with the packed core of the old town, an extremely harmonious and picturesque unit. The campanile by A. Manopola was built between 1654 and 1680, and the church, nave and two aisles by Giovanni Dozzi Alvise between 1724 and 1736. The unique architecture and valuable furnishings place this church among the finest religious structures in this area of the Croatian Adriatic.
type: Religious, parish church and interior furnishing
artist: Bell tower: A. Manopola [n.d.]; church: Giovanni Dozzi [n.d.]; sculptures on several altars: Alvise Tagliapietra (1670–1747) and his sons Ambrogio (b. 1701) and Giuseppe (b. 1711); stuccowork: G. Lattuga [n.d.]; (choir and congregation stalls) G. Besenghi "Napolachi"; organ: A. Barbini; silver antependium: Antonio Scarabella d'Este
history: In 1724, the citizens of Rovinj confided the realisation of the plan for the Parish church to Venetian architect, Giovanni Scalfaratto, who at that time was building the church of S. Simeone Piccolo in Venice. They stipulated that the new church should resemble that it was replacing and consist of a nave and two aisles. Since Scalfaratto did not meet their demands and because his plan included demolition of earlier and surrounding structures, they chose the Venetian architect, Giovanni Dozzi instead who completed the work in 1736, although the clients requested certain changes to the plan.

tags: Rovinj, Istria, Giovanni Dozzi, Alvise Tagliapietra, Ambrogio Tagliapietra, Giuseppe Tagliapietra, Angiolo Scarabella d'Este, architecture, sculpture, goldsmiths

en.name: Calligraphy
description:
This artwork blends modern calligraphy with classical Islamic *sülüs*– and *tuğra*–inspired forms. The central inscription features the Qur’anic verse from Surah Al-Anbiyā’ (21:30): “And We created every living thing from water.” The phrase emphasises the essential and sacred nature of water as the origin of life, reflecting a cosmological theme deeply rooted in Islamic thought.  
  
On the right side, the intricate calligraphic motif expresses a devotional invocation, rendered in fluid, interwoven lines that echo the movement and vitality of water. The turquoise background reinforces the symbolism of purity, creation, and continuity. Together, these elements merge spiritual meaning with visual harmony, inviting viewers to contemplate the relationship between nature, divine creation, and artistic expression.
holder: İstanbul Su Müzesi / Istanbul Water Museum
keywords: Calligraphy; Qur'an; Verse; Water

ar.name: شاب مع أسد.صفحة من ألبوم
description: يجري المشهد المبين في حديقة شاه فارسي أو شخص نبيل. حيث فقط الطبقة العليا من المجتمع الإيراني يمكنها أن تقتني حيوانات مفترسة من فصيلة القطط في حدائقها ويقابل ما يضعه الشاب على رأسه أزياء منتصف القرن السابع عشر الميلادي الصفوية.وإن الفنان صاحب اللوحة هو أفضال الحسيني (أيضا يسمى مير أفضال توني )وهو أصغر عمرا وتلميذ معاصر لرضا عباسي. ويعرف بشكل أساسي بأنه معلم رسم العراة ويفضل الرسام  أفضال أن يجسد متعة الأرستقراطيين الفرس: الشباب أو مشاهد الحب في الحديقة. وبالإضافة للشكل الفني فإن الفنان أيضا يشير إلى ذلك بنقش في الجزء السفلي الأيمن من الصفحة التي تقول: ""إنه في اليوم الأول من شهر جمادى الثاني من عام 1056 فقد اكتمل الرسم من قبل أفضال الحسيني الأكثر تواضعا "". ومنذ أواخر القرن السادس عشر فإن المنمنمات الإيرانية حازت على دور كجزء مستقل من الفن. وكان في تلك الفترة ينمو الكيان المحترم لعمل الفنان وحريته الإبداعية والاقتصادية وأصبح من الأسهل جدا تأمين المعيشة بإنتاج صفحة واحدة من العمل بدلا من العمل على كتاب كامل. وقد شكلت الرسومات المنفصلة وأيضا صفحات التخطيط ذات الأشعار ألبومات (مرقى) والتي تعكس الطلب الجمالي والفكري لجامعي مثل هذه الأشياء من الأثرياء.

en.name: *A Youth with a Lion* Folio from an album
description:
The depicted scene takes place in a garden of a Persian Shah or a lord. Only the upper elite of Iranian society could afford keeping large predatory felines in their gardens. The young man's headdress fits the AD mid-17th century Safavid fashion.  
The author of the painting is Afzal al-Husayni (also named Mir Afzal Tuni, Afzal), a younger contemporary and follower of Reza Abbasi. Known primarily as the master of erotic drawing, Afzal preferred to depict the leisure of the Persian aristocracy: young men or love scenes in the garden. In addition to the artistic manner, the author is also indicated by an inscription in the bottom right of the folio that reads: “He! On the first day of the month of Jumat the Second of year 1056, the drawing of the most humble Afzal al-Husayni was completed”.  
Since the late 16th century the Iranian miniature has acquired the role of an independent piece of art. The prestige of the artist's work and his creative and economic freedom was growing, and it became much easier to make a living on producing single page works than on illustrating a whole book. Separate paintings as well as calligraphic folios with poems constituted *murakka* albums, reflecting the aesthetic and intellectual demand of wealthy collectors.
keywords: Miniature; Iran; Safavid; Calligraphy; Afzal al-Husayni
materials: Opaque watercolour, gold and ink on paper
tags: Opaque watercolour, gold and ink on paper
partner: The Bohdan and Varvara Khanenko National Museum of Arts

en.name: Bottle with wide rim
description: This black glass bottle has a spherical body supported by a ring-shaped base. The tubular neck narrows slightly towards the top and ends with a flat rim. At its base it is circled by a twisting black glass ribbon overlay, the sole design element. Blown glass existed from the first century AD, making possible a considerable increase in the production of glass objects. The process became popular and played a significant part in the fabrication of vessels.
